review_text:
I wanted this place to be good. I really did. 

After reading several good reviews from various places, I anticipated good food, good service, and good ambiance. 

Well, the ambiance was nice. White marble shelves at the bar, clean, modern wood throughout, and a sliding glass entrance, (which if you're not careful, will cause you to trip into the place). The tables were too close for comfort. If you're sitting on the wall seats you have to lift your legs to get into the table. 

And the food? Not exactly memorable except for the fact that the entrees were too salty and way too unbalanced in size. The bread and olives were good. But after two baskets of waiting, we expected the main course to be worth the wait, and sadly it wasn't. 

I ordered the lasagna, which was a decent portion. And beforehand the server suggested that I order a side in case. 

My poor dinner companion got no such warning. He ordered the chop, and it arrived alone on a giant white plate. With nary a single piece of garnish against this small brown mass of meat. Pitiful was the word that came to mind that night. 

Dessert was okay, again, nothing memorable. 

Who knows, maybe I was there on an off night. Or maybe the establishment was pissed at us for not ordering wine with our meal, (the nerve!) Either way, it's one of those places where I'm not likely to return unless I'm all out of ideas on where to go for a good Italian meal.  To me, this place was just eh.

I do love my cookie-cutter porn shops and tattoo parlorettes but I Sodi is a welcome new addition to Christopher.

Maybe it was our seat at the bar... Maybe it was our loose flirtation with the friendly waitstaff... Maybe it was Lisa F's wake-up call to the kitchen...  I don't have the answer but know that my dining experience at I Sodi was an unexpected treat.

We started with the aforementioned bread and olives.  I'm going with Bella di Cerignola here but I'm not Italian so do with that what you will...

For the main event, my buddy opted for Tagliatelle Alla Matriciana while I selected a Seafood Risotto with an Insalata di Carciofi E Parmigiano to start.  It's perverse but the earthiness of the paper-thin artichoke slices with the bite of Parmigiano-Reggiano was spiritual for me.  A family trip through the Tuscan countryside flashed by like a ViewMaster with a light trigger.  I didn't pull a Diane Lane, but did escape into that fond recollection more than once during my work day...

Both entrees made the repeat order list.  I would jump the fence for the homemade tagliatelle next time as the turbot and shrimp in my risotto were subtle for a rainy Monday.  However, both commanded the price of admission.  And, with the weak dollar, this may be as close as I'm getting to Italy anytime soon...

We sent it all off with a quartino of Chianti (o due) but opted for a gelato nightcap down on Bleecker.  

The ambiance, upbeat staff and the simple, delicious fare landed I Sodi the mantle of 'Best New Neighbor on Christopher Street'.  However, I prefer you listen to Lisa F. so I can still get a table...

I really loved this excellent low-key neighborhood spot.  The space has a rustic feel, the menu is small and the service is spot on.  But the best part was the food.  It's exactly as Tuscan food should be - simple, with a focus on fresh ingredients.  We had:

- heirloom tomato and cucumber salad 
- antipasti for 2 - great variety of meats, cheeses, and preserves to go with it
-meat lasagna 
-spaghetti w/clams
-veal special - roasted, thinly butterflied, with a tasty tuna sauce.  surprisingly light.
dessert - profiteroles - 3, each with a different filling (vanilla gelato, straciatella gelato, and cream)

Portions were the perfect size and almost every dish was perfect.  The only disappointment was the dessert.

I will definitely be back!

Really now. Christopher street has taken a step up in my mind with the arrival of I Sodi AND Rag & Bone. Fashion, style, good taste....it has it all. 

Or, at least two places with all that.

We have been here about 10x since my first review and the food is more outstanding every time. The staff is not only friendly, but knowledgeable. Mark the bartender is so sweet and lovely to speak with, we tend to dine at the bar when it's just the two of us. The manager, whose name I can't pronounce or spell is also fantastic!

Tonight we shared the:

Antipasto for two, the seafood risotto (1/2 portion-which was HUGE!!) and the Branzino cooked with tomatoes and potatoes. 

All were absolutely top notch. If you like the movie Auntie Mame then I can tell you it was, "Top drawer.  Simply top drawer!"  If you don't get my reference then you really need to rent that freakin' movie. Seriously. Do it now. Get to Kim's.

We had a really great wine from Piedmont. Can't remember exactly what it was, but it was an extremely delicious medium bodied red with violet and blueberry notes. We didn't want the whole bottle, so the manager (who's name I can't pronounce or spell) let us buy a carafe of it.

This is a perfect place for a low-key night to make your belly happy. 

Divertiti!!!

My GF has the patience of a saint--especially after she gets a bit of her shop on. After having a fabulous brunch at Pastis with numerous cocktails, we went walking around the neighborhood with our friends Brooke and Liz. We decided we needed another drink after helping stimulate the neighborhood economy. Rag and Bone--I will say no more.

We went into I Sodi with the intent of having a glass of wine a piece; well since we really did not know that much about Italian wines, we stayed for a little education--like two bottles worth of education. We had a great visit and even though my GF was not drinking, she too had a great time. the bartender gave a tasting of a few wines and we picked out a couple. The prices were great: under $45 a bottle. Good times for a great price.

Rita Sodi is a tall, athletic Florentine whose frame fills doorways and whose smile softens the platinum curls that somehow lend her austerity rather than cool lassitude.  The doorway to her restaurant, I Sodi, open onto the most infelicitous intersection of the West Village: Bleecker and Christopher.  The tacky tattoo parlors and head shops elaborate a paucity of taste whose counterpoint is defined by the exquisite space built by the former director of Calvin Klein in Europe.

I Sodi, after suffering through the growing pains of any restaurant, has begun to receive a great deal of press and praise in the last few weeks.  Deservedly slow.  The Tuscan comfort food that is a culinary autobiography of the owner's life and a tribute to her mother's prowess in the kitchen, does not stray far from dishes that one could make at home (if they knew what they were doing and spared no expense).

Diners crowd through etched glass framed in reclaimed wood from a South Carolina barn and step into a tiny anteroom before they reach an L-shaped line of small tables that bend around a luxurious, though decidedly understated, bar that adjoins and struts out from the kitchen.  The backbar is lined with glassware, which seems to have been chosen from a Museum gift shop (the water and highball glasses rest so beautifully beside each other that an failure to order a cocktail suggests a lack of aesthetics).  The most obscure and best Italian amari are lined up in careful rows and mixed carefully in various concoctions, the most famous of which are included on a five-deep Negroni menu--the Punt-a-Groni, flavored by Punt e Mes, offers a deep coffee color and the bitter wormwood flavor that deepens gin's herbal notes.  

Impeccable service coupled with homey food underscores the well-negotiated contradictions of I Sodi: the decidedly elegant, chic, space feels is warmed by wide comfortable tables; knowledgeable waiters explain minutiae with pride rather than polish; epicurean tastes demure rather than confront the neighborhood's immature hedonism.  Our server was a two-headed hydra, one a shaggy southerner the other a goateed Northeasterner, who took turns describing dishes, clearing plates, pouring wine and exploring the differences between various Maraschino liqueurs.

Our meal was shared over a 1997 Tommasi Amarone.  The kitchen produces a delicious antipasto platter--served on the best Genovese flatware--which I managed to eschew this time without dissatisfaction, so the carciofe crudi and watercress & pecorino clearly warranted praise.  Rita Sodi despises vinegar and almost any acids, so her artichokes are threatened with discoloration, but their nuttiness is released by the loss of lemon.  The watercress, which is so often a tangle of leaf and stem, was carefully manicured and the two salads whetted our appetites while sharpening our palate.

A simple carbonara was enriched with guancale rather than pancetta, or even bacon.  The sauce was a bit too cheesy rather than eggy, so taken as a carbonara it was a bit off.  Discussed as a pasta, it was delicious and split between two it was perfectly set against the light Branzino Livornese that we ordered.  This was not the best branzino I have eaten--that recipe, that dish is most wonderfully executed by Jody Williams, but served boneless with the two fillets bracketing fried potatoes I felt curls of flavor address me from a grandmother's skillet.  The sautéed spinach and carciofe fritte filled out the meal.  Similar to carciofe guidea, I Sodi's carciofe fritte are fried in olive oil but cut into popcorn size bits, these lightly dredged treasure decorated pleasure like pearls on a patrician maiden.

We lingered for some time over hazelnut semifredo and fig tart, but the sweets were no comparison for the savory as they seemed to suffer from the carefully plotted production that cannot be found in your mother's cupboard.  The lines of the bar and the arcs of the chairs began to seem abundantly familiar and knowing we had miles to go before we were home, we left.  Content, well-fed and feeling as though we had left the convivial home of very fashionable friends.

Love this place! It's cozy and has a lovely atmosphere, sort of a cross between rustic and modern/urban. The bar is nice and long, so lots of places to sit and have a drink or dinner, or wait for the rest of your party. The somelier was very friendly and helpful in choosing glasses of wine. He offered tastes of anything we were curious about as well as a few he wanted to introduce us to. 

For dinner, most of us started with a salad. A few of us had the arugula, one had the artichoke, and one chose a salad of red cabbage. For entrees, oddly, all of us went with lasagne, everyone had the meat sauce version except me, I went with the artichoke version. I'm a huge fan of lasagne, and I Sodi does it well. Everyone practically licked their plates.

For dessert, we shared a fig tart and a flourless chocolate cake. Both were yummy, and we all rolled out of there stuffed and happy. The service was great, the food was delicious, and the atmosphere was lively. Perhaps a bit loud to be a good date restaurant, but certainly a good one for small groups or dinner with a friend.

Great service, delicious food, nice wine menu and amazing olive oil. Place is small, but cozy, and well lit. 

Had the sliced polenta with meat (special of the night was with duck); also had a taste of the lasagna with chopped artichoke hearts -- excellent flavors on both, but the polenta was slightly (just barely) too dry. Entrees range from $16-$28. 

Recommend the antipasto appetizer (small is a sufficient portion for three to taste, but not gorge, on -- cured meats such as salami and prosciutto, as well as cheeses). This place is an excellent find!

I went to I Sodi with a friend who'd read a review of it in the New Yorker.  Having wandered Christopher Street myself, I was surprised that a restaurant of its supposed calibre would open adjacent to smoke shops and sex stores.  I was curious.

And it was lovely, but nothing to write home about.  The food is all based on recipes from the owner's family cookbook.  Apparently her Italian mother sometimes is also at work in the kitchen.  I had a nice lasagna, which was tasty and filling; something more creative could have been done with the side dish.  My friend's caprese looked and tasted nice, but for my money I'd have gone to Il Gattopardo-- where caprese is served with the freshest mozzarella and basil and heirloom yellow tomatoes that literally made my mouth water for more.

A nice, cozy place; great wine list and friendly staff.  But probably not New York's best offering for Italian cuisine.

More like I SO SO.  This place is overrated.  I had the special scampi risotto which was incredibly disappointing and had no flavor, I had to ask for salt and olive oil to spruce it up   trader joes 3 dollar instant is better.  I give it an extra star since for good service and nice decor.

I had pretty high expectations for this place and was very disappointed.  In terms of the atmosphere, I thought the place was nice- it is a very small restaurant which usually is a good thing, I think.  However, it did feel a little cold even though it should have felt intimate. I think it has something to do with the decor which seemed a little sparse to me.  

In terms of the food, I ordered the cacio e pepe risotto- though it was good, i literally have made the same thing at home.  Anything with that much cheese tastes good.  2 of my friends, however, ordered the special of the day which was a shrimp risotto.  It was extremely disappointing and frankly had no flavor.  I was with a group of savvy diners and dont love to ask for salt at nice restaurants because the food should come out flavored the way the chef intended it too.  However, they had to ask for salt and at that time, the server asked if anything was wrong with the dish.  My friends were honest, and so the server asked if she could bring something else out. She brought out another dish for the both of them.  I have to say that was the one saving grace of the place- the service- our server really compensated for the bad meal and on a side note, the bartender was super nice as well.  However, even though the service was great, I can't speak too highly of a restaurant that charges $20+ for a plate of pasta that literally has no flavor. I thought it was embarassing they would serve a special like that.  

I really wanted to like the place but it will never be a neighborhood italian joint for me unfortunately.

Very friendly staff, welcoming.  Nice room, small, not cramped on a weekday eve, but a few more people at the bar would have made it feel a little tight.

The food was good, mostly, but also generally lacking.  Heirloom tomato/buffalo mozzerella is ubiquitous, but why do restaurants insist on putting it on the menu if their tomatoes aren't top notch?  I Sodi's weren't.  I will gladly pay $15 for delicious tomatoes, but these were not delicious.  The saffron risotto lacked complexity.  The special leek lasagne was good, but was too heavy on the pasta in the pasta-to-filling ratio for my taste.  The polpettone was good, and a lot of food.  We had a nice, reasonable priced bottle of wine--they have a good selection by the glass, 1/4, 1/2 liter and bottle.  All in all, a good neighborhood place, but not really special.
This place hits the sweet spot for me.  Wonderful cocktails, beautiful modern decor and lovely service.  The food is not the finest in town but it's tasty.  Well worth a visit.
great food best mozz and tomato I ever had and i have had alot i like it because its small and romantic I would deff go back and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great date spot

This is not an ordinary Italian restaurant.  It is sophisticated and individual but thoroughly authentic.  I could imagine it in Italy with no trouble.

The service is attentive and pleasant without being intrusive.  The noise level never overwhelms conversation yet the adjoining tables don't intrude (unless your table has nothing to say).

The menu is varied and mostly depends on fairly simply, traditionally cooked foods.  The huge Forentina beefsteak is Michelangelesque.  It is large for two but makes a superb lunch the next day!

Wines are intelligently and knowledgeably chosen.  There are a couple of Sicilian whites that are very good as aperififs.

reservations recommended.

The owner's attitude is basically "who gives a s**t about the customers." We arrived at 8:12 for an 8:00 reservation to find that our table had been given away to a walk-in. The explanation was "we tried to confirm with you at 4:30 and didn't reach you, and in that situation we will only hold your table for 15 minutes." When we pointed out that we had arrived only twelve minutes late, there was a shrug and "Talk to the owner." She was unbelievably rude and shouted at us, claiming we arrived at 8:17, which was absolutely untrue, at least by AT&T cellular time. Who knows what time their clock is on. They never informed us of their confirmation policy, nor did they leave any message. Reserve at your own risk, but this place has attitude up the wazoo.

I Sodi is without doubt the best Italian restaurant around. Not Italian-American, Italian. It's the real thing. From wine to dessert, nothing fails to deliver. The restaurant is inviting for a drink and a bite at the bar, dinner for two, or even for a group. You just can't miss. If you can't decide what to eat, just ask Rita. She will guide you to the perfect meal every time. She ought to know. She's cooking it.

From day one -- and I've eaten there since the week it opened -- every meal has always been perfect. The wine selection is varied and the bartenders are always willing to share their knowledge and tastings. The food, well, it's hard to describe perfection. You simply must taste it. But beware, everything is enticing, and you are apt to eat more than you planned ... but it's well worth it.

I Sodi's size makes it the perfect little hideaway. If you don't have a reservation, then eat at the bar. You will invariably meet new people and have an interesting evening filled with fine wine, fine food and a good time. 

Go. Now. What are you waiting for?

Special but nothing special?  Lovely waitstaff. Big mounds of basically bland but reliable pasta.  Extremely reasonable $ - half portions are a full meal.  Nice to know there will always be table when I just want to roll down the street and gorge on some cacio y pepe.

My boss took us here for the annual holiday dinner. The setting is intimate and very stylish, with glass sliding doors and blond wood accents.  There are only about 5 or 6 tables so do make a reservation. The food was decent, but nothing mindblowingly good. I'm picky when it comes to Italian, so that could be apart of the reason why I'm not giving it a higher rating. 

I had the arugula salad to start off with. It was light and refreshing but nothing to write home about, it's just arugula and cheese. For the main course I had the meat lasagna. This dish was a bit burnt, which was disappointing. I love the cheese on top to be caramelized, but on my dish it came out charred. The edges of the pasta were really dried out and it hurt to swallow. The meat and sauce were very flavorful, but the dish was not executed well (god I sound like that bitchy Padma from Top Chef). For dessert, I went with the chocolate cake. It was dense and tasted like chocolate cake. At this point, I was honestly too tipsy from the wine to remember much, other than the fact that it tasted pretty good.

The boss paid, so I don't know what everyone's tab came to. However, from I remember the prices were kinda high, but not completely unreasonable. I don't think I'll come back if I had to pay, but I'll take a free meal here any day.

Went here last night for dinner with the bf.  i had low expectations coming in thanks to a lot of not-so-wonderful reviews from fellow yelpers.  That said - the food was really good.  It's homecooked, solid italian food.  My bf got the antipasto (a selection of meats and cheeses), and he thought it went well with the free bread / olive oil.  That said, the olive oil really stole the show from any of the apps.  For entrees, i got the artichoke lasagna (amazing - and i don't like lasagna 9.9 times out of 10) while he got a special of noodles, butter, and nutmeg.  His was really good too, very solid, but i think we both agreed mine was better.  The pastas here are really outstanding.  Dessert, on the other hand, sucked.  Maybe we got a bad dish (ordered the chocolate cake), but i didn't even bother after the first bite.  Be forewarned - don't come to eat here if you're going out right afterwards.  Between the gut-busting food and awesome wine, you're going to want to go straight to sleep afterwards.  

Definitely going again!

Came here one night at the recommendation of a friend. He had said it was a quaint little Italian restaurant on the quiet Christopher street and that I would like it. The entrance is interesting and different as you are greeted by a sliding door that almost seemed Japanese in style after making your way through the first entrance. The space is on the smaller side and about half of it is taken up by a bar, maybe about 10 or so tables in total. I was offered a choice of tables, but decided to wait at the bar until my friend had arrived. And while doing so I enjoyed a glass of red wine, which I believe was La Grola. I also overheard, and took note, of two patrons praising a cheese plate they had been enjoying and asking the bartender about where the honey was from (chestnut honey if I recall).

After having been seated at our table, we decided that we wanted to try the dish that had been admired at the bar from others, however I couldn't find it on the menu. Our waitress pointed out that it was the Antipasto Toscano, however they had ordered it sans meat; we decided to order it as is on the menu, with meat. There were four different kinds, which included prosciutto, salami and two others whose Italian names I didn't recognize (nor can recall). The meats, cheeses, honey and apricot were all quite delicious and a nice way to start out. Oh, they also gave us some amazing olive oil and bread.

We were a little slow to consume our appetizer and they were a little fast to bring out our entrées, but no matter, we made do with the table real estate we had. I decided to go with the rigatoni and meat sauce, while my friend opted for the risotto. I believe the menu does change however I'm not sure how often. My rigatoni was very good (and very filling) and the risotto was delicious, which provided an amazingly light and sweet aftertaste.

Too full to even finish off our entrées, we passed on the desert menu, although it did look quite enticing. Overall, I really enjoyed my experience at I Sodi. The service was wonderful and our waiters and host were very gracious. It's a great little spot to tuck into and was even more appropriate on this cold and wintry evening.

This restaurant is kind of in the middle of no where, but the inside is very cute!  I was there on a weekday night and it was fairly empty.  The other member of my party was 20 minutes late, but they still let me sit at a table and patiently waited as perused the wine menu and read a magazine I brought along -- shocking in a typical new york city restaurant!  

When my friend arrived, we ordered the lasagne (free with a coupon I got from blackboard.com) and the lamb chops.  Both were not bad, but not amazing.  The lasagne was underwhelming, but to be expected considering it was, well, free.  The lamb chops came with 4 pieces, but they tasted very fatty.

All in all, the menu was very limited and too pricy for the quality.

Ah-maaay-zing food! Came here without reading a single review, wanted to try out my "deal" from BlackboardEats of free lasagna with a purchase of an entree. Didn't realize how tiny it is, only about 8 tables, otherwise I would've made reservations. Although having dinner at the bar was actually not bad for 2 - probably why the bar countertop is pretty big. The bartender was awesome, made wine recommendations based on what I like, and was just in general a great guy. Some eavesdropping, and we learned that the owner was sitting one over from us so we watched carefully for what she ordered. 

For appetizer we had mushrooms with sliced parmesan. Alright. Entrees were the steak with melted cheese on top and fries (what the owner had) and the artichoke lasagna (the free dish). Both of them were so good, I crave it now! Don't think I've ever had my steak with melted cheese and it's a shame that's not a standad everywhere! The fries were of cute cube shapes and perfectly fried. The lasagna melted in my mouth, it was so soft and well balanced with the cheese and artichoke. For dessert we split the vanilla panna cotta which beat the one I had in Italy, actually! Thank goodness for budget control otherwise I would've just kept devouring more and more of it.

Great spot to sit at the bar, enjoy a glass of wine and simple, delicious italian food.  The half-portions are enough to fill you, but still let you leave without that heavy pasta feeling.  

Waitstaff are fantastically knowledgeable and generous with tasting and explaining the interesting bottle selection behind the bar.  Always a plus.

Went back recently and had much better service, so maybe it is a one-off, the duck pappardelle and the pollo fritto redeemed this place to a point beyond belief.  Even though I still couldn't score a table, the server was much nicer this time and even gave us some really good food and wine recommendation.  I was impressed this time around, way to redeem yourself, i sodi.  Oh, and don't forget the fior de latte gelato, that was awesome.

My experience at iSodi was quite the adventure!  Though I had never heard of the adorable spot, I was tempted to try it after receiving a coupon from Blackboard Eats.  I met my brother outside of the restaurant, where we previewed the menu and deemed it worthy of a visit.  We entered the small space and were approached by a waiter who politely asked us if we had made a reservation.  We regretfully shook our heads and received a mumbled response.  As he walked away, I asked my brother to clarify what he had said, which apparently was, "We have a couple that is about to leave.  However, we are waiting to see if Matthew Broderick will be coming back to take the table.  If you could wait 15 minutes, we should know either way."  We waited in foyer with shocked faces, gossiping like giddy schoolgirls and keeping our eyes peeled for the A-List celebrity.  After fifteen or twenty minutes and no sign of Matthew, we re-approached the waiter to claim our table.  Just as he was about to seat us, Mr. Broderick came waltzing in with an older woman.  The waiter apologized profusely for having to repossess our table, claiming how he "hates this kind of BS", but knowing that it was also part of his job to take advantage of any potential press promotion.  He did, however, offer to grant us a complimentary gift of wine or champagne if we opted to dine at the bar instead.  We agreed and were sure glad that we did.

The bartender was extremely interesting, bonding with us over an educated discussion about food and wine.  While they had a large red wine list and several house cocktails, he worked with our tastes and helped me pick a sweet and refreshing white wine, while my brother opted for an elegant cava.  As we chatted away, the waiter stopped by with some bread and gossip.  It turned out that Matthew was extremely polite and was dining with his older sister.  We delighted in the interesting news and munched away on fresh, airy Italian bread, plus wheat slices packed with crisp walnuts.  Dipping each tender morsel into herb-infused olive oil only added to the spectacular flavors.

Our Blackboard Eats coupon granted us a complimentary lasagna with the purchase of a second entree.  I decided to order the Cornish Hen, which was butterflied, seasoned with rosemary, and roasted under a brick.  The huge portion of poultry was fantastically moist and tender.   The house-made lasagna was available either with meat sauce, with artichokes, or with leeks as the special of the day.  The meat version came highly recommended by the bartender and did not disappoint.  Paper-thin sheets of pasta were delicately layered with sweet, chunky meat sauce and gooey cheese.  The lean meat was seasoned with cinnamon for an added kick.  

Our entire experience - from a top-notch celebrity sighting to the perfectly-executed Italian fare - was heavenly.  iSodi's cozy dining room was a fabulous find.  Thanks Blackboard Eats!

I had the privilege of being invited to an amazing restaurant in the West Village called, "I Sodi." The New York Times described it as "rustic Italian" and yes, you feel as if you are eating someplace in Italy after sampling this cuisine. 

My friends and I ordered a menagerie of the most delicious things -- prosciutto and cheese, pasta bolognese, pan simmered fish (or was it boiled), french fries with cloves of garlic and an arugula salad.

If you are in New York City, looking for something NON-TOURISTY and very cool, hip and delicious, EAT here. In addition, the service was impeccable and the wine selection extensive.

LOVED IT! 

Directions: I think you'd take the 1-9 Train to Christopher Street, walk toward Greenwich ... (I'll post photos later!)

Pleasantly surprised with this place. Quaint with a simple but good menu. Good service as well. Do not try the green salad with cheese (forget which cheese) but it was really salty.

Housemade spaghetti with marinara was really good as was the risotto.

The first time I went to I Sodi I thought I was lost. It is nestled in between a bunch of gay porn and bong shops on Christopher Street and you can barely tell that is it there. But once inside, you are transported into and orgasmic Italian food adventure that you will not soon forget. 

Great pasta. Amazing branzino. Killer deserts. Everything is good including the helpful staff. Last time I was there, I asked that my second vodka soda be served in a tall glass because my first drink was very stiff. The waitress brought me a huge glass that was 3x the normal volume and smiled as if to say, here is a massive cocktail for the price of a normal cocktail....enjoy. You don't get that in New York very often!! 

Have been to I Sodi 5 times in two months and will keep going back because I hate being disappointed and they NEVER disappoint!!
Two words: Artichoke lasagna. It is ridiculously delicious. The meat lasagna is really good, too. Seriously try this lasagna if you get the chance, you won't regret it.

Despite its unfortunate location on one of the seediest stretches of the west village, this little restaurant is thriving.  The place churns out fantastic food, has a well priced wine list and is always packed to the gills so be prepared to dine at the bar or to wait for a table if you dont have a reservation.  (I actually prefer eating at the bar because the little tables are really tight and if you sit with your back to the bar you constantly get pounded by passing patrons and servers).

Most recently went her with a friend and we started with two half orders of pasta--tagliatelle with ragu and the cacio e pepe, both were delicious but the ragu was really robust and flavorful and shined the most.  We moved on with a half order of the ravioili in sage and butter reduction and the lamb chops.  Lamb chops were great, perfectly cooked to medium rare but the ravioli was disappointing as the reduction didnt really seem reduced enough so the flavors werent concentrated.  Had a fantastic 2007 barbaresco ($75) that made ever dish better.  

One important note--the half orders of pasta are the size of full orders at Lupa so no need to order the full size!!

I took a friend to I Sodi tonight.  It was the worst experience I have had in a long time. The staff treated us like we second class citizens, the service was rude and I ordered a birthday dessert fir my friend.  they had the nerve to ask us to move to the bar for our dessert because they needed our table.  I told them that I pulled out my back and couldn't sit at the bar, but if they really needed us to move, then they could cancel our dessert.  So they cancelled our dessert and brought the check.  I eat at several popular as well as neighborhood erstaurants in Manhattan and all over the world.  I have never had such rude service.  And to top it off, the food was not worth the harrasment!!

We decided on i Sodi after the rave reviews on Yahoo's "The 10 Best Places for Pasta in the US." i Sodi was the only NY restaurant listed. I'm not sure why as it was pretty underwhelming. the artichoke lasagna that received so many accolades was bland and uninspiring. the rabbit just tasted fried and oily. the mushroom risotto needed some flavor. the pasta with meat sauce was OK but nothing special. the best dishes were our apps--chicken liver on toast and antipasto plate. at least our service was good.

Great Restaurant.......having said this I thought the cab driver dropped us off on the wrong street. Rough looking area not well lit at night. A little hard to find your first time.
Once inside the staff were very friendly and helpful with good knowledge of their wines. Food was very good and well priced for the quality. We had a late dinner so we were one of the last people to leave...thought we may have a problem getting a cab, but there are quite a few circling down the street.
Overall a very nice experience!

They indicated the wait would be over an hour but it was more like 20-25 minutes?   The food was okay, nothing spectacular.  I wanted to be wow'ed but I just wasn't?  Probably the only stand-out for me was the gelato which I believe is outsourced from Philly... also the lasagna was definitely unique (in a good way). was more like eating a crepe.. lot of thin layers....

The greatest olive oil I've ever had.  Good anti-pasta.

Other than that, entrées weren't very good, dessert so so.  Wine was overpriced by all normal standards.  

It was ok, but I was underwhelmed.

Three friends and I just had a new years eve dinner at I Sodi and recommend it for anyone looking for authentic Italian dining. I suggest arriving early and enjoying one - or more - of the specialty drinks at the bar.  We enjoyed the porter-house special for 2, the Branzino Alla Livornese roasted whole branzino with tomato and potato and the pork shoulder special.  I suggest a bottle of Barolo. We'll be back!

Extremely popular italian restaurant in West village. Food is ok but especially the atmosphere is cool, typical of its neighborhood, rich, mature and relaxed. May be a victim of its success as you may wait long for a bit overbooked dish as it happened to me. Also personnel seems quite stressed. Sophisticated wine list. Eating at the bar is perfect.
Incredible wine list and wonderful bartender. The menu changes frequently but there's always plenty of vegetarian options.
Quaint restaurant,very homey, great olive oil, great service and great food. A definite must

I realized on my 2nd visit that EVERYTHING--absolutely everything on the menu (I'm not kidding) has cheese on it!  It's good cheese, but if you're lactose intolerant, not the place to go.  I finally had the artichoke lasagna: good, but not worth passing up an interesting special for...and definitely pushed me over the edge re: cheese (as I've already mentioned.)  This time there were 3 of us and the antipasto for 2 was still more than enough (and had 3 kinds of cheese.)  My friends raved about the tiramisu (which of course contains cheese,) they described it as perfect

I'm a pasta junkie, and I Sodi's is superb.  I'm talking about the papardelle con coniglia---many bites of which were stolen from my dining partner's plate--perfectly al dente noodles and a complex meaty sauce.  I also had the lasagna al carciofi, which was really interesting and tasty, and exceedingly rich, much more than I thought possible of artichokes.  Wine and cocktails were superb (I had a new drink 'il befana' made with saffron liqueur and the perfect balance of sweet and savory), as was the incredible olive oil, which I believe comes from the owner's personal groves in Italy.  Charcuterie plate also out of this world.  This is rustic Tuscan food at its finest.

Two stars for our nice waitress, plentiful meat and cheese board and tasty special vegetable lasagna.  Can't give anymore stars because:

1)  My special pork entree was overcooked and all of our greens (spinach and kale sides) were chopped and cooked to the point of looking and feeling like baby food.   I kid you not, it was like eating mashed greens.  Very gross.

2)  The tiramisu supposedly made with graham crackers instead of lady fingers was just a big plate of whipped cream.  So we used it as a topping for the flourless chocolate cake, which was pretty decent, and it actually made it better.

3)  The waiter who never helped us, except to ask if we were done our entrees, tried to shoo us out of the restaurant by taking our finished entrees and bringing us the check right away...without asking if we wanted dessert.  We were extremely confused by the check, of course, and so my friend asked if we could order dessert and coffee.  He, in turn, looked at us confusingly and said, "oh, you were the ones who arrived 40 minutes late, right?"  My friend:  "Um, nooOO, we didn't."  Waiter: "um, oh, um, ookaay...(brings dessert menus)."  

Our waitress ended up coming by later and taking our orders, and she definitely seemed oblivious to what had just happened (and we never mentioned it to her).

To get the story straight, here's what happened:  my friend and I arrived 5-10 minutes late to a nearly empty restaurant.  The waitress took our drink orders and never mentioned anything about needing to be out of the restaurant by a certain time.  Our other friend arrives 10 minutes after us and orders a cocktail right away.  The waitress still doesn't tell us that we need to be out by a certain time.  We sit there for a while longer before the waitress even comes to tell us what the specials are, so clearly SHE wasn't in a rush to get us out of there.  Had she or the other guy mentioned anything to us about a time limit so they could seat other customers, at any point before or during our meal, we would've happily sped up what started out to be a really nice dinner.  We would've ordered dessert ahead of time.  We wouldn't have spent a lot of time talking in between bites.  We could've helped them out.

Instead, they ended up pissing us off and souring the meal, and we ended up purposely taking our time eating dessert and drinking coffee.

We still tipped the usual 20% since it wasn't the waitress who screwed up.  But we won't be going back.

if it is possible... it just keeps getting better.... just went again last night- DIVINE heaven.
love
Small gem. Handsome bar. Very good pasta. Excellent salad. Couples seem comfortable. Attentive service with nice atmosphere.

We came here for a belated Valentine's dinner on the 15th and had a lovely evening.  I was impressed that the waiter took our coats at the door!  Other reviews here recommended the negroni, and although I've never had one before I decided to get it....very tasty, but not quite my thing (bitter!  which is, I guess, the point).

The food was fabulous.  I got the artichoke lasagna and it was heavenly....layers upon thin layers of artichoke, cheesy deliciousness, and pasta....divine.  My boy got the porcini risotto, which was very flavorful and well-cooked.  We got vegetable sides, but found that we didn't have the room in our stomaches or the desire to deviate from our main courses.  Also, our waiter recommended a great wine for us.

Bread came with delicious olive oil and 4 over-sized olives....I'm not usually an olive fan, but they were very good.

For dessert we got pear sorbet and panna cotta....both very good.
We spent almost 3 hours here and never felt rushed....great place for a nice dinner out!

Stopped by this restaurant at a friend's suggestion, and we were so glad that we did.  We didn't have a reservation, were happy to eat at the bar, but then we ended up moving to a table.  Everything was delicious from start to finish - the Negronis, the extensive wine list, and all the dishes.  But the yummy goat cheese and spinach ravioli stand out in my memory most clearly!  Whole meal was definitely enhanced by friendly, yet gracious, service.  Charlie was particularly charming, but the other waiter and bartender were also super.  We will definitely be back soon!!

We had an 8pm reservation, but were told that because of someone who arrived late for an earlier one, we wouldn't be seated right away. Being in no rush, so we took a seat at the bar, where the waiter offered us a free appetizer for our inconvenience and helped us select the absolutely perfect wine. We also got to enjoy the rightly-praised olive oil with some bread. While it took a full 40 minutes to finally be seated, I have to say we didn't mind at all. The ambience is wonderful. 

When we were seated, we ordered an asparagus appetizer with poached egg, the spinach ravioli with sage butter and the meat lasagna. The asparagus and ravioli were both amazing. The lasagna was just okay. I don't think their usage of many ultra-thin layers of pasta quite works in such a hearty dish. 

The pricing is a bit high, but that's to be expected. Service, atmosphere, food and wine list are all great enough to make I Sodi worth it.

I Sodi is a comforting, neighborhood-y, perfect Ristorante Toscano. I've been going here since it opened a couple years back and I think it keeps getting better and better. Seriously, it never wavers and is consistently delicious! This Tuscan restaurant gem is owned by Rita Sodi, who has gathered all her tremendous skills from her Northern Florence roots, putting them to great use in her pasta dishes. 

As a pasta person, it's really hard for me to go to Italian restaurants and not have pasta - so I almost always do! Every time I dine at I Sodi, I HAVE TO get Rita Sodi's artichoke lasagna, which I believe is what she's best known for. Honestly, there is no match out there for this phenomenal dish. Another favorite is the cacio e pepe; where a simple sauce of cheese, butter and pepper combine to produce a surprisingly sophisticated flavor combination. Aside from pasta, the artichoke salad is definitely worth ordering, the Cornish hen cooked under a brick is perfectly seasoned and crispy on the outside, succulent on the inside, and even the bread and olives are divine (trust me, once you order it you'll understand). All Sodi's olive oils are homemade; lovingly pressed by her gardener back in Italy. Can you believe that? Of course, she gets the olive oil so right and gorgeous - I LOVE IT. 

Honestly, you can't go wrong by eating here. I Sodi is perfect for what it is - so get out there and relish a quiet evening in its charming Tuscan setting. Eat it up!

Click here for the vlog version: http://www.kimberlybelle.com/2011/05/i-sodi-the-dutch-eat-it-up.html

This place hides in plain sight in the west village. 

The Asparagus came with a poached egg and grated cheese -- amazingly delicious combination. The Osso Bucco was a bit salty but the meat was very tender and there was a large piece of delicious marrow in my serving. The lentils that came with it were mushy. The Risotto was excellent. I'm not a huge fan of rice but this was heavenly, not over seasoned. The Lemon Sponge Cake was very good. I liked that it had merely a thin layer of cake at bottom and middle, and more light spongy cream. 

This cute place has a small number of tables and the service was good.

Great food and service.  The artichoke salad, side of peas, and lasagna was so good I am going to have to force myself not to order it every time I go.  Radicchio salad was awesome as well.  

Great atmosphere and location.  Staff was helpful and friendly.
My favorite Italian restaurant.  Just perfect.  Don't skip the lasagna or the peas ever.

I live on Christopher street and walk by this place everyday... I have always found it a little odd that this semi-fancy restaurant is on kinda a grimy block in the west village... right next to the adult shops and the "tobacco" shops (head shops). 

I literally just got home from dinner... hands down one of the best meals I have had in NYC so far... my mom had this pounded steak special... AMAZING! 

And the pasta was so good... I will be making a return trip! 

And there is no TV!!!

My family and I love love love this restaurant!  We have been in NY for several weeks now and we have made it to I Sodi once a week.  We are always taking friends there and/or just enjoying the great Italian food ourselves.  The wait staff is very friendly and if your table is not ready at or near your reservation time, then they are generous with an appetizer or after-dinner drink to compensate.  This is an all-around favorite!

While the food was fantastic, it was the worst service I've ever encountered in NYC.  The first part of our party arrived on time and checked in with the bar tender (there is no hostess).  When the second half arrived only 10min later, they had already given away our table!  While they did comp us for our bottle of wine, I still don't expect to be seated at the bar after holding a reservation for over a month.  After our table mix up, it took an hour to get our appetizer and another hour to get our entrees.  Since when does a two course meal served at a bar take almost 2.5hrs?  Despite an overly salty salad (so salty it was barely edible), the rest of the food was excellent.  They surely cook in a classic, deconstructed Italian style with quality, fresh ingredients.  Its a shame they couldn't get their act together on service, because the food was at least worth another try.

I came here for a nice dinner with a friend and all of their tables were booked for the night (Sunday) so we sat at the still - but not for long - empty bar.  The restaurant is pretty small, perhaps not by New York standards, but small enough that I could see them turning people away at the door.  If you don't make reservations, your best bet is the bar which you need to get to early.

I had the Steak Tartare appetizer and the House Made Spaghetti with Clams.  The steak was excellent - the meat was finely chopped, served with fresh greens, on grilled bread.  The small serving of the spaghetti was decent.  It  came in a parsley, white wine sauce that was a little bit too thick for my tastes but the pasta itself was decadently made and perfectly cooked.  The staff was very friendly and punctual - the dishes never came too early, the orders were just on time and the water was always filled.

For a drink, I got the I Sodi Tom Collins and it is HUGE.  Yes, it is 13 bucks.  But man, it took me the entire dinner to finish that one drink and it was loaded with gin.  

Overall, it was a little bit pricey but definitely worth it.

We had the most delightful evening. Welcoming and competent service, pleasant surroundings, excellent food, and good company. This is a neighborhood spot that is worth leaving your neighborhood to enjoy.
Highlights: Carciofi anything; affogato con nocciola (unbelievable!), the negronis were delicious, and they were willing to substitute prosecco for the non-gin drinker. We had a remarkable grappa with dessert, golden with aging. Not inexpensive, but sublime.

I love I Sodi! My boyfriend and I live around the corner, and it's our favorite Italian restaurant in the neighborhood. We usually go late and sit at the bar for dinner. The bartenders are professional, knowledgeable and charming. Both the cocktail and the wine menu are topnotch. And the food! I've yet to have a bad dish. Wonderful, wonderful. It can be noisy, which is one of the reasons we like to sit at the bar. Personally, we think it's ideal for two people.

Came here early (6:30pm) on a Sunday for dinner first date. It was very empty when I first arrived but by the end of the meal the place was packed. As far as fine dining goes this place was tiny, even for New York standards. It wasn't claustrophobic though, you had some semblance of space to move and whatnot but there were only 10 or so tables in the whole restaurant. Usually talking about random shit with a first date can be awkward with a couple sitting right next to you probably listening to every word but luckily this particular date was really fun and cute so I didn't really care. 

Anyway, note to self: I don't like Negroni's. They taste like bad cologne. I forced the Classico down but will probably never try one of those again. They had a pretty tiny wine list since it was all Italian wines only, but still had some decent options. We had a Riesling that was semi sweet but good. The food was good, my NY Strip was a bit salty but still delicious. My date got the ravioli since she was a vegetarian but it was very good. I would recommend that for sure. We got the Tiramisu desert and it was pretty good. Not made in the traditional way. 

The one thing I will say about this place is that it's not traditional Italian in that I felt like we were somewhat rushed through our meal since we did a lot of talking instead of eating which slowed us down a bit. They came by with our pasta courses before we were finished with Apps because they thought we weren't going to eat anymore off our plates but we weren't finished. That was kind of annoying and happened with pretty much every course throughout the night. My date thought it was worse than I did, she rates the service a 7/10 and I have it an 8. 

I would suggest eating here, but make a reservation and eat quickly!

VERY disappointing.  A friend who loves it took us here.  4 requests for bread before it came.  An hour for food to come.  Some things were good, but my pasta special was so salty it was inedible.  When the server asked how it was, I replied "fine".  That seemed to irk her and she became aggravated.  Then her voice cracked as if I had offended her and she was about to cry.  WHAT???   Ridiculous.  Owner sat at bar dining and chatting with friends as this all took place.  A free desert and a couple of things removed from the bill didn't make it ok for me.  A really bad experience and I had to eat a sandwich when I got home.

Terrible place! Our first visit to I Sodi last week was positive (tipped 35%). We returned 1 week later, ordered the same entrées that we had the prior week, but this time, we found one of the entrées inedible. We sent it back. Chef/owner Rita Sodi responded with an aggressive and rude reply through our server: "That's the way the dish comes." We advised the dish was good the week before, but (incredibly) Rita refused to admit there could have been something wrong with the dish this time around. She refused to send out a second dish of the same entrée, convincing us that "Chef Rita" is not playing with a full deck of cards and has no clue how to manage a restaurant and relate to returning customers.  According to our server, this kind of erratic and argumentative behavior is typical of her.  We will NEVER return.

I Sodi is a wonderful, genuine Italian restaurant in the West Village. If you are in search of excellent food in a cute restaurant, go to I Sodi. The beautiful atmosphere, delightful food and friendly staff are sure to please.

The atmosphere at I Sodi is great if you enjoy intimate restaurants in hip neighborhoods. I Sodi is a small restaurant (maybe 8 tables plus bar seating) that is only a few hundred square feet. The ceiling is high, the bar is a nice thick slab of marble and the tables are dressed in tablecloth and joined by comfortable chairs. Every detail was truly paid attention to from the beautiful, old wood ceiling to the sliding doors to the bathrooms. I Sodi is the perfect atmosphere for a simple but delicious dining experience.

The food at I Sodi is exquisite. The appetizers I have tasted include the Spaghetti Cacio E Pepe (spaghetti with pecorino and black pepper,) the Rucola E Castelmagno (arugula with castelmagno cheese) and the Insalata Di Carciofi E Parmigiano (artichoke salad with parmesan). I recommend all three, but my favorite is the spaghetti with pecorino, which has a soft butter sauce and sharp pepper taste. In terms of entrees, I have tasted the steak (it was a special the people I was with ordered) and it was exceptional and the Galleto Schiacciato (cornish hen grilled under a brick). The hen is large, although it is upsetting it doesn't come with any side dishes. From the salads to the hen the food is fresh and perfectly prepared. My only complaint is that the food takes a little while to come, but at a place like this I don't mind waiting the extra 10 minutes.

Lastly, the staff here is friendly and personable. They are professional and are truly experts of the menu. The wait staff of two describes dishes in exquisite detail and is knowledgeable about pairing wines with dishes. Furthermore, we were impressed to see that after only having come to I Sodi twice before (over the course of 6 months), the waitress remembered us and even the drinks we had ordered.

If you enjoy genuine Italian food in a chic downtown restaurant, I highly recommend I Sodi. Just make sure to make a reservation!

I really want to like this place.  I've been a few times now.  They have a menu that features several different kinds of Negronis...I love Negronis.  But the food just isn't that special...neither is the space or the service.

On our most recent visit, we placed our order, and then a few minutes later we witnessed our server telling another table about specials that he hadn't mentioned to us.  That's super lame.  I also had to practically light my hair on fire to get him to drop the check.

The only redemption was that we spotted Wallace Shawn (of Princess Bride fame) in the dining room.  INCONCEIVABLE!
Rude and haughty waitstaff; we came early; told them we had a deadline and they never got us our food and presented a check for the full amount.  Don't go there

I think I almost cried the last time I was here, and was informed that the kitchen had run out of its wild boar ragu for the night... it's that good. 

The service is wonderful, the food is always excellent and it's wonderfully cozy inside. My only gripe is that the place is so tiny, and it's not really one of those neighborhood places where you can just drop in and hope for a table. But, no restaurant in the West Village is, so I guess it is what it is. Still, it's worth the effort to make the reservation, and get there early before they run out of that sauce!

Consistently good, every time.

Not five star because we only sit at the bar... We never get a table... This place is booked solid!

Bravo!

I went here early with my GF on a Friday night  before a Knicks' game (a fair quid pro quo, if you ask me) and we were very pleased. I. Sodi is small and a little on the cramped side, but it's all about the food and service here. 

IS is Tuscan, only with salt in the bread and some pleasant creative touches. The menu is divided into appetizer, pasta and entree sections and sets up well for a four-course affair. I like that they offer the pastas in half-portions, so you can lighten the caloric intake instead of the wallet. We aren't huge eaters, and sharing an appetizer, a half-order of ravioli and the strip steak was the perfect amount of food. I particularly like the roasted artichoke salad. It was mandoline'd to resemble a lettuce salad and expertly seasoned -- an example of creative technique applied to a simple tuscan preparation that is a great metaphor for the cuisine. The menu features some rotation to keep things dynamic. As you'd expect, the wine list is heavy on the italianos and offers a good selection of half-bottles and quartinos (which you don't find nearly enough of around here).

Service was professional and knowledgeable, although they did get a little overwhelmed when the crowd picked up (we got there around 6:15PM Friday). 

There are tons of small, cute West Village italians, so it means something when one merits a return trip. I'd come back.

Had a lovely evening here: 
Excellent service from Charlie (he claims to be from Trenton but I'm sure he's a Poughkeepsie-ite).
Thorough wine list fairly priced.  Chestnut pasta was delicious.  Antipasto plate was huge--not even sure how they make any money on it.  Rabbit rolled in pork was crunchily salted and cooked perfectly.
Reminded us off the sadly departed Alba Osteria in Portland.
Will revisit next time we're in Manhattan

I Sodi is a solid neighborhood restaurant that hides behind frosted glass and feels miles away from the Christopher Street riff raff. It's perfect for a Friday or Saturday night date, because usually you can get a reservation within a week prior, it's small, intimate, and romantic. The service is generally good, with friendly staff and everything timed out well. They've got a good wine list, and the pasta is exceptional, with much or all of it made in house. And of course, my boyfriend is a big fan of the rabbit.

Lovely! Came here on a Tuesday evening with a party of 5. We started at the bar while waiting for the whole party and we had perfectly balanced assorted martini's. This restaurant is very small and intimate and has a wonderful selection of aperitifs, bitters, hard to find bottles. Bartender was knowledgeable and a lovely dialogue with the other waitstaff as we sipped away. The employees all had a sense of ownership/pride in their place to such a degree that is was surprised to hear that they were not the actual owners. Hard to find that anymore.

We were seated on time and service was excellent. Had the antipasti plate for the table and it was possibly the largest selection I've ever had. We also had the vegetable crudités with an olive oil from the chefs own farm in Tuscany. It was Devine.

Our waiter was very knowledgeable and assisted each of us in choosing between the generally two items we were torn between. Perfect calls all the way around. We all ordered pasta from the tagliatelle to the lasagna; it was all amazing. Fresh ingredients and de deceptively simple dishes. A great option is the 1/2 plate which is a lot of food still but allows appetizers that you can fully enjoy.

We ordered a few bottles for the table and although the bottles were quite costly ($183 per) it was well worth it as the wine was a perfect pairing. I am not as familiar with Italian wines vs. French and Northern Ca wines so I relied on the sommelier. He choose perfectly.

We order 3 desserts for the table, chocolate panna cotta, a tiramasu and a in house made layered bar that was seriously the best dessert I may have ever had. Enjoyed with an espresso and coffee drinks by half the party. The coffee is as pure, rich, polished and mature as the rest of the meal. 

I will be back often. I love the Village anyway and this small restaurant embodies the best of it.

***disclaimer: I recently came back from a trip to Italy which harbored the most incredible food I've ever eaten**

Now, let us join together for a moment of silence as we thank Rita Sodi for honoring the integrity of fresh farm food and the authenticity of traditional italian cuisine. 

Don't be a fool and waste your time on the Tuscan antipasti plate, which breaks down to be a lot of meat and three pieces of cheese.

Do try her own olive oil and her neighbor's olive oil with the pillowy fresh bread, but don't fill up! 

The heart and soul of this operation lies within the pasta dishes and each bite will bring joy that you won't want to end. Now I never want to compare a pasta dish to my Nona's homemade pasta, but I Sodi, you have changed me. I had to control myself from shoveling down the ravioli with spinach and sage. The pasta was cookie cutter delicate and filled with honest flavor and savory goodness. 

I could comment on the service, the atmosphere, but I left singing about the pasta.
This is one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan. The food is excellent, the drinks are declicious and the staff makes the experience enjoyable!

I have probably walked passed I Sodi a number of times and never noticed it was there. Now, I hesitate to write this review to keep the restaurant a well kept secret. However, I know that is pretty foolish as there are over 70 reviews and it was recently featured in a "12 pasta dishes to eat before you die" in NYC. If you never make it to Italy, come here and get the Cacio e Pepe, because it truly is the best version I've ever had this side of the pond. 

The restaurant itself is small, cozy and apparently once was a sushi restaurant which explains the sliding screen doors and lots of light wood around the bar area. The place only seats about 40-ish or so people, so make a reservation if its a weekend. The wait staff was friendly, helpful and always checking in on us throughout the meal -- a long lost art at many restaurants in the city.

Other must eats:

1) artichoke salad - simple artichokes with cheese on top
2) Cacio e Pepe
3) the "Chocolate salami" dessert -- served with vanilla gelato and "slices of salami" which are really just chocolate ganash with gram cracker pieces to look like marble salami. 

For specials, if they have them, get the taglietelle with meat ragu. It was to die for -- and I'm a ragu snob. Anyway, RUN, do not WALK to I sodi, you wont regret it.
Like a trip to Rome. Very subtle, small menu but authentic Italian food. Excellent wine list and service. Bar service also very detailed.

1)Very cozy, small authentic italian restaurant near tribeca.
2)Dishes are seasonal and very fresh.
3)Their antipasto is outstanding, highly recommended.
4)Wish selection is limited and overpriced.
5)Pastas are all hand made. good but not as good as i trulli.
6)Their Sorbets are out of this world!

I took my parents here on Sunday. You might not understand the extremity of this statement.... I. took. my. parents. here. 

And they liked it.

My father, who spent majority his childhood in Italy, was amazed by the Artichoke Lasagna. My never-easy-to-please mother told the friendly and attentive staff that she would come back soon.

Thanks alot, i Sodi... now I have to see them again "soon."

Positives:  

Been several times...

Very helpful staff.  They know exactly how the (limited menu) is prepared, they're patient, and they don't rush you while eating.  Polished without being stuffy.  

Food is simple and delicious.  The empahsis is quality over quantity.  I am not a big eater, but portion sizes that are grossly excessive tick me off.  This place does it right, and I never leave hungry.

Negatives:

It is small, and it can be very hard to get a rez.  Still, that's hardly a knock, just a tip to plan ahead, or go at a slightly less popular time.  Another tip: if you have a party of five, plan even further ahead as only one table readily accomodates.  I'm not a fan of taking more seats than required in peak times - unfair to the establishment.  Dinner at the bar for one or two is also a good alternative. 

The food is a bit heavy on the salt.  Doesn't bother me, it works for the dishes.  I just have an extra bottle of water.  But others may not like.

Lunch on the weekend is a total winner as it's not well-known yet.  You'll get plenty of space and attention.

What a pleasant experience. Walking in the west village looking for a new restaurant off of hudson. Turned onto christopher and found I Sodi. Wasn't sure what to expect with a smaller menu selection but dinner was excellent.

Staff was very attentive and very knowledgable in the food and wine pairings.

Thanks for a great meal.

It's so loud in this small restaurant that you can't really enjoy a conversation or hear what the server was saying. 
We ordered the antipasto for 2 to share. It was a huge portion, enough for 4 to share, tons of meat, not much cheese. No olives, artichokes, just more meat. The server should have suggested a portion for 1 would be ample and add a salad. 
I had the Lasagna, it was nothing special. My mate had the Rabbit, he enjoyed it. A few desserts were ok but nothing spectacular. We ordered 2 more glasses of wine after our bottle and of course she poured us the most expensive on the list, not nice.
I really think this place is way overrated, much better food at L'artusi.

Good Food, Not Fantastic Experience. 

The food was really good - the artichokes were fantastic, as promised. The antipasto was very generous and the meats were flavorful / the cheese was tasty. I got a butter and sage spinach and cheese raviolli and it was pretty good - very rich, as you would expect. The pasta itself was pretty fantastic. The lasagne lacked something to be desired. The Panna cotta was extremely good. 

If it was food alone, i would have ranked this place higher. 

The space is small and as others have mentioned, it got very loud. To a frustrating degree. Also, becasue the place is so small, they have a bar and row of tables with a bench on one side and just stools on the other side. People are constantly trying to get by in the tight quarters, so you often get knocked if you're on a stool. Also, the tables are small and its hard to enjoy a nice, relaxing long dinner on a stool, flesh against a tiny table, constantly having to move.

The service was great.

Sodi was an excellent experience.  The service was spectacular.  The food was excellent in every respect.  Atmosphere was great, we had a window seat, with soft music in the background.  We had a great time and the prices were good too.  For those who don't want the massive portions they offer halves, which I always like.

I Sodi is a pretty nice Italian place, considering I'm not terribly experienced as a diner of this cuisine in New York - even over my 8 years - nor am I well-versed in the foods and regions of Italy, etc.  With that in mind, I still know a fairly tasty place and with the variety of dishes we got (some halfplates, a monstrous meat/cheese app for two and a secondi), I can't complain.

There is a special, classic looking (perhaps mahogany or oak?) wood bar lining the center of the space, as well as semi-luminous crystal-esque wall lights which cast a not overbearing light on the few tables which comprise I Sodi.

But, as is the problem with many restaurants in a metropolis where space is ever the precious resource, I Sodi is narrow, which can make for an unpleasant experience.  Since I was trying to be a good friend, I let my buddy take the banquette seat against the wall while I fell casualty to everyone passing by that makes no attempt to avoid the body brush up, which all New Yorkers expect to avoid, especially when they dine in a restaurant.  The brush up is a huge pet peeve of mine, and I expect others share it as well.  When people are constantly shuffling behind you and then rubbing your shirt or leg in doing so, it's like a nagging, distracting itch that won't go away and you're expecting it at every point of the meal.

However, I know that this is ultimately inevitable especially in a small and busy place (if it's really small, does that make it busy or full? Ha), so I'm fine with conferring 4 stars to I Sodi, with a pretty good likelihood that I'll return.  

Except this time I'll be the one on the banquette.

Managed to go hear practically two times in a row.  The first was a friday night the second one week later was a saturday lunch.  Lets compare!  While BOTH were excellent experineces I"ll have to say that the lunch crowd time was the one I prefer.  While they do MAJOR crowd control in the evening time (its a TINY restaurant)  and the place is buzzing with locals and visitors, you'll just get the place to yourself on the weekend lunch.  You can see the beautiful marble walls, the beautiful wood trim and you'll be able to hear your dining companions because it is SO quiet.  Yes, go on a romantic date during the evening, but go for a nice quiet lunch on the weekend too.  You wont be dissapointed either way.

Cute and quaint spot. Reasonable prices, friendly service! I think the risotto was the best dish. We tried a number of plates and shared them all. The tomato and mozz salad was awesome!

I'd come back, positive experience.

Hurricane Sandy can now carry me away now that I've eaten at I Sodi. I was literally jumping up and down in my seat and clapping my hands with glee while eating my three different pasta dishes. Every single pasta dish was exactly how I imagine that pasta should be. It's a little bit of Tuscan heaven brought special to you :)

+Cacio e pepe: EXACTLY how I would describe it should be made. Al dente. Not too cheesy. Peppery. Slippery.
+Tagliatelle with truffle, butter, and mushroom: why is truffle so seductive? Sex on a plate.
+Rigatoni with meat sauce: yum.

If you're just 2 people: sit at the bar. The bartender is awesome and friendly. Order dessert. Be happy.

As good a Tuscan meal as I have had - including some epic ones in Italy.  This is a real neighborhood gem restaurant with MUCH better food than you could reasonably expect in a neighborhood gem.  This place will never be fancy, or cater to people who want to make a statement.  Instead it's a restaurant I would love to go back to every month (but sadly I don't live in NYC so that's not possible.....).

Have had some nice meals here until last week. We were left waiting with a reservation for 25 mins. We were 2 so we understood when a table for 4 left we would still have to wait. But when a table for 2 became free and they decided to add a seat and hold it for a future table for 3 this was ridiculous. Walked out after that. Honor patrons who reserved and have already waited. Won't be back. Its just not that good to put up with rude management.

Great little, cozy, quaint restaurant/bar near the Lucille Lortel Theater in the village. Went there as a recommendation from some friend who are theater buffs. I had a mushroom pasta dish which was excellent. My wife had the spinach ravioli. Drinks were great. This place is very small with few tables. Our service was excellent from Kristin. Had the honey grappa as desert. Another excellent choice.

BOTTOM LINE: GREAT FOOD, GOOD SERVICE, AND SUPER CUTE!

This is one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the city. I have been here many times and I am always tempted to go back. The food is amazing! I always order the caccio e pepe pasta (even if it's not on the menu and not the risotto, the pasta) and my fiance usually gets the lasagna with meat sauce (but I'm curious to try the vegetarian version). We are tempted to try the other dishes, but these two keep calling out to us! I highly recommend you go here!

Great little neighborhood gem.

Lovely dinner on a rainy Thursday night at the bar.

Pastas are authentic and gorgeous.  
We had the lasagne w/ sugo and the ravioli w/ spinach and ricotta.
A cured meat platter and the Porchetta, which was rabbit stuffed with pork and wrapped in bacon.  

Excellent wines by the glass and terrific dessert, a layered chocolate graham cracker with gelato.

Service was excellent, knowledgeable and friendly.  

Nice local crowd.
Looking forward to going back soon.

Nice for a romantic dinner or dinner with friends.
xo

The preparations and flavors at I Sodi are clean and focused.  To start, we loved the bella di cerignola olives, one of our favorites!  The restaurant owner's olive oil was rich and lovely, with green flavors.  The white bread had a wonderful chewy texture but was a little salty.  The branzino ($30) was very fresh and simple, beautifully prepared in parchment paper and served with capers.  The artichoke lasagna ($19) was delicious as well but not entrancing past the first few bites.  The slight excess of salt made it one note.  We were happy we had ordered it as a shared first course.  Definitely try it!  The Brussels sprouts ($10) were deliciously creamy, the fried artichoke ($10) shredded too finely to leave any moist heart after frying; the large portion was entirely crispy and spiky.  Several spritzes of lemon enhanced it quite a bit.  The affogato al nocino ($8) was a great ending.

Our waitress was helpful but very cold -- perhaps because of a couple of mix-ups?  Not sure who was at fault, but she seemed perturbed.  When someone had the kitchen fire Brussels sprouts (which turned out to be much better than the fried artichoke, so we were glad in the end!) for us instead of fried artichoke, she offered them to us on the house and brought us the artichoke a few minutes later.  When the Brussels sprouts and a Coke appeared inexplicably on our check, she immediately had them removed.  The other server was lovely: warm and attentive.

The restaurant was very busy, but no one rushed us out.  The first customers in the house, we lingered an enjoyable two hours.  The crowd tends to be older.  The decor is spare, light, and formal.

All considered, we had a fine meal.  Given the number of excellent restaurants in the city, we probably won't be back.  The cold service is the main reason.

Visited I Sodi with my husband on a Saturday night. Was a little annoyed since I had to make a reservation almost 10 days in advance to get something on a weekend, but when I got there, I realized why, the restaurant is super small, maybe fits about 12 tables? But it is definitely a hidden gem. 

We got there at exactly 9:30 and our table was almost ready for us, we were sat down within 2 minutes. Since the restaurant is a bit tight, they have a small closet in the back in which the server can take your jacket for you. We received water right away but we didn't get our cocktails for almost 15 minutes, which I thought was a bit slow, but it was well worth it. They have a small selection of signature cocktails. I am always willing to try restaurant cocktails before I order my typical favorite drinks, sometimes you find something good. 

When we received our drinks, we ordered out food right away.. we got the  italiano antipasti platter, which is just prosciutto, salami, cheeses and some bread. Overall pretty typical, nothing amazing about it. Then we got the lasagna and lamb special as our entrees. Overall very delish! The lasagna had about 12 layers, I counted! The pasta felt as if it was homemade, the meat was seasoned well and it was a pretty decent sized portion. When we got the lamb, it looked different than we though. We expected like a nice cut of meat, but instead it was kind of mushy and chopped up. But it still tasted good and the mashed peas were very good. Overall the lasagna was presented well, but the lamb special wasn't presented well on the plate, kind of looked  like a pile of blob, but at least it tasted amazing. We also got a chocolate dessert which was very good as well.

Overall everything was decently priced and we had a good experience. Besides the kind of slow service on the drinks, the night was pretty much perfect. Would def recommend for a date night!

The Meat lasagna with a side of spinach is as good as gets.Genius!
LOVE isodi!

This place isn't as tiny as people make it seem - it actually has very large tables for New York City. One of the largest I've ever sat at.

The olive oil is what drew me here and it was quite good. I got the ravioli (half portion which was definitely enough for me, but I don't tend to eat a lot at every meal) and my fiancee got the lasagna. Both were good - the lasagna definitely isn't something you're mom makes from home. 

Just so you know, when they ask flat or sparkling, flat means a $3 600 ml bottle. Maybe it's just me, but I definitely thought I was getting tap when I said "flat." If you want tap water, ask for tap.

Had dinner here last night with my parents and loved it.  As everyone mentions, this is a small place and it's sometimes difficult to find a reservation time (protip: walk in for an early dinner around 6pm before it gets too busy).  

The service was excellent and the food even better - everything we had was near perfection.  Highlights were the two spaghetti-type dishes (cacio de pepe and the seasonal one they had), but the fried chicken was also delicious.  Even the side order of fries were good.

A decent bottle of chianti classico runs about $50 - not too bad.

It kind of looks like a place where people might be pretentious but the staff were very welcoming from start to finish. Actually, from before the start...I walked in on a whim one Friday when family were visiting just to see if they might have a table. She pencilled me in at a time that wasn't unreasonably late. 

The restaurant is a bit small but I like that kind of feeling. They also have understated table settings that convey style without trying too hard. First course was a delicious meat and cheese plate. Next was a very simple pasta dish but that dish won me over. If you've ever been to Italy, you know that pasta is often before the entree and usually kind of simple but delicious. I Sodi seems to be aware that a pasta dish is successful if its like a pyramid - strong at the base - in contrast to the cliché Italian restaurant in the US with poor quality pasta topped with some crazy sauce. Anyways, their pasta was simple and delicious...the perfect primi. Last, we ordered the special a 58 oz steak to share among three. The choice was kind of for npstalgia's sake because the last time I was in Italy, I had a great steak with my brother in law at a restaurant called il Vecchio in Florence. We thought, why not try again since we got the impression that I Sodi goes for that Florentine vibe. Anyways, we were the envy of the restaurant when it came out and the taste did not disappoint. I think the veggies were a spinach that all enjoyed. 

No comment on dessert. We were so full we skipped it, went for a walk and had gelato down the street. I swear we did not intend to recreate a dinner out in Italy but if you want to feel like you're in Italy for a night, I Sodi is a good place to start.

I lived on Christopher Street for a year and unfortunately never made it to I Sodi even though it was on my list of places to try. The restaurant is discreet from the outside and you may not even notice it as you walk by. Inside the space is small, and the bar takes up a big section, but they make it work. My friend and I came here for dinner on a Thursday night after making a reservation in advance. Reservations are definitely recommended since there are so few tables. On to the meal...it was delicious! I loved every dish we had. As we ordered our wine, the waiter brought out bread and olive oil, which I always appreciate. We started with the beef tartare and a mozzarella and heirloom tomato special. Everything was extremely fresh tasting. My favorite part of the meal was definitely the pasta. You can order half or full size portions which is great if you're anything like me and want to try a few things. The two of us shared half sizes of the cacio e pepe, ricotta and spinach ravioli, and meat lasagna. I admit it was an aggressive order and I ended up taking home most of the lasagna - but it made excellent left overs! The pasta dishes were perfectly cooked and while the ingredients were relatively simple, the overall taste was amazing. I can't wait to come back and try some of the entrees, which also looked great. We finished the night off with dessert, some kind of hazelnut ice cream, while making friends with the table next to us. Overall great experience with friendly and attentive service. Reasonable prices for the portion sizes.

Love this restaurant; I don't know why! I think it is because I feel its unpretentious for the West Village - but has every right to be.
