The food is amazing, I love the simple and clean-cut decor, and service is always spot on. My boyfriend and I went last night and had the antipasto (get it for one - we got it for 2 last time and it was wayyyy too much), fried artichokes, and 3 pastas - the ravioli with sage sauce, rigatoni with meat sauce, and risotto. All were excellent except for the risotto (but I hold mine to a high regard). Will definitely return!

Food is delicious and service very good.  Place is small, always crowded, and you can feel cramped. Reservations definitely required in advance as this is a neighborhood favorite as well as a destination spot. Can get noisy.

Came here on a date night over year ago and loved it. Just walked by and had fond 
memories

This place has great service--it could be a totally snobby, typical NY place, but the staff are very friendly.  I really liked the heirloom tomato salad and the rigatoni that I had.  Their version of tiramisu, with graham crackers, doesn't taste like much of anything, so I would skip it.

Excellent, fresh neighborhood Italian restaurant.  Design and ambience inside the venue is great and the menu items and service are very good.  Nice selection of wine as well.  I think it's in the same league as DellAnima and L'artussi.
A wonderful Italian Italian restaurant that always exceeds expectations. Great intimate space too.

Had dinner there with a few friends and just loved it. Amazing food and even better sides. Had the ravioli which was just perfect. For sides we got the fried artichokes which are to die for, leeks, as well as one other. Great wine selection too.
overall a small cozy italian place in the west village with amazing food.

It pains me to write this. I love I Sodi. The restaurant has its trendy west village charm with a great clientele. The food is fantastic and had been our go-to Italian spot for about a year now. The vegetable lasagna is seasonal and we've really enjoyed the artichoke over the zucchini over the leek, but even the leek one puts any other restaurant to shame. It's only outdone by the meat lasagna. Although the fried artichoke is out of this world. If you want an appetizer, go for the Burrata.

Unfortunately I'm not writing this for the food. I Sodi also happens to be one of the few places without a host - and this is a warning for small restaurateurs who think it's worth saving a few dollars by not paying for one. 

The Usual: They often make you wait a bit for a reservation. It's a small restaurant and people often linger, no huge deal. But they are typically nice enough about it.

The Hiccup: We come here a lot, and had international friends visiting. Since we live around the corner we figured that after Market Table, Red Farm, Joseph Leonard.. it was about time for Italian. We had an opentable reservation for 9:15PM and had hyped the restaurant. I had a meeting all day and got out at 7PM to a voicemail from I Sodi (no name) stating:
- 7:00PM: Received voicemail of 4:11PM stating new policy that they require same day confirmation. Need to call by 5PM to confirm reservation
- 7:00: Called back, and went to voicemail. Tried two more times to no avail.
- 7:30: Tried calling again. Voicemail again.
- 7:45: Saw email from ~6PM from opentable confirming a cancellation
- 8:00: Called back. Voicemail twice.
- 8:01: Tried with different phone, immediately picked up.
- A) Charlie picked up the phone and explained that they tried calling but given I didn't respond within the allotted 50 minute window he gave away our table. That 
- B) there was nothing he could do despite explaining how we had come 4 times in the last 2-months. Explained that the policy of same day confirmation had always been there, even withstanding that I had never had this incident previously.
- C) He said that he thought I no-showed in the past so cancelled my reservation. I explained this was not possible and to check my opentable record. He explained that "No tables will be available for you and I need to attend to paying customers" 
- D) Charlie then said he would call me back on the "201" number (indicating he had been screening my "646" number calls when he could work out a new table
- 9:15: Charlie calls back to explain that he is the equivalent of the manager and that we would not be seated. Then hung up.

I apologize as this may read as a rant. I was genuinely in shock by the series of events, especially since we had friends visiting and since it took them until our reservation time to relay the final "screw you." I get that places can overbook but if that's the case at least take responsibility and apologize. Charlie made it seem that I was affronting him by wanting to show up to my reservation.

I am saddened as a patron because I really liked the food. It's staff like this that give ny a bad rap.

[Silver lining: Ended up at Hudson Clearwater.. awesome!]

I Sodi is terrific. It's a tiny West Village restaurant dedicated to the best of Italian cuisine. The food and service is spectacular. It's a small place and reservations are difficult to come by - but it's worth the trouble to eat here.

The food in general is very good.  I ordered a vegetable lasagna which
was a little pastey but good.  My husband had the boar which he said was
OK but would not order it again.  We ordered fried artichoke which was
soggy, and tasteless.  Desert was vanilla pudding and berries - very good.  We started with the bruschetta which was wonderful.  The menu is very limited.
Not a great place for those that don't eat red meat or chicken.

Service was very good.

(3.5 stars)

Came here to celebrate my birthday with the family. It's a small space that is crowded! It has sliding doors to enter and in the bathroom to save space. We had 8pm reservations on a Saturday and had to wait awkwardly on top of people for our table, given the limited waiting space, full bar and below 30 temperature outside. I know the two tops up front are good for business but perhaps adding a bench or something there instead would be handy. 7 people loitering around the tables as people tried to dine wasn't ideal, mostly for those diners!

Service was friendly throughout and we definitely ordered more than enough food. With 1 "for 2" antipasto for a table of 5, 3 sides, and 5 full entrees, we ended up not finishing 1/2 the sides and 2 entrees. Should've ordered 1 (maybe 2) sides and half portions of the pastas. We got greedy!

Everything was yummy but I wasn't blown away. NYC Italian is competitive!

Meh. Maybe I expected too much after reading reviews and my friend's recommendation to come here, but my experience was pretty mediocre.  Food wasn't memorable, space is small/crampy and not special, but service was friendly.  

Italian in NYC is so competitive. I don't think I would come back to I Sodi with all the other options available in the city... Just not memorable.

Had the pleasure of trying this neighborhood gem while visiting NY.  We started out at the bar with delicious crafted cocktails. The bartender really listened to what I liked and came up with a fresh, enticing cocktail. 

Everything was impeccable. We shared an amazing mâché salad and a gorgeous array of baby vegetables spread across a platter. For dinner the fish special was out of this world. And our vegetable sides were flavorful and robust. 

The wine list had many great offerings. The staff was well versed, poised and helpful.  I can't wait to return on my next trip to NY.

Hmmmmm...major conundrum on the star rating. I took my friend here this evening for his birthday, it was his pick, and he insisted that I award 5 stars, I think he was just dazzled by my company. I definitely had a great experience but 5 star? Not so sure. We had an early 6:00 rese on a chilly Tuesday night, I walked in on time, my date was already there at the bar. We were offered a table right away. The place is very cozy I.e. tiny with that west vill charm. To start I went with a negroni, it's what they're famous for, and wowie did it pack a punch. My date, believe it or not chose a pomegranate Martini. He had the girlie drink, I had the one that puts hair on your chest. His was very good if a tad sweet. Our waiter was very attentive and also very sweet. The bread they serve at the start of the meal was average but the olive oil with cracked pepper on the side was pretty exceptional. We decided to split everything. The mâché salad was good, nothing spectacular but the cheese cubes definitely made it. The linguine cacio y pepe as a first course was outstanding!! The right amount of pepper and cheese made this a winner. We decided to split the beef and pork over polenta and I'll have to say this was one of the better dishes I've had in awhile. Chunks of pork and beef, marinated in some sort of spicy sauce over a bed of creamy polenta? Yes please. This dish definitely had a kick to it, loaded with flavor and the meat was very lean. We decided to go with a glass of wine each instead of a bottle so we went with the super Tuscan. For $17 a glass I found it to be marginal at best. My date wanted a bit of a closer so we had the flourless chocolate cake with a scoop of gelato, very good. The entire experience was memorable for the service, the atmosphere and the food. The wine? Meh...it's definitely a locals place that I would revisit.

Such a lovely experience. It is tough to get a table reservation, but you can just walk in and try to snag a seat at the bar. Perfect place for two friends to grab a nice dinner. Intimate, but not in a specifically romantic way.

Ambience was fantastic. I would describe ambience at the bar as similar to going to a small high end sushi place, but Italian.

Service was very good. Our waiter was very knowledgable about the menu and the wine list. 

Food was very good, especially for the price. The tagliatelle and fried artichokes were absolutely spectacular. The pepper spaghetti was raved about by others, but I found it rather ordinary. Our entree (I can't remember the name) was some kind of braised beef cubes over polenta- although tasty, it was dry and far below what I was expecting for the place. Had that been better, I would have given this place a five.

I think this place is a great value and will definitely be back.

run, don't walk! great food, great service! wonderful ambiance. sit at the bar if you can, better service and more fun! all around one my favorite nyc restaurants...have been going for years and am so lucky to live nearby. ALWAYS look forward to going and never feel bad about spending a lot of money. WONDERFUL!

This is it. This is the small, amazing, delicious, romantic restaurant in the village. Everyone in the restaurant was smiling. The lighting makes everyone look great. The food is savory and thoughtful, the wait staff, at least for my meal, was fun, clever and smart. The drinks were deeeeelicious (Negroni, the drink of the house it seems) and the dessert? As if it couldn't get any better. I had the best time here with my bestie gal pal and we left bozzy happy and completely satiated of pallet. If only I were dating someone, this would be where we'd either fall in love or know it was over. It's that good. All of it.

I basically have the pickiest eaters on the planet as parents (as in my mother couldn't find *anything* to eat on the menu at the tap room at Gramercy Tavern), and they loved their meals at I Sodi.  

Great selection of pastas & entrees.  Salads are also quite good.  

Staff is friendly.  Killer negroni.  Extensive wine list.  Good ambience.

Amazing meal and ambiance all around. Wait staff was a bit stuffy but very professional.

Quality tastes in the anti, we found that the order for one was more than enough for two, even three people. 

The real star of the night was the cacio e pepe! We'll be back just for that. Ravioli was also wonderful, just the right ratio of dough to filling :) 
We drank a 2011 gaglioppo and couldn't have been more pleased.

Best Italian Food I've ever had.   

Me and my girlfriend read about I Sodi and about how they prepare their food.  Imported Olive Oil from the owner's hometown, hand choppede veggies for their tomato sauce etc and we made reservations right away for that Friday.

I would not normally write about how good the bread was, but there's a first time for everything.  Our waitress brought out a bowl of warm fresh bread and olive oil and it was honestly delicious.  The olive oil had a delicious flavor like no other olive oil I've had.  It was amazing.  For a few minutes I considered just filling up on the bread, and I probably wouldn't have felt too bad about it.

Our appetizer was off the special's menu - Chicken liver on toast.  That was amazing too, a great flavor, just the right amount chicken liver andt he toast had a great subtle flavor was toasted just right

For dinner I got the Lasagna.  I've never had pasta that actually melted in my mouth.  It was soft but also fluffy.  The spiced beef combined with tomato sauce was perfect.  

I Sodi was so good it actually redefined by taste in Italian food.  A week ago, any other italian meal not from I Sodi, that I would have given an 9/10, I would now give a 6/10.

My one gripe was the dessert.  It was a pretty standard overly sweet chocolate cake.  Not particularly good, but not enough wrong with it to not give this restaurant a 5/5.  I'd give it a 4.5/5 if I could!

I'm a big pasta/Italian fan and I read so much good reviews about here, but honestly, the meal was just ok, nothing special about it. I've been to Firenze many times,  had so much great pasta there, but compare to that, I sodi is below average...even the cocktail wasn't great ....sorry, but never come back. Service was good though.

Had a nice meal here.

Very nice gnocchi pomodori. Very fresh ingredients.

On the small side but the bar was comfortable.
Really nice meal. Nice atmosphere in lovely part of city. I had cacio and pepe and was stuffed afterwards. Platter at start for 2 ppl was also huge and quality

My friend and I ordered three kinds of pasta but none of them impressed us. Two of the pastas (the pesto and sorry for forgetting the other one) tasted pretty much the same... we barely finished them. 

Besides, I understand the owner attempts to make the place low-key as the bottom part of the windows are blurry, but they made me feel isolated like I am engaged in sort of secretive activity...

Btw, the waiter served us had some breath issue... which a bit ruined our night. (Should we have told him!?)

Really a perfect meal! No complaints & we had a bit of everything. Will make sure to stop in next time I'm visiting which says a lot - there are so many places to choose from! But this was a place I've thought about a few times... Definitely memorable.

i loved this restaurant. i live right next to it but for no good reason, i always overlooked it. we finally ate here on Saturday night, and i must say that after il mulino, it was probably the best italian meal i've had in NYC. here's what we had: 

radicchio with pecorino and balsamic vinegar- simple and elegant and in every way an italian appetizer. \
Valeriana - the same
Rigatoni Strascicati - absolutely marvelous bolognese
Spaghetti with black pepper and pecorino- again, marvelous
beans- a simple side that tasted great
vanilla espresso drowned in gelato- dido

our server wasn't annoying and was very timely and helpful. i couldn't think higher of this little nook. i'll be back in the very near future to have the special rib-eye that they serve as a special on weekends.

Four of us had a lovely evening here in early April - on a Saturday night in the West Village . . . service was attentive, the food was great, wines were excellent . . . and we never felt neglected or rushed which can happen on busy evenings.  Three of us had the cece e pepi, one had the steak.  And we shared the fried artichokes.  All delicious!  Who doesn't like great Tuscan food, well prepared?

I've held off a few weeks to post this review.   Possibly because I have been waiting for the food from I Sodi to pass from my system.  To begin,  I was excited to dine at I Sodi after reviewing recommendations on Yelp.  Never before have Yelp reviews been more off base. 

I've read the history of I Sodi and understand that the owner is replicating her mother's food in this restaurant.   I've read that her mother may also be cooking in the kitchen at I Sodi.  My thought after dining here is that some family traditions are better off left buried.   Never before have I or my dining partners experienced simple food prepared so offensively.  From bread to pasta to anything simple to prepare this was hands down the most dreadful excuse for cuisine we've ever experienced.   If the mother of I Sodi were to prepare CHEF BOY R DEE FROM A CAN -- these family recipes would have been better than what we were served.

The"homemade bread" that our snobbish waitress described to us as "freshly baked today" was hard and devoid of any moisture.  There was no alternative from this dried bread (think stale) for people who really could not eat this giant dried crouton? Really?  Something so simple that the waitress ącts so snobbish to defend without offering an alternative? We cannot be the first people who have let them know this bread was inedible.  The waitress had her "premeditated" excuse at hand to defend this travesty to wheat.  The waitress described this bread as traditional tuscan style.   I've been to tuscany and no where in the region did restaurants serve bread this stale to customers (perhaps they served it to the sewer rats).  Again,  if this is the mother's recipe,  I'd be embarrassed.  The best thing about the bread was the cured meat antipasti we ordered with it  -- which is simply bought and put together from a butcher shop - we thanked good it wasn't mom's recipe. 

On to our two different pastas - both which had the consistency of paste. HORRIBLE! We dared not dine further and order another painful course after having our senses so assaulted by the first two courses.  Bring us the check please snobby waitress. 

The best part of my dinner came from the bar - the negroni was very good.   I guess the mother's homemade recipes didn't extend to the bartender -- thank goodness!

Make merriment. Dine.  Enjoy.. But not at I so suck.. Wait, I mean i soda or whatever.... . Brian

Supremely delicious Italian. The lasagna was outstanding! Every bite here was worth it. 
The space is snug, but comfortable and the bar is beautifully set up as the focal point of the restaurant. 
An excellent dining experience that I would replicate immediately.

I was impressed with good service at this restaurant and 2 kind of wines I had were excellent.
Why am I giving only 3 stars?
Almost all dishes I had here were simply too salty.  Maybe I should give another try.

After having this place on my list for years, I did it, a Saturday night reservation.  Even with the 10pm reservation, we were left waiting another fifteen minutes or so, so definitely don't expect a quick in and out meal even with a reservation.  Get the cacio e pepe here, might be the best I've ever had.  I don't even remember what else we got but that doesn't matter since you come here for that one dish...

And yes, total date spot, do it.

Rainy spring night. Live in the neighborhood and finally had dinner here tonight.    We tried the antipasto,  arugula salad, spegh  cache y pepe , and meat lasagna .  We sat at the bar....really nice ambiance. Nice bartender/server. Fantastic  pasta...Great for a   really cold night.

The best- and I mean the BEST- Italian food in the city.  Plan ahead- make a reservation or choose to eat at an off hour.  You will not regret this.  The pasta with black pepper is to die for.  And there is a cabbage and cheese salad that will make you lick the plate.  I cannot rave about this place enough.  Just too excellent for words

We've been away from I Sodi much too long and must return soon...best Negroni's anywhere, including Italy...portions are large so my wife and I shared small portion of spaghettini verdi (favre beans), a half portion of risotto cime di rapa, a side of of verdure (beats & carrots) and topped it off with a delicious Affogato.  The classico Chianti was a perfect choice to accompany the meal.  The place has a charming atmosphere with great service and you can have a conversation!!!  Rita Sodi is a hands-on owner and makes this restaurant a wonderful dining experience even on a Saturday night.

Nice little cozy place. Don't come here without knowing you'll be spending a bit more than usual, but do so knowing you'll get some good, well prepared food.  The service is excellent, and there's not a bit of lacking quality at this place.  While you could find good food around a lot of different places, i Sodi is worth trying once!
This is one of the best restaurants we've been to. The arugula salad and the branzino special was perfect. We'll be back for sure!

I Sodi is the kind of neighborhood place that you wish there were more of in Manhattan.  Simply prepared Italian food done exquisitely well in a small, relaxed setting with phenomenal service.  The pastas in particular are great, especially the lasagna, and we also tried a few of the Negronis, all of which were excellent and uniquely prepared.  When you want to avoid "the scene" and have an excellent, quiet meal, this place should be high on your list.
This place is a cute, local gem.  Great italian staples, prepared to perfection.

Excellent service at very cozy restaurant. Almost everything was way too salty. I tried to eat the delicious rabbit but it was overly salty. It was served with over cooked salty spinach. The chef did not agree that it was too salty but the waiter handled the situation perfectly. Great drinks, excellent but salty fried artichokes and lovely mozzarella tomato salad.

KenScale: 8.0/10

I Sodi is an Italian restaurant from Rita Soti displaying various dishes from Tuscany reflecting her childhood there. It is one of the more charming neighborhood restaurants in West Village, with a tiny dining room and intimate atmosphere serving solid rustic Italian dishes. 

Heirloom tomato salad with cucumber, onion and basil was a light dish with very fresh tomato that got the meal started on the right path. The restaurant offers pasta dishes in both half and full portions. I ordered two dishes in half portions (which were actually fairly generous for half portions). I liked the rustic feel of both spaghetti vongole (with tasty clams) and rigatoni in meat sauce. Nothing mind-blowing, but well-executed dishes that you can probably see in Italian-style home cooking. I was a bit underwhelemd with whole branzino roasted with cherry tomato. It was cooked right with very good balance of flavor, but somehow the texture felt a little mushy. For dessert, the Italian classic vanilla panna cotta (which I also ordered with blueberry sorbet) was solid, although I've had better panna cotta elsewhere.

The restaurant's dining room is very small, which means it is important to get a reservation early (I was lucky that the restaurant had a last minute cancelation). The restaurant has a full bar with plenty of Italian wine selections, so definitely try a sip or two. I was charmed by the vibe of the restaurant, which is that perfect neighbhorhood spot you want to have near your home. For a casual dinner or date night, I recommend I Sodi as an option to consider.

Simply my favorite Italian restaurant in NYC for date night. A great dining experience enhanced by fantastic service. 

Pros:
1) Lasagna 
2) Service
3) Cocktails

Cons:
1) Pricy Wine List
2) Somewhat Cramped 

Experience:
We had an 8:30 reservation, but due to the standard Saturday evening delay on the subway we were running a good 15 minutes late.  In fear of losing our table, we called the restaurant and let them know we were running late and they held our table for us.  A simple and surprisingly unusual nice act.  We were greeted by name by the host, another nice touch.

The bartender served up the best Manhattan I have had in quite some time, and was reasonably priced.  The wine list was comprised exclusively of Italian wines, which unfortunately I have about as much knowledge about as the local political events occurring in Fresno.  The least expensive wine on the list was approximately $70, and by the glass prices were $15, but did feature a nice Chianti.  

The majority of the entrees are served in either full or half orders.  We ordered the ravioli and the lasagna, which only comes in a full order.  The lasagna is quite simply amazing.  If Garfield was ever sent to death row for offing Odie, this is exactly what he would want as his last meal.  It features 12 layers of delectate  pasta, with a delicious meat sauce and adorned by the perfect amount of cheese. It was well constructed and stable, unlike a track-home in Orange County.

The service throughout the evening was fantastic, exactly what you would expect from a high-end dining establishment.  The server spoke perfect English, was courteous, knowledgeable about the menu and preparation, gave good recommendations, and was very attentive.  Our first order of drinks took a little time to deliver, but I am pretty sure that is because the Manhattan was prepared in Heaven.  

The setting is very classy and NYC "intimate," so be prepared to learn about everything that is happening in the life of the couple sitting next to you.  Not a major negative, unless the wife is suspicious about her husband's recent trip to Atlantic City to invest in a new casino.

The price point was very reasonable and portion size is exactly where you won't be craving a slice on the way home but also don't feel like a beached whale being covered in wet towels.  

Overall, I would highly recommend I Sodi to a couple looking for a date night experience.

This place was fantastic. I found it through my yelp search looking for great cacio e pepe. My friend and I ended up eating at the bar, the waiter was incredibly attentive and helpful, thought the service was awesome. 

We started with a really simple buffalo mozzarella and tomato salad, really simply done and it was excellent. We also had the fried artichoke, totally fantastic, I could eat it by the bowlful. 

I had the cacio e pepe (not always printed on the menu but available if you ask for it), and my friend had some ravioli. Both were so simple and well done. I was really impressed, I really dig italian restaurants that don't go overboard with the making things complex, this place let the ingredients take the forefront. Really good. 

Definitely will be heading back, I was very impressed.

Pros:  Tasty artichoke salad and good service


Cons:  Small, cramped, very loud, no place to wait for table to become available
           AND WORST OF ALL--food was so heavily salted (rabbit) it was inedible
           Tirami Su was lacking in espresso flavor and "lady finger" texture
           Espresso had no "crema" on top

This little cosy restaurant has it all...gr8 food, good service and a cosy atmosphere. For starter we had a big plate of sausages and cheese. Yummy. For main we had lasagna and cacio a Pepe. Both was gr8 but the lasagna was fantastic. It was melting in your mouth. I'm definitely going back next time I'm in New York. Ciao
Love this place, so good!  Eclectic Italian food.  Limited menu.  Just awesome!
Yummy food, great atmosphere, and friendly staff!  What a wonderful experience I had!

Elegant spot with excellent food and service. What could be better than a negroni, lasagna, and side of spinach? It's a very small but warm and familial environment. The waitstaff is extremely attentive and the food is always fresh. Great place to catch up with the people you love, and treat them to an incredible meal.

The food was very good. The service was beyond unacceptable. Sat at the bar. Waitstaff was unresponsive and dismissive. There was a long hair in the food and they took it away without even a quiet apology. Water glasses never refilled until the check came. Will not be coming back. There are other places that have good Italian in the city.

My absolute favorite modern Italian restaurant in nyc, and I've been to del posto. Don't get me wrong, I don't think it's necessarily better than del posto in good quality but for the price and the ambience I will take this place any day. The home made pastas are to die for and I can't recommended the carmalized onion spaghetti enough.

authentic tuscan restaurant. it's intimate, reservations are almost always required, but if you're lucky they'll seat you at the bar.  i've definitely seen a few celebs eat here, which is a fun element.  but the food speaks for itself, simple, elegant, sophisticated.  it's unpretentious Italian cooking at it's finest.  homemade pasta and the works, satisfying deserts.  romantic date kind of place.
The lasagna will change your life and the cacio e pepe is luscious comfort food on the next level. Third time here and always charmed.

I thought every dish was really great, but the pasta portion sizes are laughable, especially since they are divided into half and full sizes. So when we ordered full sizes, we were like, "Har har, where's the other half." We were met with the unamused stare of our server, who looked like Anne Hathaway, except not. 

We ordered the rabbit and steak mains and both were to die for, as in, "whoa I would really go back for either of these dishes," and the pastas were great as well - there was a tagliatelle and a chestnut ravioli, which was surprisingly tasty, despite the main ingredients being "chestnuts." Their wine list is a bit pricey as other diners have mentioned, but the space is beautiful and the service expert (despite the not-quite-and-slightly-huffy Anne Hathaway doppelganger), and the food...very much worth the money though seriously, the chef could do worse than throw in a few more noodles and raviolis. 

I'd go back! Oh and highly recommended for an intimate date you would like to entertain.

I've eaten at I Sodi twice and have had excellent meals both times. I Sodi is TINY, with only 8 tables or so and a bar. It's a bit cramped, but the food and service are excellent so you won't mind. Some highlights:

Lasagna - Ridiculously good. Pricey for West VIllage Italian, but you definitely get what you pay for on this one.

Antipasto - Really nice portion size of quality meats and cheeses.

Artichokes - Great as an app or a side.

Service - The staff is great and super friendly. That, plus the small size, really makes I Sodi an intimate/special dining experience.

I liked the feeling of the room albeit quite small. The food was delicious however at the end, I had the feeling the bill was NOT commiserate with the quality/service aspects of this place. The service was very unimpressive considering the prices. Delicious but probably would not go back. In the end not that special and not that worth it .

Terrible service experience. My party arrived a little before our 7pm reservation and were told to wait at the bar...then the restaurant filled up. When we finally got a hold of the waiter he told us that they over booked. When we asked why other parties who arrived after us were seated first, he stated that since they spend a lot of money with the restaurant he wanted to seat them first. Didn't realize the service was going to be so terrible before we ordered our bottle of wine...so we drank that and eventually sat an hour and a half later. Couldn't even comp the bottle of wine we bought. Not going back here. 

Food was fine.

Outstanding n Great Value

Love this place.  Great portions of Tuscan style Italian at a very reasonable price, with a ton of charm.  You have to try the lasagne - paper thin pasta and a lot of flavor.  Regular pasta dishes were great too!  Too bad we were too stuffed to try desert - NEXT TIME!  Small quite place perfect for casual dinner or a special date, won't break the bank either.

They over 1/2 n full portions. 1/2 is an appetizer portion, full is not huge but plenty for one.  If you want gluttonous go to Olive Garden.

Went in to try their version of a negroni, one of my favorite cocktails. The bartender didn't know anything about the various types of vermouth they stocked, or he wouldn't engage in a conversation about them. I tried the negroni classico, top on their drink menu. It was awful. No complexity at all. I only finished it because it cost $14. Customer service wasn't good either. The bartender didn't check back, not even after I finished the drink to see if we wanted anything else. We weren't offered a food menu. I won't be back.

So happy I stumbled into this little place. it's absolutely adorable and the food is to die for. They also have a fully stocked bar with a gentleman who looks every part a good mixologist so you'd be a fool not to order a cocktail and let him work his magic. 
For dinner, I had the heirloom tomato salad (amazeballs) followed by the meat lasagne (another level). You also get a complimentary basket of fresh bread to start so by the end of my two cocktails and food I was feeling pretty great. Would be perfect spot for a date or to host an intimate or special family occasions.

Stick with the appetizers and the pasta dishes, which rock traditional al dente Italian style.  The wine list is good and not exorbitant - we asked for one of the labels and bought it at home.  The waiter offered thoughtful suggestions.
Recommended by Paul at Uncorked Wine. Amazing food!!!!  Probably the best northern Italian food we have eaten in the city!
Dinner at the bar with a bestie - can't be beat. Share lots of different things. Best way to taste the high quality and fresh fare.

Wow!  What a great Italian experience!  I'm not talking about a get you in and get you out "Olive Garden" kind of experience.  This place is top notch food, booze and wait staff experience. From the appetizers to the desert and everything in between it was great. The wait staff cannot be outdone. Their attention to detail to make your dinner the best it can be is so appreciated.  You'll have to ask for the check - so appreciated. The main courses were amazing. I had the Coniglio In Porchetta and it was very well prepared. The drinks and desert were amazing as well. Plan on making reservations to make sure you start off well. Although the the bar makes waiting easier. Will come again when we're down from Btown.
Great food, all freshly prepared in-house authentic Italian. The penacotta is a must have

Lasagna lasagna lasagna. One of the best in the City, and the best I've ever had! I've never been able to count the layers! Charming, crowded, fun, and the staff are always great. Our fave place to eat in this neighborhood, great if you're heading to the Lortel or the New Ohio.

Went here tonight with a few business colleagues.  I have to say I haven't had a more disappointing meal in a very long time.  The place was packed, which tells me there are a lot of locals that chose location over meal quality.

If you're in the area, don't believe the hype and go somewhere else..

Went down to the village for a play and decided to try this restaurant hoping to get a great meal. Upon walking into the bar my nostrils immediately picked up the stench of the pretentious staff. The service was slow and very forceful in trying to up sell their menu. The food was pretty decent but absolutely not worth price for the very small portions. The one positive I can say is that they were generous on their bread basket which makes up for the lack of actual food in their portions. It's the village find somewhere else to eat for future diners.

I was not impressed by the food or the prices. Way too expensive for just mediocre Italian dishes. The service was ok, although I didn't understand any of the specials (our server was in a rush) which didn't make us feel welcome at all. Overall was definitely disappointed with our meal and experience. If you're looking for a friendly, warm Italian atmosphere with appropriately priced food, don't come here.

Nice atmosphere and attentive waitstaff. Menu and food were fine, but nothing extraordinary. Cacio had a little too much pepe. Branzino was poorly deboned, especially since it wasn't actually served as the whole fish. Lasagna was tasty. There's definitely far superior Italian in the neighborhood, but I wouldn't be opposed to returning.

Best. Pasta. Ever. 

Do not concern yourselves with the petty squabbles mentioned in other reviews over wait times or "service inconsistencies". We had the most glorious dinner; albeit slightly late seating but no problem. This was the best pasta we've ever consumed. Gorgeous starters. Beautiful wine and drinks. Service was perfect - thanks Eric! Felt like we'd somehow miraculously landed in Italy. Certainly will return.

I love this place and the food is great, but we had a very frustrating experience tonight. We arrived at about 9:30 and were told the wait was about 10 minutes. They didn't take our name - told us they'd recognize us and just to wait outside. Then after about a half hour wait, another couple was given a table ahead of us, even though they arrived after us and did not have a reservation. When there's a wait, restaurants need to respect the customers that are willing to wait it out. Letting someone cut in line is so disrespectful of both the customer and the restaurant staff. Unbelievable and incredibly frustrating.

Lasagne al carciofi--actually anything with artichoke (fritti? yes!) on their menu or as a special--is delicious, as is their pasta in general. Great negronis, a solid selection of wines by the glass. Just knowing that I can slide the door open and take a seat at the bar with the expectation of a great impromptu meal makes NYC a better place. Expect a wait and a little bit of human contact at prime times--it's not Olive Garden.

I've been to I Sodi many times and I've always thought both the food and service were exceptional. However, last night was a completely different story. 

I was initially getting drinks with my girlfriend but she had to leave after an hour so I decided to stay and order a main course. It hadn't been more than two minutes after she left when a waiter by the name of Eric came over to me and said, "This is a bit awkward to ask but I will be needing these two seats (the one I was sitting on and the empty one my friend left behind). I will be happy to buy you a cocktail for the inconvenience." I was surprised he'd ask me this given that I was getting ready to order food. I even explained this to him but he completely disregarded what I was saying and continued to say he'd buy me a cocktail if I'd just let him take my seat. The story goes on and eventually I gave up my seat to the customers coming in to dine. I left feeling completely offended and totally embarrassed. 

I've never experienced anything like this at a restaurant before. Not only was it unprofessional but it was totally disrespectful.

Regardless of how great the food might be, Experience is what you always remember and I Sodi failed to deliver.
Check out the full review from Caleb Tripp and me on our food blog : http://wp.me/p6Xylz-4V

What a disappointment. I confirmed at noon the day of my reservation. I got a call from Eric 45 minutes before we were due at the restaurant and he told me they didn't have a phone number attached to my reservation so they couldn't call me the day before to confirm. There's something that doesn't add up here -- they had my voicemail for almost 7 hours yet they gave my table away. Looks like someone didn't bother to check the voicemails and didn't have the balls to admit it. So, because of his oversight, we had the "opportunity" to sit at the bar getting jostled by hangry Friday night crowds -- on a special birthday night. No thank you. We walked into Il Buco Alimentari and had a great night. What a difference a competent staff makes.

We had 5:30 dinner reservations, were seated promptly.   Reservations aren't accepted at the bar so that area was immediately packed.   Tables are about 8 inches apart -- that's pretty typical for restaurants in the Village.   It's as quiet/loud as the crowd.

Service was pretty good, our salads came about 15 minutes after being ordered, 45 minutes from ordering the pasta arrived.   Dirty dishes sat for awhile, waiter was pleasant but kept very busy.

Food was ok.  I had the arugula and cheese salad which was dry/bland, my husband had a cabbage and walnut salad which was the best course we had.  The 2 pasta dishes were nothing special, a spaghetti with pepper and cheese and a pasta dish with asparagus.   Bread was ok.

Restaurant is ok but it's unclear why there's so much hype.

Don't waste your time eating here.  The food may be good but the staff (Eric) is totally incompetent.  And with an attitude, no less - like it's your fault that no one checked the restaurant's voicemail telling them to add one person extra to an already standing reservation for five people.  Which, by the way, they can't (or won't) do - because there is no such thing as a table for 6.  Gee - is that because there should only be an odd number of people at a table?   Answer your voice messages on time, dear restaurant.

Such wonderful food and cocktails and wine! Tonight my husband and I ordered their lamb loin special and sides of heirloom carrots and fried potatoes. This, after two fennel and radicchio salads. Our waiter let us know that sharing one main would be plenty, thus reducing our bill quite a bit and he was right on...we had plenty of food for the two of us. We always get the Hendrick's gin sage martini and their wine selection is awesome; we always let our waiter choose for us. We eat at the bar; reservations are a 3 month wait for a Saturday evening bit arriving when they open at 5:30, you can be seated at the bar right away.

Let's start by saying this place is hard to get a reservation at.  It's on the small side and the food is excellent, so that is why.  So, we had to do the early bird res at 5:30, which was still ok.  The overall experience was the best.  Our waiter was very informative and attentive.  He helped guide us with app's, entrees and wine selections.  

We started with the nightly app special of pan fried artichoke, which was amazing.  Then my wife ordered the Ravioli Burro E Salvia, and I had the Lasagne A Sugo.  Both pastas were made from scratch and you could tell.  The lasagne must have been 15 layers of thin pasta, cheese and meat.  It was amazing.  The meal was complimented by a nice bottle of Chianti that our server helped us choose. 

We will definitely be back, but next time I'll make the res with more notice so we can dine at a more appropriate time.  Overall five stars *****

Food 3 stars, service 3 stars, ambiance/decor 4 stars

We were able to get a table for 4. (Bar seats are saved for walk ins). I was about to sit down and slide in on the side of the sofa. Not sure if the waiter was new and didn't know what to do, but the table leg was covered by the table cloth and when I tried to slide in I immediately hit my leg! Ouch! He should have helped us pull out the table so we could get in and then push the table in, but instead he just stood there watching us pull out the table so we could get in. Then another waiter came by to help us push the table in. Okay whatever, I didn't go to this restaurant for the service. 

Now food! Totally underwhelming and didn't live up to the hype. The fried artichokes were great and the strawberry tiramisu was fingerlickin' good! However, everything else was a miss. Their famous cacio pepe was okay, spaghetti pomodoro was also okay, and we also got the rabbit and fried chicken. Both also just okay. Nothing made me want to come back to the restaurant again except the strawberry tiramisu.

After reading the NYT review and making a reservation several weeks ago, we arrived tonight really excited for our meal.  Upon arrival, the host told us that our reservation was cancelled because they tried to reach us several times via phone, including leaving voicemails and via text.  We did not receive any missed calls, voicemails or texts prior to our reservation.

The host was incredibly rude and loudly claimed that seating us now would delay other reservations, so we decided to leave.  Have never experienced worst service in my lifetime of living in NYC.  We will not be going back.
My Numero Uno in NYC....do i eat here every second week...?

Big Disappointment.  Had read the great Times review but really
inferior food and rushed service.  While hardly halfway through with
a completely ordinary salad appetizer they brought  our entrees.
Mine was lasagna, which as my wife said, looked like it was made
a few days ago - many paper-thin leaves of dough -  but tasteless.
They rushed us so that after about an hour we left and had dessert
elsewhere.  Perhaps the disappointing food and rushed and rude
service is due to too much success that they are not ready to handle.
Too bad because we heard it once was really good.  No more,

This is a great restaurant on many different levels.  It has that homey, neighborhood restaurant feel with really great service, and expertly prepared Tuscan food (with some dishes from the neighboring regions). 

I came in with my fiance on a Saturday night around 7 p.m., and the bartender, Chris I believe his name was, warmly welcomed us and moved some people so we could sit at the bar.  The meal was awesome, and Chris helped us chose the perfect wine with our food. 

A huge standout was the cacio e pepe.  I've been obsessed with this pasta lately.  It's one of those pastas that seems easy to make but can be tricky in its execution.  I Sodi's cacio e pepe is the best I've ever had - the perfect balance of pecorino and black pepper, it's incredibly tasty and satisfying.

I had passed by I Sodi many times but it was always very crowded and I was always en route to doing something else. I had an appointment downtown and made it my business to get there for when they started serving-6P-I got there a little after 6 and the place was already packed. I was able to get a seat at the bar but there were really no other options since I was by myself. I was given a menu, ordered a glass of the house red and got the cacio e pepe. i have not seen it available in Italian restaurants I have eaten at-The last time I passed by I saw they had it on the menu. It was delicious. The bartender was attentive and i met two women sitting next to me [one from South Africa who now lives in Florida and her daughter who was going to be taking a job in Mexico.] It was an exceptional meal [the last time I had cacio e pepe was when I was in Rome] I would recommend and return. If you are eating alone, get there early so you can get a seat at the bar-if not-see if you can make a reservation. [I am not sure if they take them]

A cozy spot for a nice, but simple meal. Rustic ingredients with a minimalist approach to Italian cooking. Elegant, casual, but feels like a tiny space when the restaurant is full. Cacio e pepe is a solid choice, artichoke lasagne is a work of art. Panna cotta texture is good, simply done, no sauces few berries for garnish. Reservations are tough, but they do take walk-ins. Hit or miss wait staff, they are attentive, but not overly friendly. Service was much better years ago, so I no longer come by very often. A solid meal if you're in the neighborhood.

Had about a 20 minute wait to sit at the bar Super cute small neighborhood spot. Great service and very tasty wine and pasta. Chris was our bartender server and made great recommendations. We had the bolognese rigatoni and the pasta pomodoro - very yummy pom sauce. Also had the special burrata appetizer. Perfect size portions - not too much. Bread was a little tough. Would definitely recommend.

Finally making my long overdue review of one of my absolute favorite New York restaurants. Whenever my husband and I become wistful about our love of Italy, Tuscany in particular, we invariably call for a reservation at I Sodi. The food and preparation are about as close as you get to a great meal in say Florence, Cortona, Arezzo...ah, the memories!...without having to get on a jet. The food here is totally authentic and delicious. The service is tops. I think I waited so long to review this place because I want it to be my secret spot. Alas, lots of people already know about how wonderful it is...reservations are essential. Plan ahead! You will not be sorry. It's great!

I went into I Sodi last night for dinner with a friend and was really impressed. The space is very small-- Good for a dinner for 2- I wouldn't do a huge group dinner here. But, the food and service were both fantastic. 

To start we got 2 specials: burrata with cherry tomatoes and zucchini misto- Both were great. For the entree course we got the cacio e pepe and the special artichoke lasagna. The cacio was so good- one of the best preparations I've ever had and the lasagna was great as well. I would happily order both entrees again.

Our waiter was very attentive and knowledgeable -- It is clear that he knows food well and did a great job at helping us order. Overall, I would definitely return- Great Italian spot in the West Vill.

This used to be a wonderful restaurant with incredible service. Tonight, my boyfriend and I, who have been eating here several times a year for at least 4 years, were treated rudely for the staff for the last time. The service has been steadily declining, but we thought: oh well, the food is amazing! But, I Sodi is not a place where people who have shelled out thousands of dollars over several years feel welcome unless they are a celebrity (one walked in tonight) or a friend/family of the owner (a couple and their kid who did not have a reservation - the bald but bearded waiter said so - who were let in before us despite the fact that we had been waiting for an hour). We were disgusted and just left. Never, ever coming back again. It's just the last time, to be honest.

Haven't tasted the food yet, but I'm a solo diner.  There were a couple of tables for 2 available for walkins, but the chef does not want solo diners seated at a table only bar service.  A lot of business travelers, like myself,  are quite put out off by this "discrimination". Narrow-minded and profit oriented of the chef.  Plus, she might be surprised.  A solo diner, treated well, is often an appreciative clinet, not only monetarily but word of mouth.  My word of out will not be so good reason her policy.  Jury out on food. Anyway, it's now been 30 minutes waiting for the bar. Free drink? Doubt the chef condones that either.

We were so excited to try I Sodi after reading the glowing Pete Wells review in the New York Times. It took us three weeks to get a reservation and the entire experience was an utter letdown. The exterior of the restaurant looks like a cheap accountant's office while the interior is a cramped, noisy throwback to the 1970s of our parents generation with overstuffed, uncomfortable tables and backbreaking wooden chairs. There is no host or hostess and no one greeted us for five minutes. After the initial wait we were seated and presented with a wine list featuring one of the highest wine markups we have ever seen in any restaurant. The waiter was smug and unhelpful when we asked for a pasta recommendation. The best he could offer was "the cacciopepe is what pays the rent" and no doubt it does at $17 for a $2 dish. For fried  potatoes expect to pay $14. We also ordered one of the special appetizers described as fresh, fried artichoke hearts we received a plate of shredded, greasy chokes that were inedible. We brought this to our waiters' attention and he just said, "Ok" and did not offer an alternative or offer an apology. The pasta was extreme al dente and tasted like boxed pasta. The dessert we ordered was unremarkable and so frozen that chunks flew off the plate. The total? $200 for two. Now that is a rip-off. Wow!!! Pete Wells you have seriously damaged your credibility. STAY AWAY.

4 stars for food, one star for service.

I took a friend there to celebrate her birthday and decided to try out somewhere new, and ended up here.  At first glance, the restaurant was quaint and I loved the location, and couldn't wait to try the brick baked Cornish hen.

I asked the waiter if he could let me know which dishes were gluten-free, and he got inpatient and annoyed.  I guess rule number one at this place should be no matter how serious your dietary restrictions are, thou shall not pose questions to the all mighty waiter cause sadly, that's when our started to go downhill.

We ordered one of their daily special appetizers, grilled tomato and mozzarella and server brought the wrong appetizer.  I only noticed after my friend had dug in and I questioned why the mozzarella was green, but no biggie.  We informed him, but instead of just correcting the mistake and moving on, he dismissively said we ordered that dish and questioned me twice when I informed him that it was the wrong dish, we specifically ordered mozzarella.  

From there on, service was abysmal.  No water refills, no checking up on us, nothing.  And I mention on the reservation this was to celebrate a birthday and was really hoping the restaurant would help make it special too.  Sigh.  Thank goodness at least I got her flowers and she was a good sport - being treated like this at my birthday meal would've made me quite sad!

After being ignored long enough, we decided to skip on dessert and just get the check, and finally  got the check dropped off at our table with the help of a friendly busser.  I saw the dish we didn't order on the bill and when the waiter came to pick up the check, asked him about it - at which point, he pointed me to the deduction and kindly reminded dish that the wrong dish was "complimentary", dismissively as if he was doing us a huge favor.  Ummmm... for a dish that we didn't eat and was mistakenly put on our table (yes, he took the dish back), and it really left our dinner unpleasant and quite awkward, how is that considered "complimentary"? (Obviously, it couldn't be our all mighty waiter's own mistake... )

The food was decent, but you can get decent food at much better value and not be treated like you owe the place a big favor by dining there.  Did I mention they also ran out of hand towels at the bathroom?  

Hungry cat would rather stay hungry than come back.  Not celiac/gluten-free friendly (they do have the Cornish hen and dishes that might be friendly, but you're not going to get any sort of confirmation and reassurance from the waiter and I'm not sure I'm comfortable with his knowledge to recommend trying), and definitely two paws down.

This is becoming a favorite spot! 

The pepper pasta is literally one of the best I've had anywhere in the world.

Sitting at the bar is great - recommend it.

The antipasto plate has great meats and cheeses - the small is enough for two people.

The lasagna is excellent.

The only negative thing I'd say is that it's super hard to get a table, and they don't answer the phone for reservations - need to do it online.

Consistently simple delicious food. But extraordinarily rude, unacceptable service without grace or manners. I've been a regular for years and it wax my favorite restaurant in NYC, but I will not go back after this evening's experience. Stay away. There are plenty of excellent restaurants in NYC that understand hospitality and have regard for their customers and not just their money. Rita, you are not well represented in your dining room. Let us know when you've returned to great food and hospitality.

Excellent food in a graceful, relaxed setting.

Drinks:  we started with selections from their Negroni-centric cocktail list, and I have to say, my Nergroni bianco was perfect.  I've had that drink elsewhere, and mix it for myself at home, but I Sodi's rendition was the best I've tasted.  

Starters:  three of us shared the antipasto 'for one', and the zucchini carpaccio.  The antipasto was huge:  five different cured meats, three cheeses, plus some accompanying sauces.  The meats and cheeses were all very tasty, and the 'for one' portion was easily enough for three.
 
The zucchini carpaccio was really good, definitely something I'd order again.  Thin slices of super-fresh green and yellow zucchini, topped with fruity olive oil, fresh herbs, and thinly sliced sharp cheese.  Simple, yet very flavorful and fresh.  

Pastas:  we tried the olio et aglio, the lasagna, and the ricotta and spinach and ravioli, and of those, the olio et aglio was the clear favorite.  Like the zucchini carpaccio above, this was a simple dish that packed a ton of flavor:  fresh pasta with great texture, sauced with olive oil, garlic, hot red pepper and cheese.  Just outstanding, the favorite of everyone at the table.  

In comparison, the spinach and ricotta ravioli were good, but not outstanding, and the lasagna was actually a bit disappointing.  It featured lots of thin layers of that great, perfectly-textured pasta (so far so good), but beyond that, just a simple meat sauce.  No cheeses of any kind, no larger pieces of meat, etc.  Perhaps this is authentic Tuscan-style lasagna, perhaps I'm more used to a different regional style, but for me this took the simplicity concept too far.  

Mains:  the rabbit loin and the beef cutlet were fantastic!  The rabbit featured moist, tender, well-seasoned loin wrapped in crispy porchetta.  The contrast of textures was great, and every bite was delicious.  The beef cutlet had a nicely crispy exterior, and was also delicious.

Desserts & coffee:  the orange preserve tart and the hazelnut semifreddo were decent, the macchiatos were perfect.

Setting:  this is a small, elegant, comfortable place.  Even when full it doesn't get too loud, so would be good for an intimate occasion.

Service:  as the evening began, service was friendly and gracious, and our server provided helpful suggestions.  However, as the place filled & got busier, he was less available, and after about 2 1/4 hours, he informed us that the next party had arrived early, and asked if we would wrap things up.  I understand it's a small place with multiple seatings, but still:  for the number of courses we ordered, 2 1/4 hours was not an unreasonable amount of time to be seated, and we were only just finishing dessert, with not a moment to linger.  A bit of a curt, unfriendly ending to an otherwise fine meal.

Usually good, but when it's not, it's awful. 
Had a horrible dinner this week, over salted main courses. When mentioned to the waiter, he commented that he had heard this from other diners, but they charged me for an uneaten dinner anyway.  I called the next day to discuss, and did not get a call back.  Obviously they do not care about their customers.

Ambiance lovely and not too noisy. Appetizers mostly excellent - beef tartar, fried artichokes. Brüssel sprouts terrible - not crispy, bland w melted cheese which added no flavor or interest to the dish. Pasta was excellent. Cornish Hen was almost inedible because of saltiness. When we complained the host actually told us that no salt was added. He then offered that it had been BRINED! Well there ya go. Chicken was properly cooked but the tenderness of the hen not front and center. Bacon wrapped rabbit also suffered from tooooo much salt. Maybe the chef should re-consider her approach to these two "star" dishes. Maybe peeps under thirty need the extra salt from all their extreme sports!

This place is exceptional. You can taste the high level of all ingredients used in their dishes. The food is simple in design yet extraordinary in taste. Staff are well informed about the menu. If I had one negative comment, it would be the waiting area, since you are not permitted to stand at the bar. If you arrive early or your table isn't ready, you're forced to stand in the entryway by the door which is awkward. I've been here twice so far with plans to go back on a regular basis - I just won't get there too early as to avoid waiting in no-mans-land :-)

The pasta is great here. The beef tartare is a must. And above all - I know this sounds weird - but their bread is off the charts. The star of the show is the olive oil they serve it with, which is the best olive oil I have ever had. I wish I could come here and just eat the bread basket, that's how good it is. It is a little cramped, but the atmosphere is pretty nice otherwise. Happy eating.
Waiter bald and has a beard pushed me out to wait until he was ready to "seat" me. Very very rude
Whatever it takes, get the damn onion pasta. and book your future reservation while you're enjoying your meal.

Overall: Must go

Occasion: relaxed dinner w a friend or date w significant other - this place is small and the feel is intimate so maybe don't go here if you're not sure how it's gonna go haha
Fun fact: in my opinion this place, along with Mamo, makes the best Negroni in town
Dress code/vibe: casual but nice leave the athleisure at home

1) Drinks:
* You already know ;). I live close by and honestly get frequently even in the wintertime. I like it that much.
* The servers usually have great recommendations for the wines (if you like it there's a wine store a bit further down the street that sells a few of the wines available in the restaurants in the neighborhood so you can take one home)

2) Food:
* Lasagna - good, homey
* Tortelli di castagno - get this, it's incredibly good
*Disclosure: I go to this place when I'm craving  pasta and the dishes are very substantial so I am always too full to get something afterwards

Such a lovely, cozy place with excellent Italian food. Be prepared either to wait or make a reservation in advance. We were lucky to grab last two seats at the bar- still cozy and very comfortable to sit. Great selection of not only wine and cocktails but grappa lovers would not be disappointed! And food!! Oh mai! From different delicious salads for starters to variety of homemade pastas and great Secondi dishes. You should go yourself and check it out. I would definitely come back to them. And waiter staff is very polite, attentive and knowledgeable (and looking very cool).

Went to this place with high expectations of well executed & creative Italian comfort food. 
and. that didn't happen 

The food WAS good, it just wasn't the hype i expected from a restaurant that has minimal reservations available weeks out. I mean, the cacio e pepe (which is the most brilliant pasta dish created out of Italy) was just ok. It was droopy and heavy, no life to it. 

the wine menu though is very good. so at the very least, you'll have a nice boozy time

It was not the first time I was going there, and I had always liked it very much. I always order the cacio e pepe pasta. Yesterday the dish was extremely salty. I pointed it out to a waiter, who told me, without checking it, that that is the way they prepare it, and that if I didn't like it, they could prepare something else for me. I insisted: this is the pasta I want, it's just too salty. But he also insisted: I should order something else.
I just found it very unpleasant and patronizing.

Fine, but certainly doesn't live up to the hype that surrounds it (which will likely be bolstered by a new Infatuation review).  

You've read / heard about the negronis; yes, they're good as advertised.

You've read / heard about the pasta; the lasagna and caccio e pepe were both very good.

There's a reason you haven't read much about anything else; the grilled whole fish branzino entree ($39) was dry, the crispy artichokes were good, but overpriced ($16 for a side), and they slip in a $1 charge per person for bread, which boggles the mind.  They can't hide that dollar somewhere else?  

Three stars because the pasta and drinks were good, but this place is absolutely not worthy of the month-in-advance-reservation dance.

After reading about this place on Grubstreet as being the best Italian restaurant in NYC, I had to give it a shot. Definitely lived up to the billing and accurately more so due to the neighborhood vibe, and simple but well executed dishes versus over the top food like a Carbone. 

We got the shaved asparagus salad, Cacio e Pepe and the Pacheri with a side of spinach. All were great but have to say the Cacio e Pepe was the best.   

All in all a great meal and will definitely be back.

Great food, terrible service. Eric the host gave away our table after we called to say we we running late and then told us "our relationship was over". Will not return unless customer service becomes a thing there.

I made the reservation prior to GrubStreet proclaiming it was the best Italian in NYC. Quite an honor for a restaurant that's not the best in NYC. Don't get me wrong, it was yummy with a cozy atmosphere and fresh pasta. But not hype-worthy. And certainly not reservation-a-month-in-advance worthy. 

Also they have a lot of veggie options. I liked it, but some people want da meat, so thought I'd put that in here.

Apps and Pastas were good, but entrees were only so-so.  Also, we ordered two bottles of wine and then more glasses of wine as we ordered dessert and then they rushed us to seat another table right as we were paying our bill.  It was really weird and rude.  When we sat down at 7p, with our reservation, they never warned us that there was another table coming at 930p that we'd have to make room for.  So we ordered every course, including dessert and then more wine.  They should never have rushed us out for another table.  However, if they were going to, then they shouldn't have allowed us to order more wine as we ordered dessert.  They went about it really poorly too, not offering a drink or some sort of consolation, but sort of put it on us that they didn't plan their reservations properly.  They warned us, while we had full glasses of wine, and then came around again and told us we had to vacate the table. 
Didn't know there was a time limit on an extended dinner where you have a res, spend $$, order every course and copious amounts of wine.  Was really put off by this and won't be going back.

I was excited to try this restaurant after reading the reviews. I was told by a long time patron that it used to be a great neighborhood place but had recently become very snooty. First let me start by saying the pasta was tasty and my $17 drink was good too although when I asked for a cocktail straw they were almost embarrassed for me. Since when did a straw become "not cool". From start to finish the servers made you feel like you were just not quite good enough to be eating there!  After thinking about it and making another reservation I've decided that I don't want to give my money to a restaurant that probably encourages this "Bourgeois" behavior. I worked in the restaurant business for many years and I would never have allowed my waitstaff to behave like this. The food is tasty but not worth the ridiculous behavior that they seem to think is ok. Treat your paying customers well and with respect because we all know that there will be better review for another trendy restaurant right around the corner.....

One of the best Italian restaurants in NYC according to Grubstreet, Infatuation, and other blogs. This place has offered by far the most authentic taste of Tuscany, beautifully executed dishes atop of their 8/10 white table clothed covered tables, and excellent service.

Hypes:
- Lasagna - we got the meat sauce - you have an option of this or artichoke. It was absolutely delicious. Saucy, meaty, fresh layers and layers (probably like 100) of pasta.....really good.
- Cacio e pepe - the best I've had. better than in Italy.
- shaved asparagus salad - delicious - fresh, springy, crisp, and minty. a perfect blend of flavors
- service - impeccable. waiters knew their dishes, pronounciations, and were super attentive to everything. 
- surprisingly not as expensive as I had thought it would be. 

Gripes:
not for large groups - take one person with you. perfect date night. but maybe nothing more than that.

Tip:
Call early for a reservation. If you are in the area just walk in. We got lucky with a cancellation and were seated at 7pm on a weekday.
Outstanding in every way! The food is consistently stellar. I wish I iced in the neighborhood. I'd be here all the Time!

I didn't have the chance to eat here but the one star is for my interaction with the host when trying to make a reservation. I found the host to be rude and pretentious - barely willing to even speak with me about a reservation. After I tried calling many times over the last week with no answer, I came to the restaurant in person to make the reservation. I arrived right at opening at 5:30. The host wouldn't speak to me until he helped his customers first and told me I needed to wait outside. I completely understand waiting for other customers to be seated but I'm not sure why I was told to wait in the foyer instead of the actual restaurant where there was plenty of space near the empty tables in the front. I poked my head back in after all were helped and again he led me outside because I wasn't allowed inside the restaurant to make a reservation. He checked the date (which was a month away), offered me 10:30pm and I opted for the wait list. I asked if there were any other dates available that week at a better time and he said "I guess because I'm not busy right now I'll check for you". He acted like he was doing me some huge favor by assisting me in the reservation process. Then he finally told me there were no good reservation times for the next two months. I would have appreciated if he told me that from the beginning. He had the attitude that the restaurant was popular so they didn't need to treat people well since they weren't lacking for customers. I don't take offense easily but in this case I'll take my business elsewhere.

We had an excellent meal last night. The appetizers, main courses, desserts, wines... all were very well prepared, presented and delicious. In short, simple and traditional Italian dishes served by attentive and friendly staff, what's not to love?! Thank you and keep up the great work!

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday. Made a reservation a month out and was only able to snag a Sunday, 10pm slot. Thankfully someone canceled the day of and we were able to get a 6:30 table.  We got there 15 minutes early and were seated right away. The restaurant is a lot smaller than you'd think -- very quaint and comfortable. The servers were absolutely fantastic; they explained the menu really well, and gave us a good idea of what the portions are like.

We started with the cheese/meats platter. You get a wide assortment of both and they were all distinct in flavor. Their appetizer menu is pretty extensive and there were so many other options we could've gotten, too.

For the pasta dishes we got the cacio e pepe (their speciality) which was great. Very rich flavors, great pasta texture, very good size serving. The pastas don't look like they'll be a lot, but we were definitely full after the second pasta dish. We got the meat sauce pasta dish, as well. This was my favorite. Great flavors and good size serving, too. For the secondi we got the dry aged steak. This was our least favorite, as there wasn't a ton of flavor in it. It was passable. We get steak very often and are used to certain rich flavors. Not sure if Tuscan style steak is meant to be this way, but we were already to full from the pasta anyway to which more of it. Finally, we had the flourless chocolate cake for dessert. It was the right amount of sweet.

Overall, we'd definitely come back here for more of the pasta dishes, the great service, and the atmosphere. The food is definitely on the pricier side, but it's pretty comparable with other similar restaurants. Well worth the money.

+steak tartare
+perfect negroni
+playful, magnanimously portioned antipasto plate
+accepts discover
+less expensive than it could have been (for alex)

-cacio e pepe 45% too salty
-risotto 30% too viscous
-not enough bread to use as substrate, in general
-negroni bill adds up

Grubstreet rated this as the best Italian restaurant in NYC, I'm not sure I would say its the BEST but it is really really good. 

We had the fried artichokes to start (a special). They were perfect. Not too oily but still very crispy and most importantly had that inherent sweetness that artichokes can have. 

Then we had 3 pastas: meat lasagna, artichoke lasana, cacio e pepe. All 3 were unbelievable and I think are musts when you go to this restaurant. Don't even look at the menu just order them. The lasagnas somehow have a bazillion layers that are all so thin and wrapped in a super crispy layer on the top. 

Our server was very friendly and had a lovely accent pronouncing all the Italian words. The one downside was that he was a little pushy with trying to get us to order more food (understandably because we got no drinks, secondis, side dishes, or desserts) so his average check was pretty low...but at the same time he didn't need to be so pushy in trying to get us to order more food.

I came here one evening right when they opened, and I was glad I did. People were waiting outside of the door! I Sodi has one of the most delicious Cacio e pepe's in NYC. 

I also had the fried artichokes as an appetizer. A huge portion for 13 dollars. I was pleasantly surprised. 

I sat at the bar and had attentive and personalized service from the bartender. You will not be disappointed when you come to I Sodi!

The food was very good and we thought very fairly priced. My wife and I shared an order of lasagna and spaghetti. The sauce on the spaghetti was on point and the lasagna almost end melted in your mouth even with so many individual but thin layers.  
The service was a bit strange as our server had some odd mannerisms. With that being said she was earnest and tried to make sure we enjoyed our time. 
While there are no shortages of Italian restaurants to choose from in NY, I would enjoy going back to I Sodi.

Artichokes were over fried (almost burnt). Eric the waiter was rude and not welcoming. Same for the owner/chef - bad attitude. I sent the artichokes back - he came back telling me I'd still have to pay for them because chef says they are OK. Ended up into an argument. Dish was removed from the bill eventually - I guess reluctantly. I left 0 tip to Eric, but 40 USD to Patrick, the other waiter, as he tried to mediate. Will never go back. Almost ruined my evening but I didn't let them. They need to take their attitude down a notch or two. Read the other reviews about how rude this waiter/host called Eric is.
The Pappardelle al Limone is fantastic - a must order! The ravioli is also super delicious. Small space, no music.

A big disappointment...  Expected authentic Italian food. The quality of the pasta was great (homemade) but the tomato sauce wasn't good at all.. very basic and no taste..The entree wasn't exceptional as well and the wine wasn't good, we had to change it.  We were also bit surprised to pay for the bread... The quality price ratio is simply not good (the portions were tinies)... The service and atmosphere were nice but not enough to come back, as a native Italian we were expecting so much more. Very deceived about overall experience ...

My family and I ate here last Friday night while on vacation. It was wonderful.

We had the eggplant parmigiana appetizer. It was almost as good as my mother's. I'd say it was as good, but Italian nonnas have ways of finding things out, and I don't want to be in the doghouse for the rest of my life.

My son had the cacio e pepe, something I make all the time. But this was better than mine. Boo!

My wife had the rabbit wrapped in rigatini, which melted in your mouth. I'd eat this every day if I could.

And I had the spinach ravioli, which was tremendous.

We shared a piece of flourless chocolate cake for dessert, and by "shared," I mean my son let us have a bite each. It was delicious.

Friendly staff, terrific food -- we'll be back when we visit NYC next summer.

I loved this place. It's situated on a side street in the West Village. It takes a couple of seconds how to actually find the entrance. They offered a variety of negroni and it was well made. I ordered the Rigatoni Strascicati, which sounded simple, but it was done with perfection. The ingredients were top notch and the pasta had the perfect texture. 

Tl;dr Perfect pasta. Neighborhood vibe, non-pretentious, but intimate. I will definitely come again.

Amazing!!!!!Absolutely l loved this place. It was quaint and lovely. The food was so authentic and true to the region of Italy. I was on the best date of my life until I found out he was married. Who wears their ring on their right hand finger? Greeks I tell you! Come to find out he has amazing taste in Italian cuisine and also wives named Kathleen.  What a shame. I loved him and this place. I will 100% go back.

All things aside, I know I'm funny, but this place was so good. I just spent 3 weeks on the Italian coast. The food here was so paralleling similar it was like I was reliving my glory days in Italia! The pasta was fabulous, the lasagna to die, and the steak a little pink but that was his fault... 

Like I said, situation aside, I will be back!!! The perfect date spot etc.

I can elaborate within this review but I will just reiterate what other Yelpers have said, HORRIBLE SERVICE. 

Visiting here a few nights ago for a birthday, a  reservation which I booked so far in advance, turned out to be one of the worst experiences dining out. The kindest person working there was the busser.

Maybe they don't care how they treat customers since this place is so small, but it's quite a shame. Based on reviews it looks to be a trend at I sodi.

For the amount of money spent here, there are plenty of Italian restaurants nearby which have equal or greater level of food. 

Go elsewhere.

Amazing Italian! I wanted to try this restaurant after reading about it in Eater and it lived up to the hype. My friend ordered the Cacio e Pepe and I got the Tagliatelle Con Cipolla (a caramelized onion pasta)-- both were fantastic! We also split the flourless chocolate cake, which was incredibly decadent and delicious. 

The restaurant is small with around 10 tables and a bar (which was packed on the Sunday night I went), so definitely try to make a reservation and/or arrive early if you can. 

I hope to come back and try the artichoke lasagna and one of their negronis (they have an extensive list).

Excellent service.  Learned that our server used to actually be the chef, but decided he was tired of the kitchen and became a server after many years.  Regardless, the food was amazing, and thus the staff was extremely knowledgeable.  

AMAZING MEAT LASAGNA -- it honestly had 10+ layers of delicious and delicate pasta!  

Cacio Pepe was also excellent

The steak tar tar was out of this world.  

Can't wait to go back!!

Without knowing the story of the chef, or even anything about the restaurant, we stumbled upon I Sodi online one day and saw that it was highly recommended and felt like it was something worth a try and I'm SO glad we did. 

We were able to get a same day reservation for 8:30 and were greeted and seated immediately as we arrived in the restaurant. Our server, Nick was SO knowledgable and helpful in explaining each of the specials and made great recommendations on wine as well. A MUST TRY is the fried artichoke appetizer (I'm sure there's a much nicer name for it, but I don't remember it) which was absolutely amazing. Fried to the perfect texture with a sweet and savory after taste, mmm!
