Our server also recommended the lasagna and said it was absolutely to die for, so of course we did and it did not disappoint even a bit. I never knew lasagna could be sooo delicious. Aside from all the good antipasta and entrees, definitely make room for dessert! We had their tiramisu and affogato. I'm not even a dessert person, but wow I could not put my spoon down.

Overall, HIGHLY recommend this restaurant for authentic delicious Tuscan cuisine. Just don't forget to make a reservation.

One of the best Italian meals I have had in NYC thus far. The simple things are what stand out on their menu. I had the Gatlleto Schiacciato (cornish hen) and it was the most flavorful, juicy chicken I have ever had. I wouldn't normally order chicken, however at the suggestion of the server I am glad I did. My friend had the Cacio E Pepe and it was better than any other Cacio E Pepe he has ever had. The service was amazing as well. Our server was very honest with us about the best things on the menu and checked on us just enough. This restaurant definitely lives up to its hype.

No one loves this restaurant more than I, and we can certainly understand that restaurants cannot always hit the marks for excellence.  But this was one of those nights when the food preparation was very off and the service was borderline nasty. It is a interesting that when some restaurants gain amazing review status, some work harder and others, occasionally rest on their success.  It seemed the later on this recent evening at I Sodi.  We had some of the favorites on the menu and also some of the specials to receive only a rushed meal that was not special at all.  Food 3 1/2 stars, Service 2 1/2 stars.  Unfortunately, it seems that poor service is not unusual here and the regulars are just used to it.

Food was pretty great. The welcome though was off-putting. They warmed up but as others have mentioned prepare for some NYC brattiness at first. I'd come back, but they need to chill and lighten up. Ignacio Mattos lives you know. Be humble.

What a great spot! Feel good vibes, delicious pastas, and the service is good (not exceptional, but good). I got the cacio e pepe (amazing and cooked perfectly al dente), my friend got the tortelli di castagne. We shared because the food is too good not to share and both of our dishes were exquisite. This is glutonous but we even poured the cream sauce of her tortelli on the cacio e pepe at the end just to see how much more magical it could be! For dessert, we got the homemade tiramisu which is a must try! I will definitely be going back. It's a cozy spot, perfect for taking parents, a date, friends to catch up, because the quaintness of the restaurant allows you to still be able to hear!
The cacio e pepe was way too salty and inedible.  Lasagna was just ok.  We were very disappointed.

Tiny Italian restaurant tucked away in west village. I've seen some complaints about service, but keep in mind that the restaurant is SMALL and our waiter was not only attending to our table and maybe 2-3 others, but was also collecting coats and managing reservations at the same time. 

WHAT WE ORDERED: 
- Cacio e pepe - awesome! Reminded me of Rome where I had cacio e Pepe almost daily 
- truffle pasta - GET THIS! So amazing. truffle is out of this world 
- fried artichokes - you can probably skip this.  for 2 people, it was a little overkill.  a better option for a large table or if you are really craving fried anything
- vegetable and cheese appetizer - this is one of the specials and can't remember the actual name.  I would recommend this basically for the freshness of the vegetables, and who doesn't like melted cheese with a little bit of shaved truffle on top 
- tiramisu - GET THIS! probably one of the best tiramasu I've had. Consistency was closer to cheesecake. 

Will be back to try the layered lasagna!

Date night? Hit I Sodi.

I say that without actually experiencing date night for myself, as my only romp with this Tuscan mainstay in West Village was eating alone at the bar. But I was situated right between two different people canoodling with a prospective love interest, so I was essentially their unofficial chaperone for the evening. It's a small restaurant and conversations travel far, so I can recite nearly all the sweet nothings these lovebirds were cooing about. But enough about being the fifth wheel, as the food and drink program is the real star of the show.

Dining alone didn't give me as much access to the menu as one would like, but I had enough to determine I want to come back again and again. I went with their Paccheri Strascicati cooked in meat sauce, and their off-menu special of roasted root vegetables in aged balsamic vinegar. The former was portioned correctly for one person, and the pasta was perfectly al dente to stand up to the rich red sauce. The latter was so good, it could make that sh*tbag President of ours actually eat a vegetable instead of his nightly dose of two Big Macs in bed while watching Fox News. I could have walked away just eating the $15 bowl veggies alone and given them rave remarks. How this isn't a daily staple of their menu is beyond me, but hopefully they'll reconsider.

As a Negroni fanatic, they have a robust menu of different versions if you're looking for a fresh take. You can get your Negroni in the tried and true fashion, or get one with Cynar or any number of alternative Italian bitter spirits. If only the bar were more hospitable to pop in for a quick drink, I would be here all the time. It's most certainly a restaurant first and a bar after, but damn are those Negronis fantastic.

It's small, so either make reservations ahead of time or expect to wait if you're trying to dine during prime time hours.

I didn't eat there, but had a reservation for my husband's bday.  Got there a bit early on a VERY rainy, cold evening.  In their self-enclosed vestibule outside of the restaurant I was told I was 13 minutes early and had to wait in the pouring rain because there will be a line.  I had a reservation....I was locked out in the rain for being 13 minutes early.  The vestibule is not in the restaurant and yet I was asked to leave with the outer door locked behind me.  We went somewhere else and had a great meal, but our intention was to celebrate there.  So disappointed in the way this went down.  Besides the fact there was NO one else out there....I heard the food is good, but I just couldn't stay.
Tremendous food, great atmosphere, service that is second to none !  You cannot go wrong at I Sodi !!!  I highly recommend it

This is one of my favorite restaurants in New York. And easily my favorite Italian restaurant. The food is incredible. The staff is some of the best I've ever experienced and the ambiance is perfect. 

I've eaten most of the things not the menu and still go back for more. I highly recommend the TAGLIATELLE e CIPOLLA and the CACIO E PEPE. I often get one to share with whoever I'm eating with. I am not a big steak eater, I Sodi is one of the few places I will eat the steak because it is so incredible good. The fish and the Cornish hen under brick are consistently good. And you MUST MUST MUST get the sautéed spinach. Seems like a silly thing to recommend but it really is so good.

They have a fantastic wine list and often have good wines by the glass (one of the few restaurants that offers a glass of Amarone, for example). 

It's a great date place, especially if you really like the person you're taking out. 

Because it an be hard to get a reservation, I use the app Resy and just book a table far ahead and look forward to going.

Come here for: lovely intimate dinner, great date spot (note not based on personal experience but there is always next time) 

Food: amazing! Lasagna is 23 layer melt in your mouth heaven, artichoke salad (not special!) is also phenomenal. All portion are very large- sharing is good! Also loved the chicory side, charcuterie is strong but the small is massive and medium is a feast- order wisely. Wine list is pleasant and negroni menu is also tasty 
Decor: warm, friendly, and inviting. Only 12 tables in this whole place. High likelihood you sit at the bar and eat, but the bartenders are great, there is plenty of space, and you'll still walk out loving it 
Service: top notch! Really able to tell the story of the food, friendly faces to boot

Our food and drinks were outstanding.  Excellent in every regard.  When making a 7 pm reservation, I hadn't noticed an ending time, nor any addendum to the reservation detailing a time limit.   We were startled to have had our server inform us that he needed our table.  He should understand that dining is about more than the act of eating.  In addition, the onus on proper spacing of reservations rest with the establishment, NOT those being served.  In addition, this server, I imagine he is a head server, though professional almost to excess, should lighten up and be a bit less clinical.  He became uptight the moment we said we required more time to peruse the menu.  The owners, so focused on every detail and who run three very special dining establishments would not want to be on the receiving end of such a server.  And yes....the gratuity we left was customary by today's standards.

A divine dining experience. I Sodi is small but mighty and highly worth the wait. It's not hipster or trendy in anyway; it's very classic (down to the white tablecloths) and it prides itself in that. 

Food: the food is incredible. Authentic, seasonal pasta dishes, almost all freshly made, nothing too over complicated. The cacio & pepe is great as to be expected, the lasagna is incredibly rich and the noodles melt in your mouth, and my favorite is whenever they do the seasonal lemon pastas (I believe I had it as a pappardelle with lemon) - man I love lemon pastas. 

Drinks: very solid cocktails. Strong. Bartender is clearly knowledgeable.

Service: super experienced maitre d' and waitstaff. The waiters know their menu and specials like the back of their hand and give very good recommendations. Over the course of the few years I've been coming here, I definitely see a lot of the same people working here, which is rare for NY. 

The only downside is it's impossible to get a table here. Even when you book a month out, they don't have good dining times available. I've been super lucky with walk ins but sometimes had to leave when I wasn't so lucky.

Scene, hard to get in. Middle of Christopher bw Hudson and bleecker.

Go on Resy and book your slot way in advance or add yourself to the notify list.

Fried a asparagus is a must. Salty texture, full bowl.
Lasagna is really good but not grandmas. It's fancy style and leaves you wanting something more but sill very good.
Pasta is incredible... one of the best. Any mushroom dish in particular.

Be careful bc you'll walk out $350 lighter in a heartbeat. But that's ok bc it's an experience, and it's darn good!

Dinner here was a long time coming. Made the resy quite a while ago and it did not disappoint. Loved the vibe and the service was outstanding. Started with the fried artichoke special. Good not great as I thought it was missing something. All other pastas were phenomenal though. Can't wait to return.

Good food and nice, cute, small typical west village ambience but not worth the price or the hype. We had to wait 20 minutes past our reservation for a table. The restaurant is very small, the tables are relatively close together and there are maybe only 6,  2 or 4 tops. 
We were offered warm bread service, with amazing bread and olives, but there was a charge for this (4-6$ for 2 people) 
I tried the beef short rib, which was amazing. However, I thought the lasagna was a bit too rich and heavy. The food was good, but I thought the service was mediocre, and was just expecting more from this restaurant.

Solid meal at I Sodi on Friday night.  I have been trying to get a prime time reservation (on and off) for nearly a year, but put myself on the waitlist and surprisingly secured a 7:30pm spot.  We were seated promptly at our table, and service was impeccable throughout the night. We started off with negronis, can't remember the names but both were delicious.  We ordered fried artichokes and the bresaola to start.  Fried artichokes were amazing, the bresaola was not so impressive.  

We ordered the lasagna and cacio e pepe next.  Both were very flavorful, but the cacio e pepe was way too salty (had so much potential).  I took the lasagna home since we ordered too much food and it was still excellent the next morning.

For the main dish, we ordered this beef cutlet stewed in a tomato sauce with potatoes, a side of fried potatoes, and the piselli (green peas).  This part of my meal was awesome.  The beef cutlet was incredible, so tender, simple, and packed with flavor.  I don't even know what to say about the peas, they were mushy enough to be a starch but still popped with salty olive oil flavor.  Just perfect.  

4 stars for the salty pasta, but overall very enjoyable meal.

Seated at the bar. 
Nice decor, not pretentious, very sleek and elegant.
Knowledgeable bar tender. Great service.
Food:
Branzino. Simply cooked, the way seafood is supposed to be. Just Perfect!
Tagliatelle with caramelized onions. Great balance!
Lasagna with artichokes. It was the only downside. The layers of pasta were overcooked. Taste was there, but the lasagna was mushy and it lacked texture. Also it felt too heavy (probably too much béchamel?).
Selection of wines. By the glass they had only 5 options for red. I ordered a bottle, but prices were pretty steep. I found that a bit annoying, considering I was the only person drinking wine.
Overall it was a good dining experience.

Quality Italian fare in an intimate, low-key space...strangely, we were made to wait a bit for our table despite having a reservation. Guess they stack those resy's pretty close together.

The many-layered lasagna was outstanding but the artichoke appetizer (a special that night) was under-seasoned and underwhelming. One out of two ain't bad.

NY Magazine once described this as a "perfect restaurant". Not sure about that, but the service was excellent and, as I said, the only classic Italian dish I tried--lasagna--was exceptional. Worth a go.

We took a chance and called for a reservation on sat  we received a text back that we had one lucky us 
We had a great experience we were met by Eric at the door and he also was our server
He was great explained the menu and the wine list
Our dinner was superb  such great flavors wonderful small restaurant that we will be back. And our thanks to Eric for making it a great night

Going to see A play at the Lucille Lortel Theatre in the West Village, so this restaurant was perfect; on the same block.  An unfriendly greeting from a stuck up waiter, who quickly inquired if I had a reservation, I did not. So was immediately dismissed and told a 45 minute wait at the bar, longer for a table. No question if  I wanted to put my name on the waiting list. 2 minutes later, a young guy walks in, same waiter, all smiles and pleasantries, informs him of the waits and takes his name and number.  Maybe it would have helped if I was a guy!!!

So I have been dying to check out this restaurant for the past 4 months and finally got a reservation on Resy! While 2/3 of our party was there on time, one member was exactly 13 minutes late. After being promptedly seated, we were rushed through dinner and reminded that one of our guests was late. Mind you, the table next to us and several bar seats were available. The food, particularly the lasagna and cacio e pepe, were fantastic. The tagliatelle with peas and pancetta that just hit the menu was pretty bland tbh. This was a special occasion dinner and I was disappointed that we were rushed through. Particularly for a restaurant that has as many accolades and such excellent food, I was quite disappointed with the service. Would definitely go back but maybe sit at the bar next time.

I thought really high thing s of L Sodi, as we had to make the reservation the night they came out on the dot at midnight. Reservations are hard to get which I thought meant it was amazing. I was far from correct. The place is extremely small so that may be why. we started by ordering 2 cocktails, but the glasses were half full. We asked the waiter to get wine, and he protested against us and made my friend feel extremely uncomfortable. He basically would not take them back until we begged. He then avoided us the whole night. He came and took our order, but after that we did not see him again. We ordered the fried artichoke special which were good and the portion was small. They also gave us bread- which they charged us for unknowingly. It was only1 dollar, but I've never been anywhere that unknowingly charges you for bread, especially Italian. The bread was ok at most. Then we got cacio e pepe and lasagna with meat. For me, the lasagna was way too rich and filling- too much cheese. The cacio e pepe was good but not the best my friend had had and she had lived in Rome. We were never asked if we wanted dessert or anything. Another random man that wasn't our waiter brought us a check because our waiter avoided us all night: they also brought out our pastas Coke so we had to ask them to microwave them. No one apologized for this or even cared, just brought them out right from the microwave. I would definitely not come back here for the rude staff and sub par food.

Save your money, time and energy and dine elsewhere.

I had high expectations for my experience at I Sodi. It took time and effort to snag a reservation at 8 o'clock on a Friday! 

Don't order the Sage Martini if you want to feel a buzz OR if you aren't a fan of throwing money in the blender.  I sent mine back because it was so small and disappointing and explained I would rather wine. Instead of gracefully taking it back, the waiter (handlebar mustache) fought with me. My own waiter went out of his way to publicly humiliate and shame me for my own dining preference and then avoided our table for the rest of the night!! 

The cacio e pepe was delicious but arrived luke warm. However my friends meat lasagna ($27!) was delicious and arrived piping hot. I thought it was out of this world. However, it is very dense and after various bites it begins to have a cream cheese like texture. 

For the fried artichoke appetizer special (6 out of 10), cacio e pepe ( 6.5 out of 10) and lasagna (8 out of 10), and the cheapest bottle of wine on the menu ($47), our bill came to around $68.00 per person.

Yet another Eater recommendation that was pretty spot-on. As often happens, we wanted to go out on a Friday night but hadn't made any reservations and pretty much nothing was available. Resy to the rescue! We got an alert on Resy that a table became available at the last minute so we happily ventured out. 

The ambiance and service at this restaurant were about par for the course. We also really enjoyed the much talked about lasagna, BUT it was a bit cold on one side (hence the 4 stars). Warm it all the way up, please! 

But after we got past that we had an amazing truffle-ly pasta followed by an equally amazing Cornish hen and an equally, equally amazing rabbit entree.

All-in-all a great Friday night meal...
Simply the best. Stick with the pasta here and you'll be transported to heaven...The lasagne is perfection.

Minus stars.
Who are you kidding?
Crap food, way over-priced and the audacity to charge for bread?
Tuscan born bull shi*.
Rename it: I Sodimy
Why?
Because I went there twice and both times, I got it right up my  financial *ss.
Vero buco.
Just my opinion, of course.

When I look back on 2018, i will remember I Sodi as one of the most elusive New York restaurants that I agonized about night after night, in my attempt to get a reservation at a decent hour. Finally, after a couple of weeks of stalking the site, I managed to get a reservation for 6pm on a Monday night. 
The night finally rolled around, and we came to I Sodi promptly, at 6pm. The restaurant is small, with tables to seat probably around 12 people, and bar seating to fit less than that. However, it is elegant in an understated, simple way. 
We were brought water and copies of the menu immediately. Our waiter went over the specials of the night, before we placed our orders. 
We settled on two appetizers, including the artichoke salad, and the burrata and prosciutto (an appetizer), the pappardelle al limone, and the meat lasagne. The bread they started us off with was excellent. Both appetizers were simple, with delicate flavors, and fresh ingredients. 
Our main dishes however, were the highlight of the night. The pappardelle al limone was cooked softer than al dente (but no complaints there), in a buttery, lemon sauce, seasoned simply with pepper. It was perfect. 
My boyfriend had the meat lasagna, and we were amazed at the ability of the chef to be able to fit in so many layers- an appropriate name could have 'thousand layer lasagna'. It was delicious, full of flavor, and cooked perfectly. 
We decided not to skip dessert that night, and ordered the pannacotta, which came with a small side of berries. The pannacotta was firm, but soft and silky, with a subtle milky flavor that was complemented by the tart, juicy berries. It was also done perfectly, but not recommended for those who like heavy, sugary desserts. 
The service was attentive, personal and friendly. 
I've thrown the word 'perfect' around a lot in this review, but when it comes down to it, that was an apt description of our experience at I Sodi. Highly recommend, and can't wait to dine here again.
Amazing food! Bartender Chris is the best friendly knowledgeable bartender I ever met! Amazing in all levels!!!!! Fried artichoke strip steak lasagna strawberry tiramisu! Can't wait to go back!

Fantastic dinner here - waited quite a while before snagging a reservation.

Started the meal with the fried artichokes (my favorite of the apps), truffle burratta (good but didn't really taste the truffle), antipasto (great), and tartar (also good).

Had the pappardelle al limone which brought my back to a meal I had in Capri on my honeymoon.  Also tried the husband's cacio e pepe which I loved.

Would definitely return!

Overrated Italian and somewhat pretentious for their service. Ordered the Ravioli - overly creamy and cheese saturated. Also sampled the Pappardelle a limone - simple dish, pasta cooked perfectly - ok - many other places do similarly. For the main the Florentine bistecca (which I have had in Florence) was an unmitigated disaster. For a 120 dollar outlandishly priced offering the steak was not cooked to temp, so they took it back and brought back each piece as grilled meat going past temperature- medium rare to medium well. Additionally Artichoke fries were summarily dumped in a heap. There is an identity crisis of sorts here - lost between some measure of Tuscan rusticity and wannabe sophistication.
My negroni was well crafted so a star for that but other than that a massive mess of an overpriced dinner for celebration gone awry.

Went with 2 friends a few weeks ago. We had early dinner resi at 5.30pm that we were 10 min late for.  We ordered wine and then ordered apps, pasta and the chicken for dinner.  We asked to have it served as 3 courses to which we were told that we couldn't and when we insisted the answer was if we did thenwe weren't allowed to order dessert.  Really. How rude!   They rushed us through the entire dinner and when we  ordered our second bottle of wine, the waiter was actually angry with us.  After 2 hours they told us we had to leave as our time was up.   I told them wshould have been told of a  time limit when we made reservation.  The waiter just looked at us and again told us we had to get up.  I barely remember the food as I was so upset by the treatment, although I do remember the $126 pp bill!  All I can say is I will never go back to such a rude restaurant.

Incredible food and very warm service! Shared
the antipasto platter, cured tuna appetizer, ravioli,
Lasagna and Cacio e Pepe. All amazing dishes especially the lasagna which is probably the best I've ever had. A new fave spot to keep revisiting!

We ate dinner here & I had a very unpleasant waiter, who was Doshin.  He has a beard, mustache, and wears glasses. I asked him how the fried artichokes were prepared. First he gave me a sarcastic answer & said, "They are fried."    He was rude and disrespectful.  When I questioned him further, he said they just used the heart of the artichoke, it was breaded & fried.  He also made fun of me when I asked him another question. 
 
He misrepresented the food. When I got the artichoke dish, it was only 1/4 of the heart and 3/4 of the leaves. It was deep fried and extremely greasy!

When he came by & asked how the food was, I told him I did not like the artichoke dish. He replied, "THAT'S TOO BAD!"  Then he turned his back on me & walked away.  Why did he bother to ask me, if he didn't care. 

I am really sorry we came to this restaurant.  I will not ever come to this restaurant again or recommend it to anyone!  It was an extremely unhappy experience!

I Sodi seems to be the hot spot for an upscale casual Italian dinner in New York. It's on every damn list, and it books out weeks in advance, something I figured out when I hopped on Resy looking for a table well before my trip. I wanted to go with my husband Matt B. on a Monday night, our one night in town to get dinner without friends or family, and put myself on the waitlist. I got a couple notifications that tables were available, for 9:00 and 10:30 seatings, only to find them snapped up by the time I saw the emails. I was ready to give up, but decided to call the restaurant directly a day before our date night. I said something like, "Hey, long shot, but we're in from out of town and wondering if you have anything for two people tomorrow night?" The woman on the other end came back with, "How about 7:00?"

It was clear when we arrived why the reservations are so difficult. I Sodi is a tiny restaurant, the narrow space half occupied by a long bar. We got a two-top right against the window looking out onto Christopher Street. It was cozy and pleasant, and we felt very much like we were in a charming neighborhood restaurant in one of the toniest neighborhoods in the country. Service was excellent, welcoming and attentive. We settled in and had a stellar dinner.

We started with a round of negronis, which are apparently a bit of a house specialty, with nine variations on the menu. We tried the Negroni Chinato, with Greenhook gin, Aperol, and Barolo Chinato, and the Count Negroni Original, with Hayman's gin, Gran Classico, and house vermouth. Both were outstanding. We switched to wine at some point in the meal--I got a glass of the Vernaccia "Fiore" Montenidoli, a Tuscan white, while Matt got the Barbera D'Alba Superiore, Marina Coppi, a Piedmont red.

The food was wonderful--classic Italian, perfectly prepared. There was good brown bread served with olive oil, as well as a snack dish of purple olives. We ordered the bresaola and the burrata special to start. The bresaola was a flavorful plate of aged air-dried wagyu beef with parmigiano, arugula, and a drizzle of aged balsamic vinegar. The burrata was like a hyper-luxe caprese, with a huge ball of soft, milky cheese and a heap of juicy halved cherry tomatoes, dressed up with basil, black pepper, and olive oil.

We went with pasta for our mains, and I'm pretty confident this was the way to go. We ordered two pastas so simple, any eight-year-old (or picky 35-year-old husband) could enjoy them, and they were both sophisticated and supremely delicious. The cacio e pepe is one of I Sodi's main draws, and its appeal is immediately apparent. The spaghetti is cooked an exact al dente, and the black pepper and pecorino sauce clings just the right amount, blasting every bite with flavor. The pasta corta was a special, short pasta with tomato, basil, and pecorino. A bare bones red sauce pasta, but utterly satisfying, every part of it on point. The only thing I didn't love was our side of piselli, or green peas. This was probably a personal preference thing, though--they were on the mushy side, but I'm pretty sure they were meant to be that way.

For dessert, we shared an affogato and a strawberry tiramisu, both light and lovely. The affogato gave us a nice hit of espresso, poured over fast-melting vanilla gelato. The strawberry tiramisu combined lush mascarpone with sweet, glistening, red strawberry and strawberry sauce. I could've eaten several of these without noticing my stomach fill up.

This was a great meal with top notch negronis and brilliant pastas--really, what more can you want from one restaurant? I'm chuffed that we were able to slide into I Sodi, and would love to go back on another visit to New York.

no words 
dont 
come 
here 

they are so rude and all have sticks up their asses
we waited an hour despite having a reservation whilst others who eric 'knew' or thought looked better dressed than us were able to be seated straight away

food took two hours to come as well without an apology or any appreciation of the fact that we had been waiting so long

we were so excited about the food so it's a real shame that the staff, particularly eric, had to ruin our experience for us :(
Had the antipasto, cacio e pepi and meat lasagna. To die for! Intimate Italian secret spot.

Randomly walked by this place around 6:00pm on a Saturday night and was intrigued as patrons were coming in. There was a small line outside when I passed by it away at 8:45pm that same night. Decided I would give it a try at a later date.

Returned about 3 weeks later on a Sunday night around 7pm. Parties before me we're put on a waiting list but I managed to get a seat at the bar right away as a solo diner. There was a good mix of patrons of all ages, young and old professionals, dates, solo diners, smaller groups. The space is VERY tiny, making room for about 8 white tablecloth tables and a large bar with about 12 seats. There seems to be a crowd of regulars because the staff was welcoming every other party with questions revealing previous acquaintances. 

I had a simple bowl of pasta with meat sauce, see picture below, which was quite delicious, and savoured a glass of Piedmont wine. The entire menu is inspired by Northern Italy. I secretly wished I was not dining alone so I could try other items on the menu, as I glanced at the plates of my fellow diners. 

What truly makes this restaurant stand out is the atmosphere and the staff. Place is so tiny, it really feels that you're one of the lucky few who get to experience it on any given night. Service was absolutely impeccable and as professional as it gets. Definitely worth a visit.

We live in the West Village and enjoy dining out on the evening. We recently returned to I Sodi after a fairly extended lapse. So many choices.  This review is occasioned by a highly regrettable and unwelcome incident having to do with the service provided.  The food was characteristically excellent. I had ordered a quartino of Vernaccio with my first course based on the menu of wines by the glass being presented when we sat down at the bar. With my main course I asked for a recommendation to go with my NY Strip.  I was not shown the same wines by the glass menu but presented with a bottle and a tasting of a 2011 Super Tuscan. I ordered a quartino.  On the bill I was charged $40 for that wine. A quartino!!  I paid the bill and on leaving expressed to the server behind the bar my real annoyance at the tactic employed. The response was dismissive. I was presented  the wine by the glass menu with a vague wave of the hand pointing to the red wines on the list.  Again I was never offered that menu before accepting his recommendation. There was other, equally appropriate - and less expensive - choices available. A restaurant of this caliber ought never try to "zing" a customer. I was "zinged".
The meat lasagna, ravioli, and negronis are worth going for. Not worth eaiting to eat at an absurd hour but the food and drinks are certainly good if you can snag an earlier reservation.

Everything on the menu is cooked to perfection and delicious. The wine list makes it impossible to choose incorrectly. Tough to get a reservation, but show up around 6 and you'll be able to get seated at the bar. Save this for a special occasion or an intense craving for quality Tuscan food, as it isn't cheap. But totally worth it.

Just dined at I Sodi last night and my husband and I both agreed that it was hands down one of the best meals we have ever had. I originally wanted to take him there for his birthday in June but there were no tables available for weeks. I ended up booking a reservation as a surprise for our anniversary. I made sure to follow another reviewer's suggestion and booked several weeks in advance at midnight when reservations for my desired date opened up on Resy. The wait was SO worth it! Food was phenomenal and service was outstanding. Our waiter Eric was very attentive and gave us great suggestions for cocktails, wine and main dishes. We shared the burrata with truffles and goat cheese crostino for appetizers and I had the cacio e peppe while my husband had the meat lasagna as our main dishes. Everything was so delicious! The flavors were incredible and the food was not super heavy - I left feeling satisfied but not grossly full. We had the tiramisu for our dessert and it was amazing, I like that it has a thin crust on the bottom and not a heavy cake as I've had in many other tiramisus. Also, I'm usually not a Negroni fan (I usually find them too bitter) but the Negronis here are outstanding! Very well balanced and innovative. Our waiter Eric suggested the Terra Negroni and it was fabulous. All in all we had an amazing meal with great cocktails and wine and wonderful service! Put this on your must-try list and grab an opening on Resy - I promise you the wait is absolutely worth it!
Excellent and creative food and nice service. We most enjoyed the fried artichoke, salad greens and lemon pasta. Excellent all around including nice Italian wines.

Protip: Don't bother with the steak, that's what garnered the lower rating in my earlier review, just go for the pastas and negronis.  Truffles are back in season, so came here for their truffle pasta specials.  Hopefully you're in early because three orders black truffle tagliatelle ($35) wiped out half their stock.  Also had the white truffle pappardelle ($67), both were amazingly delicious but the difference in aroma/taste didn't seem warranted tonight.

This tiny restaurant, highly recommended by friends in the neighborhood, accepts phone reservations and seats walk-ins on tiny wooden stools tightly packed along the bar, uncomfortable if you are planning to enjoy a three course meal. The service is excellent, as well are the bar and cocktails.  The soft homemade tortelli filled with flavorful chestnuts and ricotta was served lukewarm with a thick tasteless Parmesan cream sauce; grated Parmesan on top added flavor. I might have liked it better if it was served hot.  The al dente Cacio y Pepe had a sharp pepper and cheese flavor. Meat courses are large and good for sharing unless you have big appetite. The de-boned rabbit was beautifully presented, rolled in pork belly with densely flavored chopped spinach, but the rabbit was overly spiced with rosemary and fatty with pieces of inedible gristle.  The huge double pork chop was perfectly cooked over braised endives.
Lasagna and salad were right on.  Cacio e pepe was ok.  They killed my pork chop - dry as a bone.  Could not eat.  Disappointing after wait to get resi there....

I came here with my Russian boyfriend a few days before running 26.2 miles, a feat that calls for some pasta fueled energy. We arrived at the perfect time and were promptly seated. We ordered fried artichokes and the one and only 24 layered meat lasagna of kings from the menu (this is what they're known for!) our waiter also listed several delectable new additions to the menu. We ordered the shrooms with Parmesan and truffle pasta.

Look, with everything on the menu priced in the $30 range, my boyfriend and I went bananas! The food was so incredibly delicious - even the free bread and colored olives were outstanding. I also really liked the bar scene and atmosphere.

That said, we got the check and the truffle pasta was $68!! I feel as though I have a duty to my loyal readers to share this piece of information since my bf and I were astonished to say the least. But, I do love a good truffle.

I have been waiting forever to try this restaurant and thankfully it was well worth the wait. Full disclosure: make a reservation!!!! 5 people tried to walk in while we waited for the table and the wait was over 2 hrs for a table and an hour for maybe a place at the bar.

The over all atmosphere of this restaurant is great- no frills at all but extreme quality. The atmosphere is intimate (not too many tables small space good for a date) but not overly romantic...the lighting is very cozy and the noise level while higher is comfortable. 

Upon arrival, waiting outside their sliding door I knew we were going to have an amazing meal- how? The smell. I was instantly surrounded by the amazing combination of cheese sauce bread (
Aka heaven... mouth was watering.

We had to wait a little to be seated as the party before us was finishing up and our waitress brought us water and menus to look at while we waited. Once seated she relayed the amazing specials and brought us bread and olive oil. Overall loved the service at this place- attentive, informative, and friendly.

We didn't end up getting a special BUT the special I was very close to trying was a white truffle pasta dish with shaved white truffles on top- if you go anytime soon I suggest you consider this because it sounded unreal. 

We settled on Bresaola (air dried wagyu beef w parmigiana aged balsamic and arugula) as our antipasto course (loved this app so light and fresh and full of flavor) and 3 pasta dishes as our main (with hope to save room for dessert). Unfortunately we did not have room for dessert so I would next time go for two antipastos and two pastas just so it isn't such a heavy and filling meal- however I was eager to try all of the pastas a friend recommended so I have no regrets.

The pasta was out of this world- so fresh- well portioned- perfectly flavored. Perfect for splitting with a friend or date. Perhaps if we had a little more time to digest afterwards dessert would have made an appearance (next time). We had the meat lasagna, Cacio e Pepe, and the paperdelle al limone. I have to say my favorite dish was the lasagna so be sure to include this in your meal. Overall loved this west village gem and will be coming back (if I'm lucky enough to get a reservation).

I showed up at I Sodi yesterday to buy an expensive gift card there and was told that they are TOO BUSY to sell one and asked me to come back in TWO HOURS. The arrogance it takes to ask a customer to wait for two hours to have someone swipe their credit card is beyond anything I have ever experienced as a paying customer. Bye bye I Sodi, it was great while it lasted :-(

Well, I finally got to eat at I Sodi last night.  It wasn't the easiest reservation to get but it was all so worth it.  I'll caveat this by saying every single menu item we ordered was a 5-star item.  I can't recommend one over the other.  It was all fantastic.   We ordered the burrata with black truffle, fried artichoke hearts and the lasagna with meat sauce all as appetizers.  For our main courses I ordered the rabbit that came with sautéed spinach and my wife ordered the cacio e pepe.  For dessert we ordered the tiramisu.  As for the wait staff our waiter answered every question we had. Best of all he asked about our wine tastes and recommended a wine for us that turned out to be superb.  I will return to I Sodi!
The lasagna is REALLY good and worth the hype. However, the bartender was VERY pushy and made us feel uncomfortable the whole time just because we didn't order any drinks.
Amazing experience and incredible service, the food, the service and the knowledge behind the dishes was amazing.  The burratta as well as the truffle pasta are incredible.

Wowowowowow. Best lasagna I have ever had. (Photo) 

First time here and we had a great experience. Service was great, food was great, atmosphere was great. We all ordered appetizers - we had a couple of salads, I had the endive and my sister got a very cheesy one (but it was delicious). We also got the steak tartar. 

For our entrees, I had the lasagna, my sister had the branzino, and our friend had the rabbit. Everything was phenomenal! The lasagna was so intricate. I'm not sure how many layers there were but there were a LOT. It was so delicious. None of us could stop eating it! I tried the branzino as well. It was tasty and fresh. A nice light option. The rabbit was incredible as well but very heavy and rich. Perfect if you're super hungry. 

For dessert we got the tiramisu and the Panama cotta. Both were great - I preferred the panna cotta and it may have been one of the best I've ever had. Highly highly recommend this place for good, quality Italian. Just know to come early and be prepared to wait! You can always put your name in and go to a bar nearby. They'll call! Can't wait to bring my parents when they're back up here.
Love everything about this place! Amazing food, a great service, and romantic cozy atmosphere!!!
This is a neighborhood Italian restaurant that is quite reasonably priced and the food is of excellent quality. It is a great restaurant for a midweek dinner as well as a fancy Saturday night meal.

Simply superb.  From the food to the drinks to the service to the atmosphere.  It's like your transported out of NYC and in Italy the moment you step inside.  I sat at the bar with a friend and we shared the fried artichokes, wagyu beef, truffle pasta special, cacio e pepe and spinach ravioli.  Everything was delicious.  My favorite was probably the spinach ravioli.  Additionally, I had their classic negroni that was made perfectly.  The bartender and servers truly care about your experience.  You can see it in their facial expressions alone.  I will certainly be back.

Had a great time here with a couple friends. The space is small and cozy, but very comfortable. 

Started by sharing the fried artichokes. These were perfectly crispy and tender, finished with salt and lemon. Best version I'd had of this.

We then had the lasagna a sugo - Definitely recommend. So many layers of meaty, cheesy goodness without being too heavy or greasy. The cacio e pepe and paccheri strascicati were also tasty but less memorable. Portions were a nice size but I think the food could have been a little hotter.

Service was friendly and negroni's were delicious. Would definitely come back if it weren't so hard to get a res.

After many (read: 4) attempts at getting into I Sodi, we finally got a reservation for two at the quaint West Village Italian restaurant. The food was to die for. We started our dinner with the antipasto special which included fresh burrata and toasted bread with a sundries tomato spread. It was delicious. Then for our main course, I had the Lasagna with the meat sauce and my girlfriend had the Cacio e Pepe. The lasagna was incredible. It had 20 layers or so of pasta and it was super filling. Probably the best lasagna I've ever had and I'm Italian (sorry, Nonny!) 

The only downside of this place is that you NEED a reservation in order to sit down and eat. Otherwise, it's near impossible to get a table. I can't wait for the next time we get a reservation to I Sodi. :)

Wow! I think I just had my favorite Italian meal in the city! My boyfriend and I had a reservation for 630 on Thursday night and were seated right away. The place is very small, less than 10 tables probably, and some seating at the bar so walk ins without a reservation were quoted long waiting times. 

To start we each got a glass of red wine and the fried artichoke special and this was amazing!! The artichokes were fried to perfection and perfectly seasoned. I highly recommend starting with these. 

For our mains we got the 22 layer lasagna with artichoke sauce and ricotta filled tortelli in a chestnut sauce. Both were incredible!! I couldn't believe a 22 later lasagna could be so light. The flavors were perfect in this. Also it seems like a small piece but we had trouble finishing it! The star of our entire meal though was the tortelli! It was recommended by our waiter and this was my favorite thing! The chestnut sauce they were in was so delicious, and had a sweetness to it that went with the ricotta tortelli so well!

For dessert I got the flourless chocolate cake and my boyfriend got a scoop of the stratcchitelli gelato. Both were so good! The cake is very rich and was actually really good paired with the ice cream! 

The service is also incredible! Our waiter made wine and food recommendations that all turned out amazing and was just great throughout the night! Overall an incredible experience! So glad we were able to get a reservation and try all the food. I highly recommend I Sodi to everyone!

I Sodi was fantastic. 

The service was exceptional and our waiter was super knowledgeable and quick to give recommendations based on our personal preferences. 

Definitely order the fried artichoke hearts appetizer and a glass of wine to start off. I'd also recommend the 24 layer house lasagna, which is the house speciality, as well as the ricotta-filled tortelli. 

Although I'm not usually a dessert person, I am glad that I opted for a single scoop of the classic stracciatella gelato. The fudge chocolate cake was also delicious but very, very rich. 

I would definitely come back!

This place is absolutely delicious!    It was really hard to get a reservation since the restaurant is so small but please go and enjoy this Italian marvel in NYC.  The staff was courteous, as you would expect them to be in such an intimate setting.  The food was great.  The fried artichoke was to die for! So as many other reviewers state on this page, definitely go for the artichoke appetizer.  As a main I got the lasagna and my SO got the chestnut sauce tortellini and wow!   I will be back for more so long as I can manage a reservation!

I just love this place. Excellent service. Amazing ingredients. Impeccable execution. 

Get the meat lasagna!

I had really high expectations based on reviews. Nothing here is memorable-- the antipasti plate has non-robust cheeses, the touted artichoke lasagna is dry, and the Cornish hen was tasty but "meh". The lighting was high, there was no music playing, and the diners at the tables on either side of us were wearing hoodies. L'artusi, for the neighborhood and for the money, is a much better meal.

We have been regular patrons of I Sodi for many years; however in the past few years, the service has been deteriorating. We went to I Sodi again the first weekend of March and sat at the bar. The waiter, although my son eats there regularly, treated us as if we were an inconvenience. He was rude, rushing us to order. After I had sampled two different wines and decided on the first, he proceeded to add the chosen wine to the rejected glass and refused to replace it. This disrespectful and dismissive service has become increasingly worse this past year. Paying customers should feel as if they are valued, and not an inconvenience. They should be conscious that I Sodi is no longer the only good Italian food show in town. Therefore, tolerance for dealing with snobby, unfriendly service has gotten much lower.

Definitely meets the standards of every positive review, article, word of mouth, etc that you'll hear about Rita's restaurant. 

This tiny space gets booked months in advance, so I highly recommend coming right before they open and waiting outside. Also don't recommend coming with a large group if you're a walk in bc they usually will take you right to the bar. 

Fried artichokes. Named as a special and you should def get it before it goes away. Huge portion, super crunchy not overly fried. 

Antipasto app comes in two sizes, comes with 4 diff kinds of cured meat. Amazing. Everything is so full of flavor but because of how high of a quality the ingredients simply are. 

For the lasagna (meat or artichoke option) our bartender recommended the meat option. First time I've had a lasagna with this many layers, and it's so filling. I'd recommend sharing? Honestly the lasagna blew my mind. 

Oh and their famous negronis? Yes yes yes. The classic was WOW. So smooth. They have an extensive list of vermouth options along the bar. Would be fun to go one evening and try their different varieties of negronis they offer. Classic is $15. 

Very friendly service, never rushed. It's a good atmosphere that caters to plenty of different groups. I wouldn't come with a group larger than 6. Great choice for a date night!

Definitely one of the best authentic Italian restaurants in nyc. Come here with friends so you can try more pasta dishes! My favorite dish was definitely the lamb pappardelle. Still my favorite dish to date. We shared the lemon and sautéed onion pasta and both were really good and unique. Perfect portion size. Great service but if you don't have a reservation be prepared for a wait and only a seat at the bar, which was ok by us since the bar had a ton of space for all the food we ordered. Try setting alarms on Resy for reservations.

This place serves up some excellent Italian food in the West Village. Reservations are hard to come by as it is quite an intimate space, but we were able to out our name in around 7pm and be seated at 9:30pm at the bar.

We really enjoyed everything here, especially the famous spring salad and lasagna.

Definitely worth checking out for a nice night out on the town.

I was lucky to snag a reservation here and I'm so glad I did.

Some context if you've never been before - the tables are reservation only and there are about 8 of them and the 15 or so seats at the bar are for walk-ins. On a recent Saturday visit, there was a line of folks outside by 5:15.

The food was fantastic and the service was on point, without being overly formal or overbearing. The pappardelle lived up to its hype (thanks Food 52!) and the cocktails were all excellent.
It was decent but a bit overhyped. Service was great but food was just okay. The lasagne was the best thing we ordered.

I Sodi is an excellent italian spot providing an intimate and memorable experience. I think it's overhyped in the sense that I would not wait the 1-2 months for a reservation to eat here, but if a table was available and I was feeling italian, I'd happily stop by here.

The service was excellent, and I love the quaint atmosphere. What I love about the food is that they do a lot with a handful of ingredients without going overboard, even when experimenting with different dishes. Overall, really good flavors, high-quality pasta, and well-balanced creamy profile on all of the food.

Pappardelle al limone - The pasta quality was perfect, and the flavor profile really brings out the lemon without it being too much. It's a lighter pasta, which serves as an excellent starter, and it almost reminds me of lemon cheesecake.

Lasagna - Probably one of the best lasagna I've had in my life. It might not be photogenic, but it's incredibly creamy and flavorful.

Ravioli - The pasta here was actually slightly tough at the edges, but flavorful and perfectly creamy.

The bread was pretty disappointing and served cold and a bit tough, but the olive oil was delicious.

decent food, very clean but take reservations please. They allow tables to sit empty for 2 hours when there is a line to sit at the bar to eat. Makes no sense. 4 stars because the food is consistent and if you suck up to the staff they will smile. Welcome to New York .

Food: 4.5*
Service: 4*

I think this is one of the toughest reservations to get in NYC but in the end it was worth it. The pasta took me back to Rome in the sense that the  noodles were definitely al dente with good chew to it. I had the rabbit dish which was good and it came with a bunch of greens, but not mind blowing. The lasagna and paccheri with meat sauce were really good and we had a grilled calamari appetizer that was simple, yet tasty. The meat sauce reminded me of the bolognese sauce at Il Corvo in Seattle) which is a can't miss place by the way.) I would come back for the pasta in a heartbeat...if I can get a reservation.

This place is always great. The food is amazing with great ambience and service to boot. Last time we had the grilled chicken and the rabbit wrapped in rigatina, both were fantastic. The cacio e Pepe was a little too salty and the tiramisu was ok, could have made different choices for both of those. Negronis are always a good way to start off here too. Overall big fan of this place.

We were looking forward to finally dining at I Sodi, and celebrating some big news while we were at it. Unfortunately it did not live up to the hype.
The food wasn't anything noteworthy, not something to go out of the way for. The experience with the waitstaff further knocked down the experience.

The food: unfortunately nothing impressive. The pastas were nothing special (esp considering all the hype and difficulty getting reservations) and the sides were  also nothing special. If it were "any other" Italian restaurant, perhaps we would have expected less, but to be considered one of the best... we didn't quite get it. There are far better. 

The service: 0 stars. I've never had such a rude waiter. Did not want to answer questions on the menu, spoke so quickly we couldn't understand him, was terribly impatient, and SNATCHED the menu out of my hand. (?! That was a first) He did not check in on us at all. So much for a celebratory dinner.

At the end, went to use the restroom, which was disgusting. ... a restaurant's bathroom says a lot. Let's just say, we learned I Sodi is NOT a high end restaurant, in many regards.

I came here with two friends on a Thursday evening.  We came from work 30 minutes before it opened and stood in line to get in.  They take reservations but only for the tables and there are not many.  We were seated when it opened at the bar and were put at the corner which was great.  They were also very kind and took all of our bags and placed them out of the way.  The food is Italian and excellent.  Our waiter was very knowledgeable and prompt in serving us.  There are only about 30-40 seats total in the restaurant.  It is very cozy and intimate.  We shared many plates which were more than enough but we wanted to try many things.  We loved the leek lasagna, fried artichokes, and lemon pappardelle.  The pistachio gelato was great and the tiramisu was more cream than ladyfingers.  I wouldn't wait months for a reservation as I found waiting and sitting at the bar to be great.

Had to check out this place with a girlfriend of mine to see what everyone was raving about! Definitely understand now! We started with the fried artichokes and then tried 3 different pastas. My favorite by far was the spinach & ricotta ravioli. The hint of sage in each bite was just heavenly. We also had the cacio e Pepe and lasagne a Sugo which were both great. My reason for only 4 stars is obviously because of wait time and difficulty making a reservation. However, after waiting two hours for a bar seat we had great service and enjoyed our meal.

Yeah, it was decent. Cacio e pepe was quite nice - as was the Negroni. Especially nice of the bartender to comp it simply because he forgot about it for all of 4 minutes (not at all asked for/expected). Meyer lemon pasta was not at all a crowd pleaser though and the two apps we got were just ok. Is it worth the insane wait/hype? Not really (imho), but it's fun to have done.
The lasagne is so mouth-wateringly good, I've been to Tuscany and tried the lasagne there and after finding I Sodi now I don't have to go back!

I have eaten at I Sodi 4 times before tonight's meal. I have had great meals and service after a long wait....but worth it. Tonight is another story, perhaps I ordered badly. But this still shouldn't be the case: the tuna starter that was "house cured" could have passed for canned tuna. The vongole in the pasta with vongole, were without shells and without the beautiful broth that is generated when cooked in shells. The sautéed spinach could have been frozen. All three and the fried carcofi were terribly over salted. If this was a restaurant in Providence, this meal would not pass the test of the local standard for Italian cuisine. I expect more from New York. Very disappointing meal.

One of the best Italian restaurants in NYC. Located in the west village ... the only downside to this venue is minimal dining space. Reservations must be made far in advance unless you get lucky as a walk-in. Good service and great food. Order the lasagna, you will not be disappointed.

Solidly good. I ate at the bar and was more than happy with the food and service. As one person, I would've loved a tiny bit more guidance in how much I was ordering (I took half my food out and gave away), but all in all delicious. And the bartender was a nice guy. Will be back soon.

Maitre d was egregiously bad. Dismissive attitude, unorganized, frantic and kept moving us around the restaurant. Would not explain what was going on and ignored questions when asked. It's a shame, as the rest of the wait staff were helpful and the food decent, but the awkward hostile interaction as soon as we came in ruined the tone of the night. Please find that man a more appropriate role.

After 4 trips to New York I finally got a reservation or the coveted "I Sodi" the only restaurant to deny my request for dining my 1 year anniversary dinner that was about 6 months ago. This time we got in on a last minute cancellation albeit at 10:30 pm, the last seating.

Bread: hard cold bread with olive oil, nothing special 
Artichoke salad: sour in taste, both agreed it was not good. 
Rabbit wrapped in bacon: gamey although the bacon did bring a pork note it was overall weird, would not order again. 
Lasagna: it was very good as the reviews state but honestly it was lacking ricotta which is a must in any lasagna and for the price it's easy to find better. 

We skipped dessert and went elsewhere since we know where this was going. Our waiter on a side note was great but there are plenty of other places to go in the west village for better Italian.

The most sublime pasta experience. Always start with a negroni and end with tiramisu, and never leave out that 20 layer lasagna. Such a refined yet relaxed vibe and absolutely memorable meal every time.

Very disappointing. My parents and I are all native New Yorkers who have moved out of town. My father came back for bypass surgery and I came back to support them with the operation. This was our last meal out in NYC before I headed off. We had a reservation that was a 3 hour wait. We decided to do it despite that being later than we wanted to eat. When we finally headed back to the restaurant the maître d chose that moment to inform us that our reservation was for bar stools. My parents being 83 and 84 could not physically sit at the bar esp. after my father's operation. The maître d said we could order food out and did not offer any kind of compensation for the fact he had actually made the mistake--I suggested that he could do something of the sort and he refused. Zero personal accountability. Terrible customer service.

*** ARROGANCE, NOT TUSCAN FARE, AT ITS FINEST ***

We gave this place a second chance last night, and it was even worse than the first experience. Dear Yelpsters, please allow me to explain:

On the first try we showed up without a reservation, and joined the queue about 20 minutes before they opened. We were able to get in and were offered 2 seats at the bar. The bartender was a bit cold and stand-offish, but we shrugged it off as the drinks were good and so was the food. Until dessert. I ordered the tiramisu, and was presented with: cheesecake. I wish I had taken a photo. I'm Italian and have eaten many versions of tiramisu, but this was literally a mascarpone cheesecake - a microscopically thin layer of sponge beneath 2 inches of thick, flavorless mascarpone cheese. Where were the coffee and liqueur elements? The ethereal texture? They were elusive! I nicely informed the waiter, with a gentle tone and a smile on my face, saying "I'm sorry, but this is a mascarpone cheesecake, not tiramisu."  

***** He said nothing, abruptly snatched the dish, tossed it in the garbage behind the bar, and proceeded to hand us our check. *****

Not a single utterance along the lines of "I'm sorry you were disappointed ... May I offer you something else?" Needless to say, that night, literally and figuratively, left a bad taste in my mouth!

Now, being Italian (and having been to Tuscany twice this year already), I'll admit it IS hard to find good Tuscan food in NYC, and since the pastas were acceptable that first night, we decided to give i Sodi a second chance. We showed up around 6 PM and put our names on the list, leaving our cell phone number with the maitre d. We then headed to one of their sister establishments, Bar Pisellino (Via Carota is the other), where we spent over an hour and consumed 4 drinks, which weren't cheap of course. During that time, we received a text message from i Sodi informing us that our table would be ready "in about 35 minutes" and asked us to reply with a confirmation. We promptly responded "confirmed," and awaited a follow-up text informing us that our table was ready. Well, about 40 minutes later we hadn't received that text, and so we walked back to i Sodi to see how much longer it would be. What happened next? Why I'm so glad you asked!

**** We were "greeted" by a CONTENTIOUS, HAUGHTY man, who said, in an annoyed tone "We texted you over half an hour ago and you didn't show!" Perplexed, we politely explained that we misinterpreted the "in about 35 minutes" text as a ballpark estimate, and expected we would receive a final text informing us the table was actually READY. A seemingly understandable interpretation don't you think? Well, upon offering that explanation and inquiring as to why they didn't send a follow-up text we were curtly informed "That is NOT i Sodi's WAY!"  ****

We walked out.

GET OVER YOURSELVES! You are NOT IMPERVIOUS to customer service. It will catch up with you. 

MY ADVICE: Avoid i Sodi, Via Carota, and Bar Pisellino, and patronize establishments that treat their customers like human beings.

Food is great and service excellent! The place is small but comfortable. Noise level is perfect if you want to have a nice dinner with a date, friends, family. I had the burrata special to start, lasagna and pesto special as main courses to share with someone else. All delicious!

Splendid!  Wine, sides, charming staff.  Rose took good care of us.  Devin served us with great suggestions, wine samples and lovely service at the bar. This place is delicious and beautiful.  Dare I say... perfect.

We put our name on the list at around 6 on a Thursday & waited about an hour to eat. This place is amazing!! The lasagna is phenomenal & the Cacio e Pepe was really great, too. Staff, ambiance, food, drinks...all amazing. Stop reading Yelp & just go. And while we waited we went to North Fork for drinks, which is very close by and equally as amazing. So please copy our night & I guarantee you'll end up overusing the word "amazing" like I have.

I only wish YELP WOULD HAVE SOMETHING FOR HORRIBLE REVIEWS!! NO STARS!

I ordered THE FAMOUS MEAT LASAGNA based on others reviews and spinach and had it delivered by CAVIAR who provides fast and excellent service as it did this time. They're not the problem. I SOLDI IS!! EXPENSIVE AND OUTRAGEOUS AND FOOD HAD TO BE THROWN OUT!!  

Though I requested extra sauce 3 x that I would pay for, NONE CAME!  The lasagna must have been reheated so many times there was barely any cheese or meat in layers, food was cold upon arrival ( not the delivery issue they were fast!), packed in the most unattractive cardboard boxes for $27 a serving!!! DRY SOGGY FOOD HAD TO BE THROWN OUT!! The spinach similarly was a cold dry heap even. Tho I requested extra garlic! Also thrown out AND THE TIRAMASUE WAS NOTHIBG BUT A SMALL CONTAINER OF BAD WHIPPED CREAM. ALSO DISCARDED!!! I won't order there again much less ever go to the restaurant!!!!!
If I could give this place zero stars I would. Rudest maitre d and service I have ever experienced. I'm genuinely surprised they are still in business. Don't waste your time and money.

I've eaten here before and the food is fine.  But I had the most atrocious customer service experience here, and it's really turned me off this place.  Basically the server, Eric, became extremely agitated extremely fast when I tried to ask how much longer it would be for a table - after having already been waiting for 3 hours.  I understand that working the door at a village restaurant on a weekend can get hectic, but to literally throw up your hands and yell "I'm done with you, you're not eating here tonight so leave" to a customer that's been waiting for HOURS is kind of ridiculous.  I think this guy thinks he's Maria Carey or something, because he has some serious diva behavior problems.

I Sodi... yes, you didn't disappoint but you also didnt live up to this outrageous expectations! Came here on a Saturday around 6pm to hear the wait is 2hrs, then I tried again today (Monday) with a 1.5 hrs wait. Ok I came around 1.5 hrs earlier than we wanted to eat so that worked out well. So, to summerize our visit: the food, yes it is good. Is the lasagna worth a 1.5 hrs wait and around 30 USD? Probably not. The lemon pasta was really good, my fav of the night. The service... yeah, kinda ok... but do you really serve a 21 USD glass of wine in the glass the customer just had tasted multiple different wines? I doubt so! 

Overall, our visit was a solid 3 but I would not consider this the best Italian in town although others might disagree. Would I ever come back? Probably, but not for a 1-2 hrs wait.

Had the best dinner at I Sodi last night. We'd been on the Resy waitlist for over a month for our 5th anniversary dinner, so I tried our luck and called the morning-of to see if they had any cancellations. Lo and behold, they called us back in the late afternoon and said they could fit us in. Felt like we'd won the lottery. When we got there, the maitre d was like "are you guys the anniversary couple?" It was very sweet. We ordered the fried artichokes (amazing), the heirloom tomato salad (very fresh, if not the most unique), the lemon pecorino pappardelle (to die for) and the Cornish hen under a brick with a side of broccoli rabe (amazing). The Nebbiolo was delicious, and my husband got a negroni and some grappa which he loved. The only miss was the tiramisu - definitely felt more like mascarpone cheesecake. I also asked the maitre d at the end of the night how best to get a res in the future, and he said to just walk in early on a weeknight and try to sit at the bar. The meal was costly because we splurged on booze ($220 with tip), but in the future I'd come back and just get pasta and wine and we could probably get outta there for half that for 2 ppl. Lives up to the hype.

I had been wanting to go to I Sodi for a very long time and it definitely did not disappoint. I brought my mother who was visiting from out of town and we managed to slip into two bar seats on a Saturday night after waiting maybe 15 minutes. The setting is intimate and classy and not too loud. The bartender was excellent, my mother wanted a cosmo and though he did not have a shaker he managed to mix up something delicious for her. We had the antipasto followed by the cacio e Pepe and lasagna. For a high class establishment in the West Village the portions were definitely sizeable and you could tell everything was homemade. The pasta was perfectly al dente and you could see the numerous layers in the lasagna. It was a wonderful experience and I would recommend to anyone wanting to try Tuscan Italian.

Omgosh get the pappardelle al limone!!! Soooo, so good. Beef tartar was amazing, as was the affogato. The service was quick and friendly. You need a reservation, unless you are early to stand in line for a spot at the bar.
There are only a couple of tables, and about 12 bar seats.

fuck this place!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! they canceled my reservation that i had booked for a month!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! i did not cancel my reservation, they did. i have called and emailed, no answer from the restaurant. if only i could give them 0 stars, i would. i was excited to dine at this restaurant but now i have no interest.

3 overall but a 5 for the lasagna. Definitely an overhyped restaurant...the difficulty of getting a table was not worth it. Great ambiance but has a little bit of a pretentious vibe. Overall happy that I went but I won't be going again.

Among the best Italian restaurants in NYC and believe me I've been to many.  We had an amazing fresh fish that was on par with any you'd get at any big name , huge price places.  Friendly and professional service just make it an all around pleasant experience.

I had a cringeworthy experience where I showed up on a rather empty Monday night for a 10pm reservation I had made. I waited until 10:15pm for a friend who was running late and once I checked in with the host a second time, I was told that the kitchen closes at 10:30pm and to see my way out. This is not how Rita Sodi's other restaurants are run in my experience and this host was extremely unprofessional and unwelcoming.

Pretty much my perfect meal. Had a nice arc to it. Beautiful and varied negroni list (Um yeah), mache salad was perfectly crisp, artichoke and parm salad simple and elegant. Steak tartare was best thing we had all night. Didn't make it past pastas. Pecchari was highlight. Amazing depth of flavor. All fairly priced. Varied wine list.

The restaurant used to be great, even a favorite, but something has changed.  They require a credit card to hold a reservation, which is fine, but even after cancelling my reservation they still charged me a late fee.  They won't respond to emails, calls, or texts.  There is a general aura of arrogance, and given the options in the WV, you can find much better Italian elsewhere.

Resis are so hard to get, but if you don't have one and have a little time and also are willing to eat dinner on earlier side...waiting outside roughly half an hour before the restaurant opens for dinner on a Sunday got us a spot in first round of seatings. 

From there service is quick so don't worry if you're hungry. We placed our order quick ahead of others who were still chatting and getting situated though, so that may be part of it. Service in general was great - waitress was attentive and helpful. 

We got 3 pastas: a pesto special, the lemon pappardelle and the cacio e pepe. I liked all of them, but my favorite was probably the pappardelle. My one complaint (particularly for the pesto pasta) is the noodle to sauce ratio is way off - sooooo much excess sauce and very little noodle! Was glad we ordered 3 plus an app - otherwise we'd be pretty hungry. For the app we got a simple burrata with tomatoes. Tasty/solid but also nothing unique. Next time I'd probably get more pasta instead ha. 

They're also known for their Negronis here so try one! We did and it was very smooth / refreshing.

I had not heard about I Sodi before going but all I knew was that it was very hard to get a reservation. I've had a lot of great Italian food both from other restaurants as well as from my family - and all I can say is WOW. Everything we ate here starting with the bread and olives on the table was incredible (I never knew red olives existed). 

My boyfriend got one of the many Negronis on the menu - not my cup of tea but he said it was great. We each got our own pasta and shared the lasagna. I got the lemon tagliatelle which was phenomenal and he got the Cacio e Pepe which was also delicious. Now - the best part - the lasagna. Hands down, best lasagna I have EVER had. I was so full halfway through but could not even imagine the idea of letting one bite go to waste. My boyfriend and I couldn't even have a normal conversation because we kept talking about how amazing the lasagna was. A must have.

Overall great experience. The restaurant itself is small so seats are limited but definitely try to get a reservation if possible!!

Super super solid place. Fried artichokes were delicious and I don't even like artichokes, and the pasta has extremely simple ingredients but is super high quality. The place is also quite casual so you don't need to dress up, but still has a nice vibe

Delicious but highly overrated and overpriced for what it is. Their "famed" lasagne was overcooked, leftover and was not al dente. The butter sage ravioli was too creamy with no hint of sage nor butter. The branzino for two was excellent. Fresh and the capers added crispy texture yielding incredible taste. Lastly, the arrogant service didn't help either.

It was so hard to get a reservation, so we decided to try to sit in the bar. We came here around 15 minutes before the opening on Saturday. There was already a long line, more than 20 people ahead of us, until opening, there were already more than 20 people after us. We can't sit in for the first round and were told around one and half an hour waiting. Around 6:30, we got the message to say that our seats will be ready around 7:00. At the end, it was pretty accurate. I appreciated it.

Once we were seated, the service was efficient and the food came quickly. I have to say the food was so delicious, simple but well executed. The ingredients were super fresh and had very high quality. The portion was generous, the price was very reasonable. The atmosphere was simple, minimal, I think every one came here mostly for food. So it may not be a romantic place, and since there were always so many people waiting, although no body rushed us out, we still felt not good to stay here for long once we were done. The sever was friendly, helpful and polite.

Overall, I think this is the best restaurant in west village and it is really worth the waiting and the money. I will definitely come back. If you can not get a reservation for table but still want to sit in the bar, my suggestion is that still come here as early as you can and leave your name and phone number, sounds like that their system is pretty reliable. But be sure to come early, because during our waiting for sitting in, it was around 6:45, the sever already told people who were coming in that next available slot would be around 10:00. Anyway, that was the case for Saturday, maybe some other time, the waiting is better.

Small space with a well done interior. Somehow rustic modern. Great details - various types of stone, warm woods, coffered ceiling. Even with a crowd it's pleasant and cozy. 

The staff is all delightful. Friendly, knowledgeable, responsive. 

The drinks are myriad and delightful. Classics and clever spins. 

Incredible menu mainstays and a rotating list of additions. All delicious. 

I die for their lasagna. It's exquisite. 

The fried artichokes are also a favorite. They're seasonal so get them if they have them. No regrets. 

Haven't had anything bad. Try all the food. Try all the drinks.

I never post reviews (this is my first one) but after our mind-blowingly terrible experience tonight, I feel like I have no choice. My husband and I were looking forward to this meal after so many positive reviews and recommendations from friends who, like us, love good food and wine. We were told it was better than Lilia and Misi (which are both excellent). SO NOT TRUE! I am disappointed to say this is among the worst overall dining experiences that I have ever had in my 20+ years in NYC. Every single pasta dish was overly salted to the point of being inedible. We sent back 2 dishes for being too salty and the staff didn't even seem to care. It was as if they were used to that reaction. (Even the people next to us said their favorite dish was the dessert, which is rather telling.) At no point was there any follow up or attempt to address these issues. DO NOT BELIEVE THE HYPE AND WASTE YOUR TIME AND MONEY! You're welcome.

I went to I Sodi around 5:45 on a Wednesday. There was no wait at the bar and we were able to be seated immediately. I had previously tried to walk in on a Friday around 8 pm, and was told there were so many people on the waitlist ahead of me they couldn't take more, so be weary. 

The restaurant has a cool ambience - there is a sliding door separating the waiting area from the restaurant to make visitors feel as if they are in an exclusive dinner club. 

We got the Artichoke Lasagna, Cacio e Pepe, and the nightly special side of Broccoli Rabe. The Cacio e Pepe was delicious, and had the perfect balance of creaminess and kick from the pepper. The Broccoli Rabe was excellent - cooked and seasoned very well. The star of the show was the Lasagna - it had many incredibly thing layers of noodles and it was so tender it almost cut like a desert. It was extremely delicious. We also got the bread - beware it is not free (it costs $2)!

Overall good food and experience - would recommend trying to go early on an off week night if you don't have a reservation.

For the love of God, this place is still going strong. 8 years once my first review and it's as delicious as day one.  Here's my tip of the day: I haven't made a reservation here in 5 years.  If there are 1 or 2 of you, they will always find room at the counter.  They will always tell you "30 or 40 minutes", but it's rarely that long.  Go have a cocktail somewhere in the village, let them text you when they're ready and enjoy.

My tip is to come as soon as they open the doors to get a space at the bar. I came 15 min later and was dismissed with a come back at 8:45pm. Eric the manager is the front face of the restaurant and he gives off a vibe that they really don't need your business.

Got there at 6:30, was told the wait was 2 and a half hours, decided to put my name down anyways because of the positive food reviews. Got a text at 10:30pm saying we would no longer get a table. 4 hours down the drain. Went back to the restaurant to double check and a handful of people were in the same boat as us and another couple who had made their reservation 2 months prior was there waiting 1 hour after their reservation time. On top of this the host was extremely rude and wouldn't answer anyone trying to understand if they would be seated. Quality of food is only half of the experience, service is the other. I understand it's a small place, but plan out your walk ins accordingly. It's a shame because the food is supposed to be great but I definitely will not try to go back

Food was good, however service was horrible. We had a reservation for 3 and when my sister got sick we showed up only 2 and the manager said we did not fulfill the reservation. He would not give us a table even when we made the reservation 30 days out at midnight. He said that we could sit at the bar only if there was availability. We were treated so poorly that we will not return. 

Also, for the food the cacio e pepe is good but not as great as Via Carota. The lemon pasta is NOT good--do not order.
