Horrible service and attitude. Good pastas and food. Overall, If you want to fight unnecessarily  hard for a reservation or wait 30+ minutes before opening to get a mini bar stool seat with bad service then this is the place for you.

Excellent, homemade Italian food that's unique and expertly prepared 

From the outside, I sodi certainly feels exclusive and intriguing. The halfway frosted glass makes it so that you can't see any of the guests. when you walk in, you're in an empty wooden alcove without a  host. Not a very welcoming entrance, but you see a glimpse of the bright interior and smell a whiff of the pasta and you decide it's worth waiting like everyone else.

We came on the Saturday night after christmas. We were told an hour and fifteen minutes wait and we were able to leave and wait for a text. It ended up only being a thirty minute wait. The bartender told us that Christmas weekend and July 4th weekend are the least crowded and best chance to walk in without a reservation.

I ordered a glass of wine and my boyfriend ordered a whiskey cocktail. He was so impressed by his drink. I took a sip. I'm not a whiskey person but it was so smooth, I would've enjoyed it too

We had two vegetarian dishes after exquisite bread and olives that they serve. The lasagne with artichoke bechamel was light as air and had countless layers of fresh noodles. The butternut ravioli (they used a fancier word) was so delicious, sweet and savory. Mad respect for the seasonal, unique offerings.

Can't wait to come back and see what's on the menu next time

The worst service I have ever received. The staff were incredibly rude and it is not with the time or the money. Do yourself a favor and go to one of the many other wonderful Italian restaurants in the city. I strongly recommend Rezdora as an alternative
Old neighborhood spot, gone downhill. Awful service (starting from the fascist reservation experience) with mediocre food. So many better options nearby - don't waste a meal here.

Sister restaurant to via carota.. I was a little underwhelmed leaving here. 
We ordered a bottle of quintarelli, it was their base level but I wasn't super thrilled with it. It also was a little warmer than it should be. 
Our pasta was a pappardelle, it was well cooked with a good flavor. We also split the steak tartare, I don't GET IT!!! It's definitely lacking in flavor, and seasoning. The quality of the meat was also very average. I was expecting more. 
Waitstaff was great, they made the experience even better than the food!

Gave it a try and waited in line for 30 min before opening.  Managed to get bar counter seats.  The food is simple, clean, and high quality.  We ordered wagyu carpaccio, white bean salad and cacio de Pepe pasta.  My favorite was cacio de Pepe.  The pasta is chewy and sauce was perfect to it.  I would like  to go back just for this even though you have to wait for 30 min outside.   Service was excellent. Wish it was easier to get a reservation!

What a dissappointment!! Waited a month for our reservation (which isn't easy to snag)and whEn we finally went, we were not impressed. We walked in and saw our open table, a waiter quickly told us to wait outside in the freezing little box "lobby", so we did after 10 mins of us fuming my boyfriend went back in to see I if we could atleast get a drink while we wait and not made to wait outside in the cold lobby like an animal, which they said NO! Wait outside, at that point I went in and asked what is the problem, we have a reservation and that's our table open!! The waiter with an attitude sat us. The food was average but the customer service is TERRIBLE!!! Do your self a favor and don't bother! So many other better Italian spots in the city. If you want great food and amazing customer service, head to Il Mulino downtown. NEVER AGAIN!!!

I went to I Sodi on Saturday for my birthday, NOT WORTH IT - and here is why...  The staff is rude and pretentious and they will treat you as if it's your PRIVILEGE to have a seat there. Sorry but no, this is NYC, we are not in the middle of a desert where Italian cuisine is sparse. There are WAY too many other fabulous Italian restaurants a stone throw away (Fiaschetteria Pistoia, for example, right across the street blows I Sodi out of the water) why would you wait to go to a restaurant with outdated décor, dirty bathrooms, and rude staff? Via Carota is the sister restaurant, with a  MUCH better all-around experience. I live right around the corner from I Sodi so putting my name down and coming back an hour later was not a burden at all and I STILL will never go back. The lasagna was definitely delicious but the waiter with the mustache and horrible attitude will be what I remember, not the lasagna. NYC restaurants are pricey and for these premium prices, premium service should be a given. Sorry I Sodi but like many other yelpers are saying - you are NOT worth the hype.

Finally got a reservation for I sodi at a decent hour and decided to try it out.

The service was impeccable, our server was very sharp, attentive, and very knowledgeable about the menu.

We ordered the indiva and tartara for our antipasti and for the entree, we ordered the Lasagne Al Carciofi Artichoke and Galletto Schiacciato.

Indiva- Amazing, GET THIS! this endive salad should win salad of the year. The parmagiano was so fresh the salad almost tasted like a cheese burger.
Tartara- Also amazing, the steak tartar had almost a caramelized onion taste to it.
Lasagne- this is where it got disappointing, I don't know if it was due to the layering of the pasta, or because it was a vegetarian dish, but the lasagne was mushy and only tasted like artichoke, nothing special.
Cornish Hen- Tender and juicy. I could cut this hen with a spoon; however it was not memorable and lacked flavor.

I had a reservation at 5:30 for 3 people at Isodi on Christopher street. We sat down with 3 people at a 4 person table. My friend had a work emergency and needed to have her computer on for 5 minutes before the meal began. The manager came over immediately and said she was unable to have the laptop out because this is a fine dining establishment. She said not a problem, totally understood, and left to go to the nearest Starbucks. That left two of us at a 4 person table. The manager asked us if she was going to come back and if she wasn't, he wanted to move us to a 2 person table. We said we weren't sure if she's going to come back but we would like to order anyway. He said he would not take our order because we were an incomplete party and that he had another party reserved for that table. He then let us know that the party he was referring to was coming at 7:30. We said no problem and we would make sure to be out before then.  We then said we would move to the 2 person table and we would tell my friend not to come back. Keep in mind, I made a reservation six weeks ago at midnight when the date came out and 5:30 was the only time available as it's very difficult to get a reservation. It is also a very tiny restaurant and 3/10 tables were occupied at this time. When we said we would move to the smaller table, he said he was very uncomfortable about the situation and I said I was too. He didn't let us move to the smaller table and asked us to leave. I asked to speak to the manager and he said I'm the manager Eric. I asked if there was someone else I could speak with or if the owner was around and he said no, then abruptly handed me their business card with their phone number after they told me they don't answer the phone because they don't have enough employees for that. I then received an email where they charged a $90 no show fee. Thankfully we were able to get a table across the street at Fiaschetteria Pistoia and it was great!

Some of the best pasta outside of Rome- incredibly flavorful and authentic! 

I don't understand why the Yelp ratings are so low. Everyone in the restaurant seemed to really enjoy their food. We certainly did. 

Started with the bresaola beef carpaccio which was good but skippable. Two of us decided to try three pastas because why not. We had the chestnut ravioli which was light and slightly sweet because of the chestnut, covered in a creamy sauce. A unique dish that's very hard to find outside of Italy so I'd recommend trying it. The lasagna al sugo was some of the best I've had outside of Italy as well- very thin layers and the perfect ratios of pasta to meat. This was our server's recommendation. My personal favorite was the cacio e pepe. I lived in Rome for three months and ate cacio e pepe almost daily. I Sodi's is the closest you'll get outside of Rome. It packs a punch flavor wise and the sauce is the right, slightly thick consistency. I will dream about this pasta. 

Bread is good but an extra $2. Coffee is good as to be expected. The tiramisu was also yummy. They have special appetizers and pastas of the day as well. Reservations are very difficult to get but the bar seating allows walk ins and it wasn't hard to get a seat at weekend lunch.

Why do people line up for this place? I mean it's a cute spot, posh interior but food was nothing to write home about. 

Thankfully i live in the area and got there around 5:20ish, 10min before it opens. There was already plenty of people before us, we were worried we wouldn't make it but the person before me was an incomplete party so we got the last bar seats (sorry but yay!). I'd say there's maybe only abt 10 or 15 bar seats.

We got the infamous cacio e pepe, spinach ravioli and chocolate ice cream. The cacio had good texture but was wayyyy too salty, almost inedible. Ravioli was fine but too much extra pasta and not enough filling, and it was also too rich. Ice cream was just meh. The place is a bit overpriced for what they offer.

They ask if you want bread casually but it's $2 extra. Always be aware! If an italian place asks if you want bread they will probably charge you. Most of them just bring them out. Also the server seemed very focused on upselling, constantly asking the diners if they want something else, like appetizers or coffee after dinner. He wasn't rude to us but was curt since we weren't having a big  meal. Also he asked how the food is when it literally arrived..? I mean it looks fine??

For some odd reason cacio takes 20mins here, and you will be informed by the server. I've never had a place that takes 20mins to do a simple pasta.

What is it about this place? Is it like hamilton? Just the fact that it's hard to get a reservation may be fueling/perpetuating the hype. A lot of reviewers warn you it's underwhelming and it is true. I guess waiting in line before the shop opens and waiting for 20mins for a salty pasta makes it special.

Plus their water glasses are exactly same as their candle holder. It is basically a vase.
The best lasagna I've ever had. Lived up to the hype! 100% worth a visit. Reservations are hard to come by and I can see why

Another diner mentioned the "egregiously bad" maitre d' ("Eric") and I could not agree more with that diner's review. We had a reservation and from the minute we walked in, he set a hostile and dismissive tone. We have been dining in Manhattan for years and as much as the "aloof" maitre d' is very much a New York thing, this was far and above anything we've ever experienced. He even went so far as to cancel our reservation--that we had for over a month--because he "did not like our attitude" (apparently based on nothing more than our appearance and a 20 second interaction where we informed him we had a last-minute cancellation to our party and would be 2 instead of 3). Arbitrary, disappointing, and infuriating, to say the least. 

In sum -- there are plenty of other top notch, similar restaurants in New York, including right here in the WV. L'Artusi, Via Corota (same restaurant group), and Rez D'ora (in Flatiron) are others that come to mind -- similarly difficult to snag a reservation, but the food is great and  the front of house will  not make you feel like he is doing you a favor by just acknowledging your existence. 

Hard pass.

It was so hard to get a reservation here and I admit I was a bit disappointed. I thought the ambiance was strange because there was zero music playing. 

My husband and I really loved the lasagna but we both got food poisoning from it. It was really a shock to get sick from something like lasagna ?
Food was amazing and service was outstanding. The only people giving this place a bad review is people who has to wait and didn't make a reservation. This place may be my new favorite Italian in nyc!

Came across this business thanks to a ny-based insta-foodie and we were lucky to find an open spot the morning of for a 5:30pm slot which was the first seating for dinner. We were super lucky because apparently you can only book 3-4 weeks out for prime time! Someone must have backed out last minute. Another way you can snatch a seat or two at the bar is to wait there. There was a massive, long line for walk-ins around 5:20pm. I believe some people started waiting since 4:50-5pm. But be aware that once the bar is filled and if you are in the back of the line, the wait to get seated might be as late as after 9:00pm. My best tip for you is to plan/book ahead and wait patiently (Credit card required to book).

Going right straight to the food. Their menu wasn't very extensive but they have specials and that's where the gems are. I couldn't miss out on the black truffle pappardelle ($39) because I mean, truffles! Best decision made that night because it was the best pasta I've ever had. The creamy pasta with an abundance of black truffle pieces (Refer to my photo) - it was made to perfection. Some might think it's overly creamy but you just need to put yourself into the right mind and put any diets you have on hold. Even though their meat lasagna was good, a customer favorite, the truffle pasta was on another level. Worth. the. money. We order negroni cocktails which was a nice compliment to our meal and they were pretty strong (+1).

Not sure how this place gets poor reviews. I've eaten all over NYC (and haven't left enough reviews sorry) and this is not only my top Italian restaurant (yes it stacks up with Italy) but also one of my top dining experiences in the city. Pick a friend or partner and put your name down for seating at the bar. It will be about an hour wait (I waited less than that each time). The service is exceptional, the drinks are top notch, and the food is next level. It's a professional dining experience without being pretentious. You'll be in awe just looking at the shelves of liquor you've never seen before. The crowd may suck a little but oh well that's what you get with such a quality dining experience. Can't dock a place for that. The lasagna, cacio pepe, and the truffle pasta (they don't tell you it's about $50 lol) are the top selections here.

I have only two nice things to say about this restaurant.  The host was nice.  And the fried artichokes were good.

Everything else about this place ranged from off-putting to unprofessional.  The first sign the place was actually a restaurant in Florence catering to American tourists was the $2 charge for bread, which was unstated until we asked specifically to clarify.  For a nice NYC restaurant (charging $46 for their branzino entree and $17 for cocktails) this is chintzy, and frankly just embarrassing (I guess the tourists don't mind?).  I mean, the bread was fine - it's not like it was homemade and came out warm from the oven.  Late in the evening we heard the people next to us enthusing to the bartender "thanks for that recommendation, it WAS special bread!" which means they had Stockholm syndrome by that point, or had never eaten bread before.  We couldn't decide.  For our part, when we expressed mild surprise about the charge the bartender told us haughtily that "it includes free refills" because I guess I Sodi is actually an Olive Garden? 

The thing that really soured the whole experience for us was the bartender, who was pushy and weirdly rude.  He rushed us from the beginning, including asking us what we wanted to order for food while I was still deciding on a drink.  Dude, we sat down five minutes ago, please relax.  Several times we asked him to give us a few minutes, to no avail, which created a really awkward vibe (why are you back here 1.5 minutes later staring us down when we are still clearly looking over the menu?).  When ordering, we were interested in the specials and when I asked him if their prices were in line with the rest of the menu he said "oh yes!"  LOL the special pasta was $39 on the bill, a full $15 more than the other pastas. Why not just say so when I asked?  He also brought out our appetizers just a few minutes after our drinks came, and the main dishes while we were still eating our appetizers, which I hate (why are you rushing us???) and without asking or apologizing, started clearing the appetizer plates while I literally still had salad in my mouth (AND ALSO TOOK THE SACRED OLIVE OIL THAT CAME WITH THE SPECIAL BREAD - DISASTER!).  One of the pasta's sauces had congealed, making it obvious it had been sitting out for a while, and both pastas were boring and not particularly good.  

After we put down our credit cards, but before signing the receipts, we were drawn into a short but intimate conversation and were speaking with our heads closely together for a few minutes, obviously deep in a discussion, and the bartender actually reached all the way across the bar to where the bills were sitting OBVIOUSLY UNSIGNED, and rifled through them - clearly trying to tell us to gtfo.  We ignored him but were actually kind of shocked that after paying $170 for two people we couldn't have five minutes at the bar to finish our conversation.

We were beyond turned off by the whole experience. WILL NEVER BE BACK but I hope all the tourists enjoy it.

Delish delish delish!!! Make sure to get the lasagna or the cacio e Pepe spaghetti! Everything is so delicious , authentically Italian, and perfectly cooked! I will be returning soon- Kudos to the staff who were so attentive and awesome even tho they had to work in 97 degree heat with masks on- you rock!!

Overpriced for the quality. The waiters aren't very attentive and service is very slow. Maybe because it's covid but they didn't have a lot of food options. The cacio e Pepe was alright. They also said we would only wait 15 minutes which turned out to be +45 min. I wouldn't seek this place out

Rude stuck up serving staff
Times are tough and when you are treated poorly-
Screw that 
I'll pass
Plenty of places with happy employees that need the work and want to be pleasant
So excited to finally get to try this place! Food and service was amazing! Highly recommend the lasagna and lemon pasta dish!

What a terrible letdown.

The bald man at the front could not be any more of an a**hole. 

The restaurant does not even make an attempt at making outdoor dining a comfortable experience during the pandemic. 

Our table and seats were on the part of a sidewalk that was angled and broken.  

Can you at least make an attempt to make your dining experience enjoyable especially when you are fancy restaurant. 

your food sucked. 
no diet coke or any soda. what a joke.

smh after eating at i sodi

Do not waste your time/money here. Was so excited to try it, but the staff was rude and the food was so disappointing.

The waiter was unfriendly and condescending when answering our questions about the menu.

We did not eat the majority of the food. The only item we liked was the beef carpaccio- diced meat with balsamic glaze- was definitely good. 

We got the fried artichokes also however, which were burnt and tasteless. We also got the "tuna" appetizer which looked like 2 cans of cooked tuna fish dumped onto a plate covered in oil. 

The vongole clam pasta we ordered was awful and I couldn't take more than one bite. It looked like chopped clams from a can were dumped into spaghetti with the syrup from the can as well. The sauce overly starchy and sticky. There were no shells in the pasta, it could not possibly have been fresh clams used. The taste was so bad- I've eaten clams all my life and the taste was as if they had gone bad. The bolognese was fine, but came room temperature not hot, and still for the reputation and price of the restaurant it was nothing special.

By the end of the meal we were so disappointed we asked the waiter (in a very polite way) if anything had changed recently because we felt the food seemed extremely off- in the middle of saying this to the waiter he curtly interrupted saying SORRY U FELT THAT WAY and walked away while we were talking.. it was extremely offensive and an upsetting way to end an already unpleasant dining experience. 

I actually called the restaurant the next day to explain what happened. They said the owner would get back to me, but they never did.

Walked up to the host working the door tonight and asked if there were any 2 tops available. He was not warm, he was very dismissive, and he did not approach me or my partner in a way that makes us want to make a reservation and come back. Times are tough all over NYC and beyond and the least we can do is be kind. Coming from someone who works in the nyc restaurant business. I only wish for this note to be a gentle reminder. Thanks

They are so anxious for business but as a single diner have never been able to get a reservation for 1. There
never  seem to be any tables for 1 ??

Had an absolutely horrendous experience with I Sodi.  I made a reservation using the Resy app on the day of the reservation only to be able to find out that I couldn't make. I tried cancelling the reservation and was then notified that it would charge me $30/ person for cancelling the reservation that I had literally just made. 

I live really close to the restaurant, so at 5 pm (2 hours before the reservation) I walked over to talk to them about cancelling it.  I was then greeted by a bald maitre d/ waiter with an arm sleeve of tattoos.  If you see this man, be ready to be treated like absolute garbage by someone on a weird restaurant power trip.  

He refused to cancel my reservation without charging the $30/ person (which, hey, I get that is the policy) but he then treated me extremely unacceptable way telling me that it was 2 hours before the reservation and acted like if I cancelled my reservation they were going to lose out on money.  There is no doubt in my mind they would have been able to fill the table with 2 hours to spare, while he acted like I was cancelling the table 2 minutes before the reservation.  

I left, keeping the reservation in hopes that maybe a friend could take it, and thought maybe if I pick up takeout from them at 7 that would suffice.  This way they can fill the table and make money from take-out... seemed like a win-win to me.  I went back and asked the same guy working there if this would work to which he then had a minor freak out and threatened to cancel my reservation right there and charge me the $60 without even the chance to fill the table or see if I could make it.  

Overall, I will NEVER be going back here and I recommend everyone stay away, despite how their food might be, based on their treatment of people.
Used to love this place, but they shouldn't do delivery if they...can't deliver.
$180 meal and the best thing on the menu was a $14 glass of wine... What an absolute let down! l artusi around the corner is infinitely better
This place was really good. Yummy food, great service. I would definitely visit again
Worth. The. Money. (Also got a little saxophone show with our meal for all the sax fans out there) Get yourself some i Sodi

I hate this place. Will never return. Made a same day reservation and cancelled within 5 minutes. Should not have caused any issue for them. Yet they still charged me a $60 cancellation fee. 

Tells you a lot about how they think about their customers.

While we would certainly have preferred eating in the restaurant, being able to order I Sodi's amazing food through Caviar is such a treat during the Pandemic. The bottled cocktails are simply wonderful. Until we can again go in person this is a wonderful option.

It's my second time at I sodi. First time was probably 2018-19, and had an amazing experience sitting at the bar, service and food was  great. The most recent experience is why I scored a 4, I booked indoor dining (before the official close of indoor dining in NY), it was roughly 32 degrees outside. When we approached the restaurant they notified us that their indoor dining is closed and to choose a seat outside, and said they confirmed with outdoor dining. As we chose our seat I proceeded to check the Resy app which stated indoor dining, but about an hour prior to the reservation I received a confirmation text, which I skimmed and confirmed. Not noticing the "outdoor" seating. FYI...supposably canceling would cause a 30pp charge. Seems like a table next to us were also shocked that they were seated outside.

sadly the same story with all the other bad reviews. They have a bad attitude.  No we are not privileged to be eating there. This place wouldn't last a day in Italy! It's quite amusing that the staff and I guess the owner thinks differently. 

Be nice!
By far the best lasagna I've ever had. Simply amazing. The ricotta and spinach ravioli dish was also amazing! I highly recommend the "Last Meal" dessert. Great food. Great service.

It is a beautiful day at the end of March and my friends and I are enjoying the high line. We are an older group of people, so we are not too crazy, but we decided to go to a bar to have a drink and continue our conversation. (Craaaazzeeee)

I walk in and look for a possible second bar and a gentleman follows/scoots behind me aggressively and lets me know that this "is a restaurant". I walked past the bar, and FULLY understand the difference between a bar VS a restaurant. However, this person obviously assumed I did not get what a restaurant is. He tells me that I cannot just walk into the restaurant, this is a restaurant and I told him that I was looking for a bar, I told him will pay whatever he wants and he again told my obviously ignorant self that this is a restaurant. RESTAURANT!

There is a pandemic going on, no one knows all of the restaurant rules, guy. Let's work together.

Nooooppe.

Now, I'm a military kid from the freaking Midwest. There is nothing agressive about my stance to my speech. I was even considerate as he fussed me out of "his" establishment. 

I don't know if there are too many brown people trying to sneak in to... Have a drink at a bar, but I was obviously the last straw. *Shakes fist to sky*

He huffs and pointed to a "bar" down the street who was more than happy to take our money. Because THIS IS A RESTAURANTUHGAWD! BAR PEOPLE ARE BENEATH EVERYTHING HE KNOWS!

Unless  you are into getting humiliated in front of your friends, I suggest not eating here and I would encourage other people who look like me to do the same.

Boo. I have been a hostess to a waitress while PMSING and I've done better on a worse day.

*Sigh* I want the restaurant to do well, It's tough times. so... I would still suggest this place. It smelled amazing (for a restaurant). Just don't go on a Monday night.. 

poor freaking form, dude.

I dined indoors. The staff seemed a little spread thin as there were only 3 people serving all the tables inside and out. I would highly recommend the lemon pappardelle, wagu app (bresaola) and the lasagna.
Great food and service! The chocolate cake was amazing, same with the pasta and other plates. Total respect for the servers dealing with all the people wanting to barge in and being rude about it.

Ordered takeout and it was pretty damn awesome.

Rabbit - Flavorful, tender and just amazing
Lemon Pappardelle - Went very well with the rabbit and mache salad 
Lasagna - I mean what can you say - rich, decadent - almost a savory dessert. 

Will def order takeout again!

Do not come here if you are nonwhite.  The food is great, but it's not worth being treated like a second class citizen.  

I had a reservation with a group of friends, all of which were black.  Some of our group was late and we couldn't be seated right away--fair enough, that happens all of the time.

But the host (and then subsequently the waiter) was  extremely hostile about it and it persisted throughout the night.  This is even though we were clearly on track to (and did) leave well before the next reservation.  We left feeling extremely uncomfortable and unwelcome.  

This is hard to express in a review because racism is more of a feeling, and if you know you know.  I'll just say I've lived in New York my entire life and I've never felt anything like that.

I'll never be back, and you should take your money elsewhere.

I'm disappointed to be giving I Sodi such a low rating, since I've been wanting to come here for over a year now, but the customer service was just appallingly bad. I was shocked, given how famous this place is. 

My friend and I came here around 6pm to put our names down for four, and were told that it would be 2-2.5 hour wait. About expected, based on what I've heard about I Sodi, so I told my two other friends (who were planning to dine with us) to arrive around 8:30p. About thirty minutes later, at 6:30p, we receive a text letting us know that our table would actually be ready at 7:30p, an hour early. Great! I message my two friends again, who are running errands in the city, to actually arrive an hour earlier than expected. Fifteen minutes after that, we receive yet another text, letting us know that our table would actually be ready at 7pm -- which was in fifteen minutes. My friend and I rush over while I try to call my two other friends to let them know that the time had once again been moved up. Both of them rush over, but the earliest they're able to make it on this last minute notice is 7:20p.

Meanwhile, the maitre d' (who is also mentioned in several other reviews) doesn't allow us in without a full party, and comes over to us multiple times, exasperated, to ask where our other two guests are. We tell him they are trying to make it as quickly as possible, given the two time changes, and at around 7:15 he says he will release our table. After some back and forth, he at least allows my friend and me to dine as a table of two, but on the way in, he turns back and tells us to "tell your friends they're not welcome at this restaurant."

Truly one of the most unprofessional dining experiences I have ever experienced. Giving it two stars instead of one because the lasagna is actually very good (the artichokes and gin martini are skippable), but not sure I'll be returning so long as the same maitre'd is manning the door.

Would give it zero stars if possible.  Made a reservations weeks in advance, received a text message day of reservation to confirm, we confirmed via text.  A few hours later, and a few hours before our 9pm reservation, we received an email from resy informing us that the reservation has been cancelled by the restaurant. No explanation, no nothing.  Tried calling the restaurant, no one picks up, tried emailing, no one responds, tried reaching out via social media, got nothing.  Don't waste your time with this place -- enjoy your time at a place that respects your time and energy.

This is New York. If you want to eat here you should 1. Have a reservation and 2. Understand that they will not seat you until your whole party is present. There are ten-ish tables and the host is also one of two waiters. They are working their butts off and don't have time for your shenanigans. We showed up for our reservation on time but one member was 20 minutes late. They sat us when he arrived and we had two hours from the time of our reservation to complete our meal which was still more than enough time. The bresaola, lasagna, pork chop, and cacio e Pepe were all delicious. Come here if you want amazing, authentic Tuscan food with a cute ambiance in the west village.

We came for my boyfriends birthday, and it was truly a special experience. The place is tiny, and has super cute West Village ambiance. The food was superb, and rivaled my other favorite, Babbo- also in the West Village. We got their fresh salad with balsamic, Parmesan, and olive oil- beautiful. The steak tartar, also tossed in balsamic which was an unexpected treat. We ordered the cacio e Pepe, which was the perfect blend of creamy, peppery with loads of fresh cracked black pepper, and the most amazing al denté bite for the actual pasta itself. The red sauce potato gnocchi- was perhaps the best gnocchi I've ever had. So light, fluffy, and deliciously delicate. I have made gnocchi myself at home, and it's difficult to make it so light by hand, the more you roll/knead it the more tough it gets. I Sodi's gnocchi was created with love, and it truly shows. Now the show stopper which initially called us here, truly lived up to its hype: the meat lasagna. WOW. The meat sauce is so deeply savory, with almost a creamy, velvety feel- absolutely incredible. Accompanied by their eggplant special, this was truly out of this world dining experience. For dessert, we ordered the panna cotta, and tiramisu. My boyfriend who does not enjoy desserts said the panna cotta was the best dessert he has had- ever, and I could not agree more. The tiramisu was so beautifully soaked in espresso, with a light fluffy creme on top- I accidentally ate most of it and forgot to share. In addition to this gorgeous food, the cocktails were excellent. Hendricks extra dirty martini for me, exquisite. For my boyfriend, a Negroni terra, which he loved so much he had 3. They check your vaccination card upon entering the restaurant, and honestly I was so happy they did. For the space being as small as it is, it wouldn't be fair to other patrons, or the excellent serving staff to be exposed to someone who isn't vaccinated (aka vax-holes). The lovely people who have left less than glowing reviews have clearly never been to a restaurant in NYC, let alone the West Village where every single place worth dining at is teeny tiny. It's common knowledge, if your entire party isn't there- they will not seat you. Why would they? Your party isn't respecting their valuable time, why should they respect yours? If you're putting your name down, it is common sense to go no more than 2 blocks away to wait for a drink, or literally to even sit on a bench. If they text you your table is ready, you need to be there within MAX 10 minutes- again respect the restaurants time. For the squad of people that were coming to this gorgeous restaurant, with such few tables, and uses the bar as extending seating for eating AND drinking patrons, one question; are you fucking kidding me? Schlep over to the east village and post up in a bar there, don't take up valuable seats at a RESTAURANT, a small restaurant at that, when you're looking to have one drink, especially during this covid/post covid life we are living. We could not have had a better experience with the service, the ambiance, and the exquisite food. I've already texted my bestie that we have to come here again, and I can't wait to be back!

Waiter was a complete cocky asshole. Rude, sharp talking, condescending, phony, and chauvinistic. Very very suprised they would hire someone like this.  Once we were done with our appetizers the entrees were on the table. Feel like they were herding cattle. 

Food is good and priced appropriately. However, so are many other places in nyc. Will not return.
In short, this place does not live up to the hype.  The pastas were bland and over-cooked (not al dente).  L'Artusi is much better overall.  The service was also terrible, led by a rude headwaiter.

Ordered takeout from here and the food was wonderful. 
We ordered all three of the lasagnas, the meat sauce was my favorite, the artichoke was tasty and unique, the cacio pepe was ok, mostly tasted like a block of cheese. 
The lemon pasta was phenomenal but the meat sauce pasta was just ok, I'd go for the meat lasagna over the meat pasta. 
The spinach side dish was delicious and came in a very generous portion size. 
Loved the food and will definitely be coming back to try to get a reservation.

Food is good but restaurant is overrated. Crazy they take no reservations and unless you know how to skip the line it is not worth the wait. They don't seem to have priority for regulars or locals either so really feels like everyone has to wait. Outside dining not comfortable with all of NYC's drifters and drunk elements constantly walking thru your dinner.  Inside is tight but intimate and still crazy busy because have to say food is good. Lasagna is special.

I wouldn't rush back compared to competitors in area. Meat Lasagna was good but seemed  old and dry. Also got the rabbit which was dry. Not worth the "hype". Still good customer service but wouldn't stress about going after trying good italian food in WV.

We thought the food was excellent but unfortunately we agree with other yelp reviews that the service was very bad. Specifically, the manager (who also served food) was rude and arrogant. Yes we know this is a highly regarded restaurant but there is no reason to treat people so poorly. Not only did we experience this but we saw him treat some other customers the same way. There are many other great Italian restaurants in NY so we will take our business somewhere else.

If I could give 10 stars, I would. In my 10 years in NYC, this ranks in my top 3 dining experiences, and my top 3 pasta spots.

From start to finish, the service was impeccable. Friendly and attentive without being helicopters, and great descriptions and recommendations for food and drinks--made us feel very welcome and at home :) (to the other reviews: we were a mixed race group, and did not experience anything but welcome)

They have 8 different Negroni's to choose from, but can make so many other cocktails. The best, though, is the Espresso Martini to pair with dessert: it's made with true, freshly brewed espresso; not an espresso flavoring in a bottle!

The Carciofi Fritti were some of the best fried artichokes I've had outside of the Jewish Ghetto in Rome--delectably crispy on the outside, but so tender and full of flavor on the inside. The special Mozzarella with Tomatoes was incredible, so flavorful and perfectly seasoned.

The pasta is the true star here. We ordered the Ravioli Burro e Salvia as the 4th selection, behind the 3 others we ordered, but it came out as #1! So pillowy and bursting with filling. The Pappardelle al Limone was also delicious, and you can tell the noodles are homemade--has a nice raw edge, and was cooked absolutely perfectly. The Linguine e Vongole was also very good, a little watery with the sauce and a bit salty. The Lasagne Bianca (Cacio e Pepe) was also good, but pretty dense--would try the standard Sugo next time, considering all the layers of (expertly thin!) pasta sheet + sauce you end up consuming in one bite. Kind of felt like a savory, saucy Lady M cake, with all the incredibly thin layers they managed to stack atop one another! A neat texture explosion in your mouth :)

Finally, the Flourless Chocolate Cake is one to save room for. I didn't want to share with anyone else, it was that good. A perfect balance of density and lightness, not too rich, not too sweet. Just exactly right!

My group of 4 sat at the bar around the corner: 2 on one leg, 2 on the other. It was the perfect arrangement to talk to each other as well as our waitress at the bar, and have a view of almost the entire rest of the restaurant. Highly recommend this seating arrangement for 2-4 people!

Can't wait to return to try alllll the pastas :) Thanks for everything!

This is the greatest Italian restaurant in NYC. It took me 11 years to find it and finally get in (got a table outside instantly), but I know now. The rumors are true. The hype is real. The pastas here are better than pastas we had in Italy.

The star of the show was the special pasta - a homemade thick pasta with pesto sauce. I wish I could eat this every week. The lemon pasta and the meat lasagnas are also outstanding, heavenly layers of thick pasta, deep and balanced flavors. Even their olive oil and bread is top-notch. Your tastebuds will go nuts.

Big shoutout to our server Chris who was jovial, kind, welcome - the whole package! 

5 stars!!!!

Had really high expectations for I Sodi that were quite honestly not met. While you could tell each pasta was made with high quality ingredients, they lacked a little something extra. My favorite dish was their Lasagna a Sugo (meat option), which had the exact ratio of meat, cheese and thin layers of noodle to make a perfect bite each time. It's the main reason for the 4 star rating, (plus the great service) otherwise I would have given I Sodi a 3. 

The Genovese was very fresh and has great chunks of Basil for a fuller taste in each bite, the Cacio e Pepe wasn't too rich and the Burrata was alright. The Fried Artichoke was also lacking a little salt but had a nice texture. 

Overall another good Italian in the West Village but it's really hard to compete with such amazing options in New York, so I wouldn't rank it in my top 3 per say.
Had a wonderful time with my wife last night. We usually go to Via Carota, but didn't find a table last night. The food was good and the service was top notch.

This is not a review of the restaurant per se.  But the management Doesn't know the "law" when it comes to Covid.  Arrived with a family of 5 after the manager called us with availability hours earlier (we had called earlier in the day and were told there was no availability, but manager was nice enough to call with an opening).  Manger said he could not take us given 11 year old was not vaccinated and they "didn't do 11s."  Went further to say it was NY law that they could not take an unvaccinated 11 year old.  So be it.  If that's their policy then that is their choice.  But don't say it's the law or be clear in what the policy is.  And don't be rude about it.  Like we should have known their policy when the website is ambiguous.  Every other restaurant we went to over the last several days took all 5 of us (4 of which are vaccinated; 11 year old kids cannot be vaccinated).  Cannot comment on the food or ambience, just disappointed to be excited to experience the restaurant and then be treated like we were in the wrong.

Good, not outstanding. I went here with two girlfriends and we were able to be seated immediately but went at a weird time (it was like Sunday at 5pm). We ordered Negronis (great), the fried artichokes (good), their caprese special (good), charcuterie plate (good/great). We also got the bread basket which was good but should be included instead of being an extra $2. 

For pastas, we got the ravioli, the Cacio e Pepe, and the pappardelle. The pappardelle was my personal favorite and all were reasonable in the low $20s. 

Food wise it was a solid 4/5 but the reason I'm deducting a star is because the host was horribly mean to a couple outside for seemingly no reason. They had a reservation for 3 people and apparently their friend got sick, they tried to call numerous times and couldn't get in touch with anyone, and showed up just the two of them. The host would NOT drop how they were supposed to have a third person and was just very snooty and rude about it. The couple was nice and seemed devastated that they had to be seated at a sad patio table outside. Then we get in and the table (for three) next to us sits empty the ENTIRE time. I just can't in good consciousness strongly recommend a place that treats patrons like that.

All in all good but you can get better food and better service in the vil

Teeny tiny Italian place in the village. If you get a reservation, it's a must. Intimate feel, wonderful pastas and excellent wine menu. Had the pesto pasta, a salad (farro corn etc summer salad vibes) and a red sauce pasta. Wonderful. I imagine dining at the bar would be especially lovely. Thank you for a wonderful meal I Sodi.

Absolutely the best Italian restaurant in NYC. Service is superb and the food is consistently delicious. 

Daily specials, no shortcuts, a wonderful atmosphere and very reasonably priced for the quality. This restaurant is a great  credit to Rita Sodi. 

Hats off to the entire I Sodi team, led by the indefatigable Alex, ably assisted by Chris, Devon, Danny and Luis.

Been trying to visit I Sodi for the last year. Finally got the chance when we got a 5pm reservation last minute of a Monday.

Really enjoyed the dinner but would only give it 4/5 given all the other amazing pasta spots out there in the city. Highly recommend the Fried artichokes and the Cacio e pepe. Thought the Ravioli was ok - given the spinach filling was overpowering vs a weak cream sauce. 

Would come back here again and try some other things on the menu - artichoke lasagna. Maybe in a year!

Heard lots about I Sodi and had it on my list for months. Was excited to try it and I wasn't disappointed but I wasn't wowed either. I definitely would be willing to go one more time and try a few dishes I didn't get to and if anyone suggested going here I wouldn't say no either. Didn't order any of the apps so I guess I'll try them next time. Here is my order:
Bread basket- I feel like I can tell a lot from a restaurant based on their bread. Nothing special if you ask me. Wouldn't eat it if they brought it out again
RAVIOLI BURRO E SALVIA- Now this was amazing. I loved this Ravioli and I could've eaten the entire thing without sharing it. The spinach tasted fresh and the sauce delicious. I know a pasta is good when you eat it yet it doesn't taste heavy. No question best thing on the menu and would rate this dish 5 stars
Tagliatelle- They don't have this on their online menu so I don't know the exact name but it was with caramelized onions and parmesan. the initial bite I was like okay but by the end of the bit it leaves a bitter after taste. The onions were starting to taste burnt and I couldn't finish it. My friends liked it but it just wasn't for me. 
LASAGNA CARCIOFI- Now the waiter told us the Lasagna Cacio e Pepe was very rich and veered us towards this choice. I was very impressed this restaurant had not one but two vegetarian lasagna choices. We all had an initial bite and were like yes, awesome love this. By the 4th bite you're over it. This one was very rich as well and definitely a dish worth ordering but not a dish to have on your own. 
Cacio e Pepe- Now cacio is my classic dish (as it is everyone's) that I order at every restaurant. I have to say, they did it well. It was good, it was great actually. It was the perfect balance that cacio e pepe needs and I was definitely happy with it

final consensus- I would go back. I liked it, it's a solid choice but I didn't love every option I had ordered. I will give it another chance for another star if I order all the apps I wanted & the other pastas and if they make a good impression.

Service attentive and food was delish. Looking forward to going back. 
We ordered:
meat lasagna- 5/5
Steak- 4/5 but husband loved it 
Beef tartar- 4/5 ( Lafayette's is better) 
Ran out of time to order dessert, we had a play to catch. Next time!

Definitely good food, but not out of the world. 

Fried artichokes were amazing! Highly recommend getting this if you can. 

Cacio e Pepe: not too creamy, but perfectly balanced. Nice amount of pepper and flavor 

Lasagne: nothing too special

Rabbit was a bit salty, but definitely would get again if I come again.

As many others have pointed out, the service of this place is appalling for a restaurant of this caliber. I can say I have not been treated this poorly in any restaurants in NYC of the same caliber or less. Truly appalling the management of this restaurant would allow its customers have this kind of experience.
This place is way overhyped. The host was rude (our waiter was nice though!) and the meal was average but we paid a premium price for it. Save your money and go elsewhere.

Yes it's worth the hype. Lasagna al sugo is an 11 out of 10.  Lemon paparadelle very good.  Branzino very good. Fried artichokes outstanding.  Burrata with truffles ( I'm not a huge fan in general) was loved by the rest.  Flourless chocolate cake outstanding.

The cocktails here are amazing. I was a huge fan of the Manhattan with an Italian twist and my date enjoyed his Negroni. For starters, we ordered the beef tartare which was one of the bests I've had, perfectly lean, chopped and paired with fresh greens and also ordered the white truffle burrata which was so unique! For mains, we went with the oxtail wide whole wheat pasta special which bursting with flavor and the Tagliatelle Con Cipolla which had the perfect amount of Parmesan.  Great quality pastas here, loved the vibes, would come back!

Truly a disappointing and frustrating experience. The bread was stale, the olives were tasteless. No matter how badly you want the buttata - you will regret ordering it. It was the tiniest thing I've ever seen & was way too liquid- may as well have been milk. The pasta portions were great but was under seasoned and bland. It took way too long to arrive and service was sub par. Experience leaves overall so much to be desired for a place that has garnered so much attention.

Writing this review months after my visit because I still dream about the lasagna. Service was awesome and the Negronis were amazing definitely go out of your way / make time for this experience of a lifetime. 10/10 would recommend

Very disappointing as I had this restaurant on the top of my go to list.  Was so excited to get a last minute reservation as it was a celebratory occasion with my daughter. 
The food itself was okay, nothing special and left us feeling the opposite of what we felt when we booked the reservation.

From the minute we walked in,  I can't say that we were greeted by the door because it was not welcoming at all.  Seated by a table near the door where the cold air kept blasting in everytime the staff went in and out leading us to where our coats during the meal.
We were excited to have the cacio pepe lasagna (one of the main reasons we wanted to go) only to find out it wasn't on the menu that night. We were told the specials and ordered the burratta with truffle and honey.  Buyer beware... it was a tiny piece of burratta with no hint of honey on it.  The bigger shock was to discover the price of it when I received the bill.  Please, if you do go here, ask the prices of the specials and note that they charge for bread and olives!
During the course of the meal a shard of glass broke off and cut my companions two fingers leaving her bleeding.  We called the maitre'd over and he asked, 'how did that happen' in what I felt was an accusatory tone.  Like I carry around bits of glass in my purse. 

They did bring out band-aids and checked on us but was disappointed that there was no recrimination on their part.  A we're sorry was no where to be found.  Can I get you a drink or dessert on the house for this, nope. NOTHING.  


So we left, disappointed, cut up, and with a totally opposite feeling of the excitement we felt when we made the reservation.
Bread is wheat: why? Wine menu was difficult to read (the font). Food was good. Truffle options were fine. No matches :/ AOC was eating at the bar, not sure it was her vibe.

It's all about the noodle.   Perfect Al dente pasta served simply to really let the pasta shine.  Shine it does.   If you want classic Italian American fare- this is not your jam.  No red sauce to be had.  If you want expertly made pasta, delicious appetizers (baby artichokes) or solid secondi dishes, this might be your jam. Don't sleep on the drinks either.  Had the best sazerac outside of New Orleans and the best Negroni.  Place is charming and a little sexy too.   One of the best meals I have ever had.

I sodi is a very expensive, small italian restaurant in the west village that is basically impossible to get a reservation for. If all that scares you off you shouldn't go. IIf it doesn't scare you off, I sodi has some of the best, most authentic italian food I've had in the city and I genuinely look forward to going there.

Starting off, I recommend getting to the restaurant right when it opens and putting your name down to dine at the bar. Some days are busier than others, but if you don't do so you probably won't be able to dine there.

Food 4.5/5: I Sodi food is expensive but they're a few dishes they do extremely well. Appetizers wise, all the options are good but they're extremely pricey and imo the only option that is really worth it is the fried artichokes. When it comes to entrees, I sodi makes an amazing cacio e Pepe that's a must have. 

Service / ambience 4/5: Classy but cozy restaurant feel and the servers are very professional when you get inside. However the process of having to get into the restaurant (lining up, leaving your name, etc.) given the lack of reservation availability isn't the most pleasant so docking a point for that.

This place only takes reservations EXACTLY two weeks ahead (which I learned from studying Resy and finally getting ahold of someone to say the same).  So I stayed up till midnight to snag a reservation for the date I needed. 12:01am - no reservations available. 12:02am - same thing until 1:00am. Next morning, still nothing. I tried to call both numbers over and over and it said you couldn't leave a message. So I emailed and got an excuse that didn't acknowledge the question I even asked. I know this place is small, but it also seems like because they are full every night, they can be rude and have no customer service at all. I spent hours of research reading reviews for nothing.

My sister and I have been trying to get a reservation at I Sodi for a while and have been unsuccessful. After being rejected from multiple restaurants in the area, we thought we would attempt to walk-in around 5pm on a Saturday. We were greeted by Chris, who was very friendly and put us on a waitlist (!!!). After only about 45 minutes, we got the text that our table was ready. Much to our surprise and delight, Chris was then our server too! He made the entire experience amazing for my sister and I. Outside of the fact that the food was delicious, its worth stopping by and asking for Chris if you want to add some charm to your evening!

So I've never actually heard of this place as a New Yorker however, it's obviously hard to hear of every single establishment in this great city LOL

My cousin and I scheduled a very very last minute date to meet up and she was recommended this place by a colleague. The place opened at 4, she got there at 5:45 (i was sitting in my car to avoid a ticket) she texted me that all tables were full and there was a 2 1/2 hour wait. I told her no way that's ridiculous and let's just sit at the bar. Bar was FULL

We were immediately disheartened and ended up going somewhere nearby (I will not disclose where since this place deserves its credit) Anyway plot twist, we were going to hit a bar and she shows me a text from I Sodi that a bar seat will be available in 10 mins. We took this as a sign and went right back!!!

Though we had just ate, once you step foot in this place, the AIR alone, you can test the food. It was like nothing I'd ever experienced. So, we ended up ordering the spinach ricotta ravioli (we shared it was about 12 nicely stuffed raviolis) and we ordered the bread. This ravioli, IS THE BEST RAVIOLI I've ever had in my entire life. (And I've had my share!!!) it was light, it was fresh. The bread and the OIL! Omg. Amazing. 

We paired it with a Negroni Terra (recommended by our awesome bartender/waiter Chris) absolutely delicious and will be coming back once I try and get a reservation!! 

**definitely try and book a reservation first

While I Sodi remains one of the hardest restaurants in NYC to get a reservation, the lasagna is so worth it. Intimate atmosphere but great vibes and service, not snooty like some tough to get in NYC restaurants.

Finally made it to I Sodi. Everyone talks about how hard it is to get in here but if you are willing to walk in late on a weeknight and wait 30-45 mins, you will probably get lucky. I also just kept an eye on reservations on Resy and there were usually last min reservations available. 

Anyways the food was amazing, all pasta was homemade and perfectly cooked. The Toscano anitpasto was an a solid starter if you like fresh Italian meats and cheeses. 

For what it is, the price is reasonable.

Atmosphere very homey and quaint.

I truly don't know what there is to say about I Sodi that hasn't been said. This place is amazing! I'd argue that their ravioli is the tastiest I've ever had. Service was amazing, the food quality was so good. Ordered 5 pastas and a cake for the 4 of us and it was just about enough (we could've got more though honestly). Hard to get a reservation but if you get one please go!

Favorite Italian spot in W Village. Yes, it is small so you might not get a reservation but, try! And if you can ever get one of their aged nagroni's nobody does them better. Make sure it's the aged one. But don't do what I did and have more than one, unless you can handle it ;)

I wanted this place to live up to the hype so bad but sadly I think there are far better options in the city. A reservation to I Sodi is quite elusive so you could imagine my surprise when I got to I Sodi prior to opening and was able to snag a coveted seat at the bar.  The steak tartare was the best part of my meal and was tasty but I've had better (ah- so not trying to sound pretentious here but I have!) For main I had the ravioli which was lackluster in taste. Opting not to order dessert I was quickly given my bill. No time to even digest but they want to turn a seat over to another patron that's dying to try a restaurant that's all hype and no flavor. A hard pass for me.

The food was very good, however our server was very unfriendly. When we asked for suggestions, he seemed impatient and provided none. The table next to us had a fabulous server. Service makes all the difference.

Chris was amazing and so accommodating when we wanted to expand our reservation due to a last minute cancellation. He really took the time to make our experience memorable. The food was excellent--lasagna sugo, cacio e pepe, and tiramisu were the standouts for me!

Got the burrata, red lasagna, and lemon pappardelle. Everything was really good, but the reservation being so hard to get did set my expectations a bit higher. Would go back but wouldn't wait up until midnight to get a reservation again

Where do I start?
Horrible service great lasagna. After a day of sightseeing, headed to the restaurant hoping to land a table for 2 (no reservations). 

Upon arriving we were greeted by a server. I inquired about a table for 2 and was told the wait was 2-2.5 hrs.  I decided to place a togo order. 

Once we put the order in. We were told by the server it would be about 30-35 mins for our order.  We decided to take a walk around the neighborhood. We headed back to the restaurant 25 mins later. 

As we were waiting outside, a couple walked up stating they had no reservation and wanted to see if a table for two was available. The same server informed them that in fact a table was available.  As the server was getting the couple's table ready I confirm with them what I just heard.  

After the server seats them he comes back out to give me an update on my order.  I ask, "what happened to the 2-2.5 hour wait. It's been 25 mins?"  To which he answers, "a few reservations didn't show up."  I then ask since our order isn't ready could we be seated and have our meal inside the restaurant.  The server  informed me that, that wasn't possible. He wasn't able to make the change.  The icing on the bad service cake. As we waited, another couple walked up. 

You guessed it, "we don't have a reservation and wanted to see if you had a table available?"  The same server, "give me a second and I can get you seated."

Honestly, I would have cancelled the order as the tone and attitude was horrible.  Unfortunately, I had already paid.  

We grabbed our food and headed back to our hotel only to find no utensils in the bag.  

The lasagna was good. I'd pass on the cacio e pepe.  However, all of this was completely overshadowed by the service.  

In the end, I wish I had read the reviews prior as this seems to be an ongoing issue with service.

A resounding yes on I Sodi! Worth the hassle of getting the reservation. 

We started with the artichokes which were amazing! They were beautifully light, with each leaf separating into crisp layers, while the heart was soft. I would definitely order this again. 

For mains, we ordered a special porcini lamb pasta and the meat lasagna. I really liked the porcini lamb pasta (it tasted much better than it looked). The pasta came in these wide sheets that picked up the sauce well. The lasagna was also great and I enjoyed that it wasn't too saucy. 

We finished with a flourless chocolate cake. Decadent and creamy, without being overly sweet. Definitely a great option, especially if you're impartial to chocolate, but otherwise it might be trying something else on the dessert menu. 

It can be difficult to get a reservation here because it's such a small space inside, but I really enjoyed the experience! I'd love to come back soon.

I and two friends with an Italian background enjoyed I Sodi. Appetizers were OK+, pastas were very good, and, unfortunately, deserts were a complete disappointment. The meat lasagna and a special pasta with mushrooms and lamb were the highlights.

Service was fine and dinner for 3 with 3 drinks, 3 appetizers, 3 pastas and 2 desserts was $233.54 (20% tip included). This was very filling and we took some of the pastas home, although we each only ate a few bites of the two desserts we ordered because we didn't care for them.

Super disappointed... came for the much hyped lasagna and it was served cold. I told them all they tried again and parts of it were still cold... They must be cooking it earlier in the day or the night before or something and maybe even freezing if and then thawing it out / like microwaving it. Really unbelievable maybe it was some weird night or something.

I Sodi he's been one of my favorite restaurants for years.  The food is next left and staff top notch, but I'd like to take a moment to gush over the simple, understated and outrageously chic interiors.  The use of natural woods and stone is a master class in it doesn't matter if something is simple of the materials are high quality and love and devotion goes into their selection.  The fluted glass partition at the entryway and in the front window allows light to enter while maintaining this meca of fashionable dining's intimate and private vibes.  The blown glass light fixtures are what I must assume murano and a nod to the owners Italian root.  My only negative is the chair selection for a space that is so tight, the chairs wood back wrap around and pretty imprison you to the table which isn't the worst place to be but makes it a feat of acrobatics just to get in and out of.  Still hands down one of my favorite dining experiences of all time and I will always and forever dream of the fried artichokes.

First off, I did not make reservations. Therefore I can't say that we would've gotten the same seats but either way it's extremely tiny in there. We were at at the bar, and the actual tables were empty our whole duration of our dinner so I'm not sure why we couldn't sit there but the bar was so uncomfortable. We were squished between people and we were celebrating a birthday so I wished we had a more intimate setting but we truly wanted to try this place. As you see in the picture we had order some
Meats and cheeses, they didn't cut up the cheese and it was extremely difficult to cut. The honey was slabbed on a plate usually it is served with the honey comb. No crackers or different breads were served with the antipasto. Though the meats were great. The pasta! Oh how delicious and fresh! So hot you couldn't even eat it but that's great! Just shows how fresh it is. But it was delicious food. I don't think we will return though.

The rating of this place is absolutely not true, this is one of the best Italian places in all of New York and should get a 6/5 stars. Incredibly amazing service, fresh pasta, and great cocktails. 

Highly recommend the tomatoes & burrata, the lasagna, and the eggplan parm. 

I will be coming back!

I dined at I Sodi three years ago and it quickly became my #1 restaurant in NYC. The intimate atmosphere, amazing food and drinks- what else's can you ask for? Here I am coming again to NYC for my birthday and of course I would like to celebrate at my favorite spot. I spent 3 months monitoring their openings for reservations (the place is very small and it is hard to get reservations). I finally got a spot for prime time on the night before my birthday! I told my son all about it: we talked about the menu and we're excited. We arrived 15 minutes early to be greeted by not so nice host. There were three of us: my husband and I and our 3 year old who had been looking forward for this special treat. The host kinda gave us a look but I figured he was just cold getting out to greet us and didn't pay much attention. After about 7-10 minutes he said the table was ready and asked for our vaccination cards. Both my husband and I provided ours and then he asked for one for OUR 3-YEAR OLD SON! I explained to him that he can't get vaccinated yet (I wish!) but the host in quite mean way told us that since our son is not vaccinated, we can't dine inside!?!?!?!? Excuse me? He did offer to seat us outside but their outside area is pretty horrible and there was a huge pile of trash just next to the restaurant entrance, not to mention it was 30 degrees outside. I asked the host to talk to the chef a.k.a. the owner but he immediately said it will not change anything, this is their policy. It not listed on their website. I believe this host merely discriminated us because we had a child (well behaved and with a great taste). Not only it is against the law to discriminate based on age but it is also a bad business practice. I am sure they don't care they lost one patron out of the city but I hope my review will keep some locals out as well. Stay away from this place.

I dined at I Sodi last weekend. Admittedly, it's hard for I Sodi to live up to it's immense hype, but they truly excel in certain areas (but lack in others). 

As expected, the lasagna and pastas were wonderful; these are some of the best in NYC. In addition, we really enjoyed the tartare and ricotta special. That being said, the artichoke salad and short rib weren't great, and although a small compliant, the bread was served cold.

Additionally, although nice, the wait staff is clearly in a rush to get you served and out the door.

I recently ate at I Sodi after reading an article about it in the Times. I knew it would be busy after reading the reviews and finding no available reservations. After failing to obtain one, I decided I would just walk in and take my chances. 

Pappardelle with lamb
Coniglio in panchetta

Maître'd 45 minutes. Said would text. After 1:10 no text so decided to check in. I waited right by door and with no courtesy said miss can you please wait outside. After another 15 minutes he summoned a couple to their table and giving me a blank look asked if he could help me. I said you put my name in about an hour and half ago and told him my name. Said "I texted you, you didn't come so I was about to give your table away" I looked at my phone, text from 3 minutes ago. I just got it. 3 minutes!!?? After waiting an hour and a half? 

Cocktails not impressive. All the food so salty.

Loved everything about it.  Fresh, crazy delish food in an intimate and friendly space with tasty cocktails and a solid wine list.  Shannon at the bar had great recommendations and made all feel at home.  The team clearly has earned all the fanfare!   #TheFutureIsFemale
Absolutely delicious and wish I could eat here more. Tough to book but worth the trouble

Dinner for two at the bar with less than a twenty minute wait?  Yes, please!  I have been hearing/reading about I Sodi for years, and actually feel bad for restaurants like that because impossibly high expectations can be hard to satisfy.  We went in absolutely thrilled to be there and excited try the food.  Service was friendly and sans attitude. Towards the end of our meal, the bartender was lost in the weeds and everyone at our end of the bar had to wait for a variety of things.  In the meantime, it was fun to watch prospective diners timidly enter the dining room only to be tossed back into the vestibule of shame by the unflappable host.  

The dining room was warm and intimate, with a pleasant buzz.  Excellent negroni to start, great bottle of wine, and then the food...some hits, some misses.  Bread service got things off to a great start - loved the salted and peppered olive oil for dipping, and the delicious olives.  Steak tartar blew our minds - maybe the best ever?  But the artichoke salad reminded why I wasn't such a big fan of artichokes to begin with.  The ravioli completely satisfied, but the lasagna will reign supreme as the biggest dining letdown this year.  After seeing photograph after photograph of its beautiful, bechamel slicked layers, imagine our disappointment to find it completely dry and un-voluptuous.  And the tirimisu was worse - way too much mascarpone, way too few boozy ladyfingers.  

We were almost won over by I Sodi, but Il Buco kind of serves the same purpose, and it's not impossible to get into.  We came, we saw...
Bomb lasagna with an insane amount of layers.  All other dishes looked beautiful.  Great bar too.

Best for a weeknight dinner. Loved the interior: dark wood, bar seating, small space and perfect sound level. Portions were very generous and everything tasted great! Found the lasagna slightly too dry to my liking but still very enjoyable.

Well, I gave management at I Sodi over a week to reply to my kind email, in which I requested a phone call regarding the exceptionally poor service we received on 9/18. Not only have I not received a call, there's yet to be a reply to my email. Quite inhospitable for a restaurant of this caliber. 

We were a party of 5 with a 445pm reservation for my parents' anniversary. They were super excited to come to NY and celebrate at I Sodi, as they had only heard wonderful reviews. Unfortunately, our experience was far from wonderful. We arrived promptly at 440pm and immediately felt a pretentious energy from our server, George. It seemed as though we were doing him a favor by dining there and that feeling only escalated throughout the remainder of our meal. His only goal seemed to be getting our order to the kitchen so that we could leave as soon as possible. About 5 minutes after sitting down, he came to our table with a minimal greeting and asked what we'd like to order. We told him that we were still reviewing the menu and needed a couple of more minutes. Within 1-2 minutes, he came back again asking, and we replied the same. He proceeded to stand at the table, visibly looking at his watch until we were ready to order. The energy at the table was tense and we were just panicking trying to pick menu items so we didn't have to go through this cycle yet another time. We picked about 4-5 starters and he requested our full order, which we hadn't fully decided on because we'd only been sitting down for a few minutes. I must add that we were not taking an excessively long time so this behavior was completely uncalled for and unprofessional. We were concerned the food would all come out at once, but he reassured us that the kitchen would pace it out so there was nothing to worry about. After the appetizers, the 2 pastas, 2 main protein dishes, and 2 sides that we'd ordered all came out at the same time, which was exactly what we were advised would NOT happen. George had absolutely no trace of hospitality in his demeanor and was clearly trying to turn our table as fast as he could. My entire family left feeling as though we should've dined somewhere else and avoided that entire experience, which we'd felt from the start was going to be disappointing. Unfortunately the poor service overshadowed the food, though the food was also not as good as we were anticipating. $600 later and I will never be returning. Very unfortunate!

I wanted to love this place so much, but it just didn't live up to the hype. It's super hard to get a reservation, the acoustics in the space are a nightmare, and the food is very meh. My husband and I ordered quite a bit, including the lasagna, didn't really like anything, and took nothing home. Maybe it was an off night, just seems too far off from what I expected for it not to be?

I visited I Sodi with a girlfriend during a weekend trip to the city. We were able to get seats at the bar right away and the service from the bartender was fantastic! He was able to recommend wonderful wines to both of us based on what we were looking for. He was also helpful when it came time for our meal selection - ensuring we picked options that paired well together.

We split everything and my friend even had some leftovers that she was able to bring home for dinner the next day.

You can't go wrong with Cacio e Pepe - it was one of the best I've had! We also HAD to try the lasagna after seeing it all over Yelp and it did not disappoint. I would definitely visit here again and either get the same dishes or try something new - the menu had plenty of options!

Where to even begin with this restaurant's absolutely horrendous service. It was enough to make me make a yelp account today. I'm genuinely and generally and extraordinarily patient person when it comes to dining because of my personal experience in the space. All I can say is please take your business to any of the other local Italian destinations and spare yourself the 50% chance of the service/staff ruining your evening. No amount of pasta can replace the sour taste in your mouth after the horrendous experience I have had across 2 reservations at this restaurant. Its disgusting to think how much support a place can get from hype all the while treating their customers like filth.

Today:
Figured I'd give them a second go...special occasion, friend who really wants to try out this place based on word of mouth etc. Was told by a colleague that they had an explicit "talk" to improve the service experience. Well this is how THAT went today....Have a reservation here that you made literally after hours of stalking Resy? Better respond to their reservation confirmation call during work hours within 15-30 seconds. Oh you missed it? Well you can't call back because neither of their phone lines get answered ever. Then they UNILATERALLY CANCEL your reservation moments later with no notice 2 hours prior to seating. Is this a joke? Tried to resecure it on Resy but its gone. Gave them a chance to make it right by sending a polite email. No response. The ineptitude is startling given they charge $30/pp for no shows anyway and fill their no show tables every night with hopeful walk-ins.

Prior experience:
Show up 10 minutes prior to reservation. Don't get seated until 40 minutes after. No apologies, no updates - just "please stand outside" in the summer heat. Ask for a recommendation for a bottle of wine and the only suggestion is a $600 bottle followed by rudeness when your table politely selects an alternative bottle. Its not like we didn't spend over $100 per person in the  time we were there for authentic but horrendously overpriced food.

This restaurant will never amount to true acclaim beyond the occasional paid-for article in the Times or elsewhere to generate hype alongside the elusiveness of a reservation here. I won't name any of the specific staff 

I highly recommend checking out local alternatives that have done such a good job that I continue to come back to over the years: Rezdora, Don Angie, Via Carota, Fiaschetteria, (or for a less traditional experience: Lilia, Misi, L'artusi, Carbone). ALL of which Ive have had better food AND experiences at.

We walked in on a Saturday night and got there just before they opened at 4. We were seated at the bar and thrilled to have gotten in. I had high hopes for this restaurant; but it was really good, not great. Service is wonderful and wine is good. The pasta is divine but heavy. Don't skip dessert- you can't go wrong!

I ordered take out tonight. A quite good primo. The staff were very welcoming even though it was busy. At one moment during my minute long wait, the maitre d walked by with two glasses of red on his platter. They smelled divine. I ate my dinner at home, and it was quite fine.

Such an amazing dining experience and by far the best meat lasagna of my life. The restaurant itself is small so I would highly recommend having a reservation. Our group of four came on a Friday night at prime dinner time and every single seat in the house was full, including all bar seats. Service was incredibly quick, efficient, and helpful with our menu selections.

We got the prosciutto and fried asparagus chips to start. Four our mains, we had the cacio e pepe, ravioli, meat lasagna and one of the daily special pastas. We finished our meal with the tiramisu and panna cotta. Everything was delicious, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. I highly recommend this spot and they even deliver with DoorDash and I'd have to say, the lasagna does travel well.

Phenomenal lasagna. Phenomenal food, and the host could be a little mean if you are putting your name down / waiting to get seated, but it is understandable after all since this is a roughly 30 people spot restaurant and everyone and their mothers are in town trying to get a seat. Portions are a lot bigger than you think, and the wait for 2 people on a Friday night at 5:30pm is 3 hours. Still better than the impossible Resy to nab, which fwiw comes out at midnight.
Delicious + worth the wait! A must try when in town! Make sure to get there an hour early or so to make sure you have a chance to get in.

It was my date's bday and so we decided to go here to celebrate. He had it on his bookmarked and so we thought it would be a nice treat to check out a restaurant that both of us have never been too. 

The ambiance was cute and warm. Though the table was quite annoying as the legs are located on all four sides instead of having a pillar right at the center. If there was a pillar then I would have felt more comfortably seated. Either case, this was minor in comparison to the food. 

We ordered a slew of dishes. Starting from their fried artichoke hearts to their brussel sprout with cheese, to their charcuterie. For entree we ordered their pasta with cheese and peppers and lasagna. 

Everything was a disappointment. Their artichoke does not come with any dipping sauce so just eating pure deep fried artichoke was way too much and oily. I felt like I was eating a bag of chips. Their brussel sprout tasted microwaved (according to my date's opinion) and sprinkled with cheese. As for their lasagna, it tasted like it's been sitting around all day and only sliced up when ordered. I dunno but for $28 a dish, I expected more. I thought each lasanga dishes would be made to order but it seems like it's precooked and then cut per order.

The only dish that was decent was the pasta with cheese and peppercorn and their charuterie.
