Both my date and I was left feeling disappointed and oh yeah....if the restaurant offer your their house bread, please note that it's $5 a roll.  This irks me because there were no mentioning on their menu that their house bread roll were $5.

Either case, there are so many italian eateries in this neighborhood and I would strongly suggest to think twice before going here. The quality of the food does not stand up to their price tag. 

The only thing that I liked was that my date was happy that we went out and got to experience something we both can agree that we didn't like.

Absolutely delicious restaurant in West Village! Came here and put our name down as a walk in on Friday at 4:45 and we got a table about 45 min later. 

We went the full special menu and got truffle pasta, oxtail and mushroom pasta and roasted carrots. All were amazing. The truffle had a nice truffle butter and fresh truffle shaved on top. The oxtail and mushroom had every flavor one could want and had a very wide noodle shape which was a fun change of pace. The carrots were honestly the best part though, they were roasted long enough to fall apart with a fork and had a nice balsamic flavor to them.

Highly recommend this spot if you can get a table or a spot at the bar!!

I really enjoyed the lasagna and ribeye steak here!  
I actually liked the steak here way more than 4 Charles prime rib. 

It's a very intimate restaurant as it's not very big, the waiters are quite knowledgeable in the wine list that they have.

If you manage to get a reservation here, order as much as you can!

My favorite place among the two co-chefs/co-owners' small West Village empire of eateries (Buvette, Bar Pisellino, Via Carota, and Commerce Inn). It's just very solid and consistently above-average Italian fare here. It's not easy to get in but get a seat at the bar and tuck into a bowl of pasta. On my last visit, I didn't see the snarky, often rude manager with the grey beard and I'm hoping he's long gone; that guy has been my only criticism of I Sodi.

I think I Sodi is the best!!!  They flavor is very simple yet, tasted much better than the others. I guess their ingredients are superb. 
With this quality of food with this price range, can't find any others.... 
Need to make a reservation otherwise need to wait 3 hours which I did.
One of the best steak tartars we've had! Lasagna was very heavy but worth trying. Enjoyed the pappardelle al limone very much!
Wow, just wow. The pasta is incredible! The lemon pappardelle was my favorite of the dishes we ordered. The chocolate cake is unreal and a must-order item.
Best lasagna hands down in NYC. The cacio e pepe is better at Via Carota, but I always walk out satisfied and full. Excited for them to move to their bigger space.

The lasagna was very good.  melts in your mouth. However, I don't think I'm a huge lasagna fan. Everything at the restaurant is very far in very cheesy so be prepared very large portions. We definitely over ordered. The pasta with truffles was around $60. They should have warned us when we ordered it. I don't think it was worth it very difficult to see the prices on the bottles of wine so be careful. I thought I was ordering a bottle that was $120. Turned out to be $180 service by the waiter. Chris was wonderful I love his smile and his energy. Definitely a place that is worth trying in so far is a bucket list place. Not sure it's worth a repeat. $350 for two people but we did bring home a lot of food.

Yes, I did enjoy this restaurant, so I'm struggling a bit with the three star rating. I suggest you put it on your list to try and decide for yourself.  It is definitely worth a visit!  For the record. I do not consider I Sodi to be a one and done restaurant. I will return!  My favorite dish was the fried artichokes!!  They were so crisp and light like delicious little potato chips!!  I have had fried artichokes at many restaurants in the states and alway been a bit disappointed with what came on the plate. I Sodi's fried artichokes are the best and closest thing to the true Italian dish I have enjoyed in Italy. The three stars are because of the rules!  One must order their entire meal at once, fine, but what if we want more fried artichokes???  Not allowed as per our waiter.  Plus, the pasta was very good, but it didn't blow me away. It was just good. I wanted great after all of the hype about this place. Honestly, the only memorable dish was the artichokes. I will come back and order different items because it seems the potential is there.

This was one of my best meals! I had high expectations before getting a last-minute reservation, and I Sodi met them. 

The atmosphere: it was a small restaurant with only around eight total tables. Half of the room is the bar, but the feel is like you're in the chef's apartment. It feels very intimate. I enjoyed the design.

The staff: was very kind and attentive. Our waitress was always around when we needed her and ensured we were well looked after. She was also very good at giving menu suggestions.

The food: was immaculate! The chef can make simple dishes incredibly flavorful and luxurious. The lasagna, Cacio e Pepe, and special oxtail pasta were all some of the best I've ever had. The flourless chocolate cake was also superb!

Cleanliness: the place was in order and nicely cleaned.

I Sodi is and always has been the pillar of consistency. You go in and no matter what, you're going to enjoy your meal. You may be a little put off by the host who basically won't let you inside, but it's endearing (kinda). The quaint dining room has always been charming so I'm curious to see how that translates into their new larger space. We ordered the endive salad, lasagna, pappardelle al limone and the paccheri with meat sauce. Everything was fantastic with the exception of the paccheri - a little too al dente. I've had the lasagna now 3 times and I can say without a doubt it's worth the hype.

Pastas come out barely warm and overly rich and salty. Lasagnas are super dry, thick and kinda unnecessarily burnt on top. I don't get the appeal and I consider myself a well-traveled foodie and excellent cook. I'm also Italian and no one in Italy would think of these pastas as authentic and maybe that's not the point but this interpretation misses the mark. Are the noodles home made?, yes but the meat sauce needed warm water added to it in the heating process to loosen it slightly. The ingredients are top notch which helps things along but at this restaurant and sister restaurant, the pastas do not shine, not at all. At Via it's best to stick with the extensive veggie-salad section + mains and here the mains are pretty good.
If you're looking for a right off the stove piping hot flavorful plate of al dente pasta with a delicious sauce/condimento this is not your place but then again I guess it's clearly a matter of taste because you can't get into any of these establishments. Once the temperature of food drops the consistency quickly changes. Am I the only one who likes hot food served hot?? Seems so...

The verza salad may have been our favorite dish of the night. It was very creamy and delicious. We also really enjoyed the fried artichokes appetizer. For our main course we split a variety of pasta dishes along with a pork cutlet. My favorite pasta dish was the caramelized onion pasta. The meat lasagna was very good as well though I do wish it had been baked for slightly less time as the sauce was a bit dry.

I've been wanting to try this place for a while now and it lived up to our expectations! No wonder it's hard to get a reservation, since the interior is quite small - they really fit as many tables as possible in! The atmosphere is nice though and dimly lit, and the service was quick. 

For the food, we shared the lasagna with meat sauce and the tortellini special of the day. We also got bread and olives (which was $5, not included). 

Lasagna - worth the hype!! I loved all the layers and it was filled with meat sauce. Not too oily, saucy, or cheesy at all! And we were able to comfortably finish it despite the generous portion. 

Tortellini - I love when you can taste that the pasta dough is handmade, and this one is just that! The broth is super nice, light and flavorful, and complements the tortellini well! 

They have a wonderful selection of Italian wines as well and our server knew exactly what to recommend to us!

I Sodi is a small, dark, intimate Tuscan restaurant and dinner experience (although they are moving to a larger location sometime in the near future). 

I was able to snag a reservation for four for 9PM and we ordered an app, a good number of pastas, and a little dessert family style. The carciofi fritti was great - the fried artichoke was crispy but "meaty" (in a good, hearty bite way?). It did not necessarily need it, but thought an aioli or sauce would've been a nice addition.

For the pastas, all were pretty solid. Both the meat and the vegetarian lasagnas (A Sugo and Carciofi) were pretty good, better to share and get a taste of versus get as your own entree. The Tortelli Di Castagne, the oxtail and mushroom pasta daily special, and the white truffle pasta daily special were good and I thought the caramelized onion and lemon pastas were the main standouts. The Tagliatelle Con Cipolla was like a French onion soup in wonderful pasta form and the Pappardelle Al limone was delicious, lemony, creamy goodness. The Paccheri Strascicati had a hearty meat sauce, but was a little too al dente. Zero regrets trying more of the pastas than fewer, but in hindsight do wish we tried a proper main while there. 

For drinks, I tried their classic Negroni and another variation the server recommended. Both were good and did the job. I thought similarly about the desserts as well. We got the Torta Di Cioccolato (Flourless chocolate cake) with scoop of ice cream (gelato?) and tiramisu and it was a nice finish to the meal.

Mediocre in a word. Difficult to get a reservation but seeing the location of this neighborhood spot it makes sense. Lots of locals in the area. 
Entering, you are in a small closed portico, a sliding door opens with the host asking if you have a reservation, he tells you it will be a few minutes, in a non welcoming manner, then closes the sliding door So you wait like cattle until it is time to enter the restaurant. 
It's a sweet venue. Small but warm and cozy. 
Same host seats you, rattles off Specials for the evening and disappears. As dishes were delivered to the other tables the food looked delicious. 
He came back, took our order, in a very ..."I'm doing You a favor. Attitude"
Appetizers were ok. Artichoke salad was bland. The Special, baked radicchio with Gorgonzola was cold , but tasty. 
Lemon Pappardelle was overcooked,  had little flavor of lemon and was not warm. Disappointing 
Lasagna... was highly recommended... tasty but also was room temp. 
Gelato just ok... have always had much better! Panna Cota was delicious!
Cocktails in very small glasses
Very underwhelmed with I Sodi
Will not be a repeat guest.
i got food poisoning here... really bad cleanliness. don't go here for overrated pasta.

Right away when I saw the menu, I knew I wanted that multi layer Lasagna a Sugo! I've only seen a multilayer lasagna like that in instagram photos, but the real thing doesn't disappoint! I ordered it to go so the photo doesn't do it justice, but it was hands down the best lasagna I've had so far!

What an amazing meal!  We got the black truffle burrata, fried artichoke, lasagne with meat sauce, cacio e pepe, pappardelle al limone and the oxtail pasta special.  My favorite was the lasagne but the boys both loved the cacio e pepe. The fried artichoke is another MUST.  It really was amazing but a little aioli or some dipping sauce on the side would have made it phenomenal. They also gave us a side of grilled endives since one of our pasta dishes arrived a bit on the later side which was also perfectly charred. The drinks were also spectacular - I had three different negronis.  The negroni rosa was my favorite even if it was on the sweeter side.  Absolutely worth the hype. Get that reservation and get ready to feast!

I Sodi has the noteriety of being the hardest reservation to get in nyc, and while i always love a challenge if the food lives up to the hype, this place is decidedly is not worth the trouble. my friend wanted to go here for her birthday dinner and made a reservation for 4 people right when reservations were released, and still was only able to get a table at 5pm. 

the restaurant is cozy and chic, service was attentive and friendly, but the food left me underwhelmed. 

we ordered a number of dishes so i was able to try a bit of everything, we ordered some appetizers, one of the salads which was forgettable, the artichoke fritti was also a miss for us as it was over fried, but my friends enjoyed the steak tartare. their lasagna tasted pretty good although served lukewarm, be warned it's extremely dense and rich, after a few bites we were done honestly. they didn't have the tagliatelle capriossa on the menu, or any pastas that featured tomatoes for that matter because the waiter said they were out of season... so I ordered the lemon papparadelle and it was just fine. one of my friends who is gluten free got the short rib and polenta but it was such a small portion of short rib she was still hungry. 

I Sodi was i guess decent enough, but with so many other excellent italian restaurants in the city, i would say don't bother setting that alarm at midnight to get a reservation here.

Pretty conflicted on this place. Saw this place had a very good lasagna so wanted to try it. Had a reservation and were seated promptly. Our server was amazing, explained the whole menu and was super attentive the entire time. The restaurant is super cozy and definitely somewhere I would come casually if I lived in the area. Started the meal off with the Italian meat and cheese plate. Definitely tasty when eaten with the honey and bread. Decided to go with the lasagna, cacio e Pepe, and their ox tail special pasta. Additionally we got the pork chop to split. I was expecting the lasagna to be insane, however it was extremely lackluster. Was lukewarm and honestly just super average. Was pretty disappointed about this. The cacio e Pepe was very good though, pretty decent portion and good flavor from the peppercorns. Ox tail pasta was also great. The star was honestly the pork chop. It was thick cut and lightly breaded. Super intense porky, herby flavor. Really good. Overall I would come here again for the ambience, the food is generally good but there are definitely some misses on the menu.

5 stars for the Lasagna a Sugo!! This is the reason we came here and it was worth the hype. Perfect ratio of pasta to sauce. Didn't want it to end!

Also recommend the Tortellini stuffed with prosciutto if it's still on their specials menu. We got this as an appetizer and it was served in a nice broth 

The rest of the dishes were good, but honestly not as memorable as the lasagna. 
- Pappardelle Al limone: very light sauce so mixed reviews from the table. I personally liked this 
- Fried artichokes: a little too fried for me. Could hardly taste artichoke 
- Oxtail pasta: this was on their special's menu. The sauce was delicious but didn't pair well with the wheat pasta 
- Tiramisu: this was a little different than traditional tiramisu. The top was super creamy/ custard like and very little espresso taste since there weren't soaked ladyfingers throughout. Personally would pass on this 

The place is super small/cozy - makes sense why it's so hard to get a rez here. The service is excellent and waiters offered us a drink until our table was ready. Overall, worth it if you can snag a rez, but there are equally good Italian spots in the area

This place is insane. I've been here twice within a month because I couldn't stop thinking about their menu. 

Whatever popularity ISodi has is worth the struggle of fighting for a table. I did both the walk in bar seat and the table via reservation seat. Amazing both times

They're famous dish-- the lasagna was huge it's really flavorful. The texture it was a bit mushy which is different but not bad. The cheese sprinkled on top is perfect. I reheated it for lunch the next day and it was still amazing. 

The cacio e Pepe was the best I'd ever had. Like, I'm my entire life. So creamy yet light. At risk of sounding like a broken record, it was so flavorful (because I'm convinced every dish on their menu is insanely flavorful). 

The service is good. They could be a bit more kind, especially given how few tables there are. Speaking of tables, the interior at isodi is romantically lit the tables are near each other but not too squished. It's intimate and cozy with an upscale vibe. 

I left isodi telling all of my friends they needed to visit. Stat.

Solid Italian spot in the village. We had their meat lasagna, oxtail tagliatelle, artichoke salad, and flourless chocolate cake. I didn't think the lasagna was that memorable as it felt a bit dry, however - the oxtail tagliatelle (their daily special) was INCREDIBLE. We sat at the bar which was a great vibe and the bartenders were friendly. Their cocktails were also strong.

Got there at 5:15 on a Friday night, put our names on the list and were seated by 7:45. Honestly the food was below average. The lasagne was dry and lacking flavor. Wayyy too much salt. The short rib was 75% fat so we sent it back. Customer service in this situation was honestly embarrassing. Our waiter didn't care and acted as if we are missing out/stupid because "short rib is typically a fatty dish". The ribeye was also tough, salty, too fatty, and lacking flavor. It's very cramped and crowded with no decor. Truly nothing about this place is worthy of the praise it gets. I am very disappointed since we were expecting a wonderful meal. At least now I know I will not be going back.

I don't know why people are not rating this place as high as it deserves. Yes, staff is a little pretentious and it is hard to get a table but the food is excellent. Stopped in without a reservation around 5-5:30 and wait was about an hour. Started the dinner with an order of Burrata then meat lasagna and orecchiette with sausage which was the special for the night. Both our meals and the starter were excellent. Our server asked us if we wanted bread but he didn't make it clear that they charge for it. It's not much, 5-6 bucks and we would have said yes if we knew they charge for the bread, but I thought it was odd that they offer bread as a menu item while it's not on the menu. Tiramisu was really good, mostly cream but tasted good. 
Small cozy dining room. Totally recommend and I'm glad we were able to get a table.

Walked in early on a Thursday evening and had to wait 15 minutes for seating at the bar. The restaurant is small and intimate. Service was excellent and staff was friendly. We started out with a couple glasses of wine, bread, olives, and the Burrata. The Burrata with prosciutto was excellent! For our mains we split the Cacio E Pepe followed by the Fried Pork Chop. Both were delicious! I am a big fan of Cacio E Pepe and I Sodi's did not disappoint. Pasta tasted freshly made and the sauce was perfection! Highly recommend all dishes. Reservations are difficult to get. If you arrive around 5pm the wait is not too long for bar seating.

Everything was perfect. The service, the wine, the lasagna, the broccoli and sausage pasta.

I didn't know lasagna could be that good.

Best lasagna I've had in my life. The specials they had were also so good. Had the broccoli and sausage pasta special and it was so good. I also got the burrata with prosciutto which was some of the best I've had as well. Cozy atmosphere and really helpful and friendly staff. There's so many good Italian places in West Village but this one really shined. I've read through so many of the bad reviews here and maybe people are just picky because I don't agree with any of them. MUST GO!

This place is so overhyped. The service is ok, not good but not bad. The food was super salty. The noodles were on the harder side. We had the following: PAPPARDELLE AL LIMONE , LASAGNE A SUGO , & BRASATO. All were very underwhelmed. The place is very small so that's part of the reason reservations are so hard to get.

First time, amazing meal. Crispy artichokes were spectacular. All the pasta dishes were fantastic, lasagna, Cacio e pepe, lamb special, lemon sauce. Rabbit was delicious. Nice portions. We had leftovers, yah!! Great cocktails and service. So lucky to get a reservation!!

The food is really good and the restaurant is charming, but the staff is incredibly pretentious and snooty.  We had a great meal there last night but our waiter was unpleasant bordering on rude.  Really puts a damper on the overall experience and makes it not worth the hype, which is unfortunate because I've enjoyed the place over the years.

HORRIBLE. Not at all like we remembered. Bartender was awful. A complete jerk to us. Trying to push us out the door. Lasagne was dry. Just an awful experience. Not worth the expense at all. The bartender should be fired.

Been  on  notify  3  months  
CAnt  get in  

Not  cool  when pandemic  hit they asked for  contributions to the staff 
I did

I  guess they don't  reward loyalty

The place was cozy and simple. It was hard to score a resy so I had high expectations. Given how hard it is to get a resy, you will have better chance lining up when it opens and get a bar seat. We ordered several dishes:

- Burrata E Prosciutto: the burrata was fresh and the prosciutto was yummy
- Maltagliati sul agnello: this was one of the specials. It was handmade pasta with mushroom and lamb. The pasta texture was so yummy and the sauce was tasty
- Lasagna sugo: this was what I Sodi was known for. Personally I'm not a mushy lasagna person so even getting half of the dishes was too overbearing. I mainly tasted the meat and the sauce, did not taste much of the pasta sheet texture when eating. The burn on top was a nice touch.
- Cacio e pepe: we got the lasagna and the cacio e pepe at the same time and decided to go with the lasagna first. By the time we got to the cacio e pepe, it was kinda hard and cold, so I was not impressed at all. The pasta was cooked al dente, the sauce was not impressive. 

Overall, only 2 out of 4 dishes were good. The two famous dishes were either not my cup of tea, or I didn't give it a fair chance (given I didn't taste it warm). As for me, I prefer other Italian spots in the city than here.

We finally tried the famous Isodi lasagna. I loved it (10/10). It was one of the best lasagnas I have had in my life, but my husband said it was only alright because their lasagna was not cheesy enough. Some people might say it's dry.. but hey, it was worth trying it! It's definitely a different style of lasagna. We also ordered orecchiette with sausage which was the special for the night, this one was extremely salty for me and I honestly did not like it (2/5). Special salad (bean with basil/mint) was delicious. We couldn't finish everything and we were very full at the end. They also have great wine selections, cocktail (Especially negroni) was delicious, ambience was great, and service was great.

Started with the fried artichokes. Tasted good but it needed a wedge of lemon or some sort of dipping sauce. It is also a huge dish. The two of us could only finish half of it.

The lasagna was gummy but had a meaty sauce. It looks great but disappoints at the end of the day.

The orichette was thick and doughy. It was handmade but that doesn't always make things better.

Service was attentive and good  though.

One of the best places for pasta in all of NYC and beyond. The setting is perfect, great neighborhood, and phenomenal staff. The lasagna is what made them famous and make sure to get it! They even have a vegetarian version that is also amazing! A very filling meal and worth every penny
One of the best meals and service I've ever had in NYC. I LOVED the salads and branzino If you can get a table you gotta go!

Husband and I walked in on a Friday night with no reservations and miraculously got in - this was right before they made the move to a larger location and we thought the smaller venue was perfectly cozy (although I'm excited to see the new spot!)

Drinks were excellent - we both love Negronis and the Negroni menu was to die for. So many options and the ones we ordered were very well made.

The food is what really stood out. My husband, notorious for not liking artichokes (a personality flaw that breaks my heart), couldn't get enough of the carciofi fritti appetizer, and neither could I. The real star of the show was their lasagna, which is what they're known for. Neither I nor my husband particularly love lasagna - I tend to think it's all just fine, and it wasn't very high up on my list of things to order. The server recommended it however and we are so glad we followed that recommendation - it was easily the best pasta dish we've had in ages.

We can't wait for them to open in their new spot so we can have dinner there again!

Enoyed a lovely round of meals ( brought 2 friends and we cross tasted our orders)  steak- pork chop and short rib  All really tasty, juicy, flavorful!  Homemade pasta was terrific and the appetizer was exceptional
Fried artichoke!!  Service was very good.  If I lived closer I would return often.

Arugula salad plain and easily serves four. Bread good but [small, not advertised] upcharge. Burrata/tomato app special was melt-in-ya mouth delish. 15-layer lasagna (Sugo) very tasty, but a tad dry. Northern Italian lasagna should be messy and not cut like cake. Needs more sauce/bechamel and/or parboil the noodles longer so they don't suck the liquid (sauce) out of the dish. Never saw with meat on top, but enjoyed that. Bronzino/capers--nice portion, tasty, but no veggie/side? Can't comment on the Negroni I was looking forward to since they'd just moved and were waiting for new liquor license.

Best meal of our trip to New York. Reservations are impossible to get, but went with our good friend who lives nearby, is a regular and we thankfully got right in. Our server, Chris, was friendly. Professional and warm. Every dish was simple, but delicious, made with the highest quality ingredients. 

We started with a round of Negronis and the fried artichokes which were so crispy, salty and highly addictive! Then we ordered a bottle of exquisite Chianti and had two salads between the 4 of us - the Valeriana  (mache, pecorino and balsamic vinegar) and the Rucola e Castelmagno (arugula w/ castelmagno cheese) - both were incredible - and the arugula was just 3 ingredients - arugula, olive oil and cheese - but again, perfection. 

For our next course, We split 2 pastas, the Cacio e Pepe (spaghetti chiatarra w/ black pepper and pecorino) - one of the best I've had - and spinach Ravioli Burro e Salvia (spinach and ricotta ravioli in a traditional butter and sage sauce) - so good.

For our entree, the 4 of us split the Ribeye special "for 2" - but it more than fed 4. We ordered it medium, which was perfect for us - still very pink, more like a medium rare. So flavorful. Also had a side of the spinach (very fresh) and the dainty peas (purposefully well-cooked, but a little mushy for me). 

Then, we saved just enough room for two affogatos which were incredible, and one espresso martini, such a warm, cozy, friendly place. We thoroughly enjoyed every minute, and hope we are able to return next time we're in town.

FYI / PSA - I didn't catch it on the menu if it's there but so-so bread and olive oil will cost you 5 beans. So if wait staff asks if you want it, you know before the bill comes. :-)

It's deceptively small as you only see the front room when you walk in, but we asked and they had a back room and an outdoor space for those nice days. It was packed for a Monday so we were lucky to be seated. 

Service was fine. The bruschetta I would get again - the cheese and tomato combo just worked for me. I thought the lasagna was over cooked. With all the layers maybe this is how it's got to be but not my preference. I finished most of it anyway because that's what I do. My friend enjoyed her pasta and has been here multiple times.

No dessert or bathroom visit.

I was really looking forward to having dinner at I Sodi, but I left disappointed. First off, it is nearly impossible to get a reservation. I went on Resy as soon as reservations opened for the date I wanted to have dinner and nothing was available. However, I emailed the restaurant and Chris was nice enough to get me a table for the date I wanted. Prior to dining at I Sodi, I informed the restaurant we were celebrating a 30th birthday. Unfortunately, there was no candle or acknowledgment with the dessert we ordered. We ordered a bottle of wine that our waiter recommended -- the wine was awful and was insanely marked up. For appetizers, the Fried Artichokes were pretty good and the portion size is large. The bread is nothing special so I would recommend skipping on that. The Cacio e Pepe was fine -- it lacked flavor. The pasta with marinara sauce and cheese was good. The Eggplant Parmesan special was nothing special. The Lasagna is the only dish I would go back for -- that was delicious. We ordered an Affogato for dessert, but we received two desserts that we did not order; when we told the server, he took them off our table rather than offering to let us enjoy them as they were sitting at our table for quite some time. Overall, the food and service were just okay. For the price of the entire meal, I was disappointed.

So...I Sodi was high on my list of restaurants to visit as it is widely considered one of the best Italian restaurants to go to in NYC.  I woke up at 12am to get the reservation and snagged one for a Friday at 4:45.

Honestly I wish I had just gone somewhere else. 

I don't understand the hype here.  There was a line of people already waiting when me and my wife got there and honestly I was super excited to experience what even Infatuation called one of the best pasta restaurants in NY.

The service was ok, nothing to write home about.  The waiter offered us the homemade bread which we accepted but found out it was a $5 charge when we got the bill.

Now comes the food.  I ordered 3 pasta dishes and a meat dish since I wanted to try as much food as possible at a place that is considered one of the best.

Lasagna a Sugo: Like other reviewers have mentioned, this is probably the main dish that is recommended here, but it lacked in a lot of areas.  The dish came barely warm, and it was very soft in texture.  Not terrible, but not at all what was expected.

Pappardelle al Limone:  Well cooked pasta with butter, lemon, and pepper.  Ok?  Anybody with the ingredients available can make this, and possibly make it better.  Just very basic.

Ravioli Burro e Salvio: The best dish in our opinion.  Nothing to complain about here.   Great sauce and great pasta.

Cotolleta alla Milanese:  At first glance and taste it was perfect.  But when you cut deeper there is too much fat left on the pork, which for our personal preference is not a great texture to bite into.  Very gelatinous fat, but I will say it was seasoned well and fried perfectly.

The drinks I can say were spot on and delicious, at least for us.  

Really left disappointed here especially considering the hype.  We have visited other highly regarded Italian restaurants in NYC, which I will not name as to not make you guys think this is a biased review, and have had so much better experiences.  We have other places on our list that are highly regarded, but our experience here has made us possibly change our minds in visiting them.

Nice cozy restaurant. The food and the service are all good. The drinks are mostly negronis and martinis but pretty good as well.

They hit above their weight from appetizers to the mains. Worth going to if you are in the area for no frills Italian dishes.

Oh I Sodi! I have dreamed of going to I sodi and never thought I would be able to get a reservation.  My friends and I were lucky enough to snag a table of 6 at 8:15 pm on a Friday the day of and were PUMPED! The vibe and ambiance inside was incredible. There are two dimly lit two rooms, one by the bar, one through the back and then a stunning outdoor patio. One compliant it is VERY quiet inside which I didn't expect and isn't what you typically find at the highly sought after and vibey WV spots. The waiters like many other yelpers have said are slightly pretentious and overall really not that helpful. We did find ourselves waiting and waiting for them to refill our wine glasses, and his took probably over 20 minutes before they were filled. Which is fine but not something you would expect at a place which such status. 

The apps very great! The fried artichokes are a must, the meat and cheese board was delish and the burrata was good but not a must get. The lasagne sugo  was by far my favorite pasta dish and the special of the evening the pesto pasta  was very unique and delicious. I've had better cacio e Pepe and limon style pasta but they were still very good. 

We were too full for deserve but the espresso martinis were good! I would def go back to sit on the patio!

It's been one of New York City's best Italian restaurants for years. The new location is great; slightly less cramped, and the pasta is as good as ever. 

I think some people miss the concept of ISodi and expect saucy meatballs and fancy salads; leaving disappointed.  It's not trying to be Bad Roman or Via Carota (both great). In my experience, Rita is cooking food her parents and grandparents would have cooked. Expect simple quality ingredients, incredibly well prepared, and served without pretense. 

If you go, get a Negroni. They're all delicious and have been some of NYC's best Negronis for years.

This place is the perfect example of how reviews are completely flawed. This is an excellent restaurant.....period. You gave this place a 3.7?  You had bad service or have no taste in food. Every single thing we had was absolutely delicious from the pastas and the insanely delicious Lasagna to the ribeye steak which was literally perfection. Everyone who gave this place a 3.7 should understand you literally don't know food and should stick to 5 napkin burger.

I had an appalling experience here, which is extremely disappointing because I frequented I Sodi as well as the sister restaurants (Via Carota, Buvette, Bar Pisellino) frequently during the pandemic.

We had a mix up with our reservation information and the host's behavior was outrageous. He was condescending and rolled his eyes at us. It was beyond belief to be treated with such rudeness when we were prepared to spend +$300 on dinner for two for a special occasion.

I usually aim to look for the positives in my reviews (my profile speaks for itself with +40 5 star reviews) and in the case of such a bad experience would normally reach out directly to the restaurant before posting on yelp, but the phone line is unattended and, even more shockingly, there are many other similar reviews on yelp and google calling out this exact host's behavior - so it's hard to imagine the restaurant takes their hospitality seriously when this behavior apparently goes unaddressed.

I'm sure they will continue to fill tables with tourists, but this is no way to run a restaurant if you want to attract locals, and it's clear the operation is resting on their laurels. There are many more hospitable restaurants on this block worth your money on this block, let alone in NYC.

Honestly not an Italian food expert but I've had better Italian food at an Olive Garden. Service was terrible--not sure if standard for NYC restaurant. Food took forever...forgot to bring bread, rushed through first courses only to wait an hour and 15 for dishes. Over hyped. Port cutlet cooked well. Cacio e pepe good. Tomato salad really good. Everything else was meh

Incredible all around! The service was perfectly paced, did not feel rushed at all despite the people waiting for a table. Food was amazing. We enjoyed the pastas and appetizers we got. Definitely try the lasagna! Very unique. Recommend sitting outside if you can.

Given the hype my expectations were high . I've lived in nyc for 25 years and finally made it to I sodi . Major disappointment and no reason to go frantic for a reso . From the service which was rushed and chaotic. To the underwhelming food I was very surprised . Seems like mgmt has really dropped the ball here . I will say the fried artichokes were awesome . This place is clearly a tourist trap that is living off its name from the good ol days . There is way better Italian restaurants for food, atmosphere , and service .. Hard Pass

One of the best meals I've had in a while. I Sodi is simple, refined, and understandably hard to get a reservation for. The servers know an incredible amount about what they are serving and seem to respect the establishment. Feel free to ask your server to make you a cocktail based on a specific description of what you're in the mood for and they'll seemingly read your mind and bring out exactly what you were looking for! 

We started with the fried artichokes and a salad with apple, parmesan, walnuts, etc (not sure what it was called). Both were great, but the fried artichokes were definitely a hit. They are apparently their most popular appetizer. 

For mains, my group shared the famous lasagna, the pappardelle al limone, the ravioli burro e salvia, and one of the specials, a lamb pasta in a burgundy sauce. We totally discovered why the lasagne a sugo was such a special dish, and as for the others they were all great, with the pappardelle Al limone a surprise hit (cooked in a parmesan sauce, it had a wonderful parmesan-lemon flavor). 

Overall, I Sodi is a great dining experience. The inside of the new location is cozy and lively. If I lived in NYC, I would definitely make this a regular spot for nice Italian food. Shoutout Devon for being an amazing server and reading our minds when we described what we wanted to drink!!

Crossed our fingers and walked in to I Sodi on a rainy Friday about 5pm. Two seats at the bar just waiting for us, it was fate. Started with two negronis which were dynamite, $18 which is reasonable for NYC prices. Artichoke salad was honestly skippable, but they more than made up for it with their special: heirloom carpaccio w/ goat cheese. Got it in right before the season ended! Of course, had to get the lasagna and finally see for myself if it could meet the hype: it exceeded it. I don't normally order lasagna but this one blew us away and it is an absolute MUST TRY. Overall, four cocktails, two starters and and entree was about $125 pre-tip. I felt that was fair and I would absolutely return here, if they'd have me!
Terrible experience. Host was increbibly rude, and while the the food was good, it was nothing special. NYC has better places. 2/5. The hype is unwarranted.
I Sodi is amazing, the food is to incredible, the service impeccable, and the atmosphere is great -- you feel like you're in Tuscany. Definitely make sure you go here!
Recommended by celebrated food review & chef for past NYC mayor. Trendy spot, but worth it.

Came right at 4:30 pm and was able to get bar seating immediately. Friendly bartenders provided expertly crafted drinks and served our food. Started with bread and olives - bread was warm and delicious with olive oil. Started with a great antipasto platter with delicious meat, cheese and honey. On special was the fried artichoke hearts which was incredible. We split the meat lasagna, spinach and ricotta ravioli, and Parmesan limone pasta. They were all delicious but the meat lasagna was phenomenal and stood out. A nice small restaurant that gets busy and hard to get a reservation. It was a fun and enjoyable experience.

First time at the new location and it's just as great as it always was! My boyfriend and I put our names in on a Monday night at 6:08 PM and were seated at the bar at 7:27. We shared:

+ Tartara
+ Fried artichokes
+ Chestnut tortelli (seasonal special)
+ Lasagne 
+ Marmalade crostata

We went the day the NYT review dropped, so I'm sure it's an even worse wait now, but always worth it.

Well! Love Via Carota, love Buvette, was excited to try the food here. Not a great experience. After a lecture from the host on reservation vs wait list (we had a seating at 6:20) we were seated at a small table. As it turns out, the table abuts a wine storage room (??) so I had to get up twice during dinner, in heels, to let servers in. Really unprofessional. The wait staff blamed their architect. Lol. 

Food was ok, but not what we expected. First, when my husband, who doesn't drink alcohol, tried to order a soda, he was told that the restaurant doesn't carry Coca-Cola products. Fine, but what soft drinks do you have? He was offered nothing but water. The artichoke starter and pastas were good but not great. (For what it's worth, our server butchered the Italian pronunciation throughout - better to just use English.) Pork secondi was not good at all and the spinach - no flavor, no seasoning at all - truly, tasted like a frozen block my mother used to reheat. We won't be back.

Honestly this place exceeded my expectations in every way. The lasagna is definitely worth it. Best lasagna I've ever had. The sheets of pasta are super thin and plentiful. Cutting into it feels like butter. The faro salad that was on the specials when I went was great. I'd skip the rabbit but we also got the pesto pasta dish and it was actually the best pesto I've ever had. Perfect nutty flavor and not too oily. 10/10

Really don't find that this place deserves the hype/long wait times that it gets, and not sure why as the food is just fine and the service is subpar, I'd say. On a Thursday at 6:30 pm, they had a 3.5 hour wait for the inside, so we dined outside immediately - great!

The starter bread (for $5 FYI) is solid - the bread is a bit mealy, but great olive oil and olives as well. I thought the fried artichoke appetizer was pretty good, considering they're not my favorite vegetable; I was impressed with how crispy they got them to be and I thought they were flavored nicely, although I got a bit tired of them by the end since they end up just being like fries.

I was disappointed I'd say with the pasta. The gnocchi I got was cooked so beautifully (like perfectly collapsed in my mouth), but the sauce was extremely bland. Nothing interesting about it at all that I think calling it a bolognese was a stretch. The presentation was mid with the weak shredded cheese on top and I wasn't too thrilled about the final product. Very similar comments about the lasagna too.

Service was pretty slow and not super attentive I'd say, but I get it, they're busy! Wouldn't come back on my own as the food didn't impress though.

TLDR: Save your time and money and head to Via Carota if you can

Started off with the bread and olives- pretty standard except the bread felt a little too grainy for my liking. 

Got the artichokes soon after and they were good but definitely could have used a dash of citrus to break up the heavy oil and saltiness of the dish. Just a squeeze of lemon and it wouldve been great. 

The pastas looked and sounded so good but were ultimately pretty average to disappointing. The texture on both the gnocchi and lasagna were great but the sauce fell so short. I ate maybe less than half of the lasagna before feeling sick of it.

When I finally gave up on getting an in-person reservation at I Sodi, I decided that takeout would be the next best option. I'll preface the review with saying any menu that has FRIED artichokes on it is near and dear to my heart and with the abundance of artichokes on this menu I was already in a giddy mood. We ordered the fried artichokes which were the best I've had (tied with Palma) - perfectly cut, fried, golden and salted. I sodi is quite famous for the 26-layer lasagna but getting that as takeout to go is not a good idea- the Cacio e Pepe lasagna and the Artichoke lasagna were very soggy by the time we got home...not to mention it felt like both were dipped in pure salt over and over again. The Ravioli Burro e Saliva  was perfection-- perfect mounds of spinache and cheese in a perfectly flavored parmigiano, butter and sage sauce. Would try this place again if they rolled out the red carpet and made it easier for us mere mortals to get an in person reservation.

Probably closer to 4 stars, but I'm going to go 5 stars because this place gets some unnecessary hate on Yelp. Also disclaimer - this review based on my dining at the original location, as I have yet to check out the new space yet.

I Sodi probably is a victim of its own success -  the vibes I get from eating here is that it was intended to be a neighborhood spot that made home cooked Italian food, that somehow got discovered and then became one of the toughest reservations in town. 

Gave up on trying to score a res on Resy, so just walked in at opening to sit at the bar (which was a cinch!). We ordered some negronis, the fried artichoke, pappardelle, cacio e pepe, and the famed lasagna. 

The negronis were 5/5 (at this point I was already 2-3 negronis in since we came from HH @ Dante right before this) - I recognized the bartender who used to work at Leyenda for several years. Wonderful apertif, highly recommend.

The fried artichokes were good - but they kind of taste exactly how they look, you really can't hate on something that's fried. Not life-changing, but good nonetheless.

The pastas were both excellent. The texture was absolutely perfect. If there was a textbook way of how these pastas are to be made, this would be it - but again not life-changing.

The lasagna was super good - I can't imagine the amount of effort it takes to assemble this thing with all its layers. This is lasagna in its highest form.

We finished the meal with a couple of decaf lattes. By this point we were completely stuffed.

Overall, this was a lovely meal - great vibes, great service. If you're expecting a mind-blowing/life-changing meal, you probably will be disappointed. However, if you want expertly made Italian food in a cozy setting, I Sodi will definitely fit the bill.

Long story short - the pasta and main course are way too too too salty, which I couldn't put up with, and even the salad was too salty. Everything was salty...  Why this kind of restaurant has so much hype. I think it's name "I Sodi" should change to "I Salty". Anyway, however, it still has its good parts... More details as follows:

The most salty one was the Coniglio in Porchetta (rabbit meat). It was like being soaked in highly condensed salt water. The salt taste made the meat itself tasteless. However, the good part was the condition of the meat. It was very juicy and tender. If it was 90% less salty, I bet it would be the best rabbit meat.

The lasagna was salty as well, especially the pork sugo part. But the pasta sheet was excellent. It was so soft and melty in my mouth. My fiancé described it as "like the lasagna version of Lady M's mille crepe".

The arugula salad was also extremely salty. And then I asked them to make a new one without any added salt, but then the second one was much better.

Another dish that I didn't like was the beets. Felt like the beets were not fully cooked. It was a little hard.

The two dishes that I loved were the Bresaola (dry aged wagyu beef with smoked stracciatella) and tiramisu. The smoked stracciatella was super delicious. I almost wanted to ask if I could order some to go lol. And the tiramisu was also very nice. It was the best tiramisu I've ever had. My second best was Via Carota's.

Our experience was perplexing. A reservation was quite hard to get yet the room remained half full for our entire visit. The food was fine but nothing special or remarkable. The service was aloof and our server was distracted by also serving as host which is odd at this price point to not have a dedicated host. The atmosphere is bland and lifeless. Overall we had a very lackluster experience. Would not visit again.
Everything we ordered was extremely over salted. And I like salt! We sat at the bar and the bartender was very gruff- poor hospitality.  Mediocre at best. Not worth the wait and overhyped

Very crowded and server was a bit rude. Our daughter does not eat most things so we had to bring her packed meal. We ordered plenty of items. Yet the server got very rude and said outside items were not permitted and this upset my daughter and made us feel uncomfortable. The pastas were ok but overall I don't get the hype. Should have listened to the other yelp reviews here.

My friend and I came here for an impromptu lunch on a Saturday. We were just two so only had to wait 15 mins for a seat at the bar. I loved the bread (idk what others have said, the bread is fluffy and warm and perfect for dipping into the delicious olive oil) and the olives. We got the fried artichokes (which are solid if you like them) and shared a special: a thickly cut pasta with braised short rib and mushrooms. The pasta was AMAZING. Perfectly hearty and comforting and delicious. We also got their sbagliato which was perfectly smooth and tasty. Would I be willing to wait more than 30 mins for this place? Probably not, but all in all I enjoyed it and would come back!

I jumped on an early bird reservation that opened up last minute on a rainy cold Tuesday night. The hype around this Tuscan restaurant from the Via Carota team has made it a challenge to just pop in on a whim so even the 5:15 reservations don't grow on trees. Side note: bar seats are reserved for walk-ins only so you can always try your luck that way. 

The drink menu consists of about eight different types of Negronis and ~$20 glasses of wine - standard affair for this neighborhood. I did enjoy the bourbon Negroni option as a variation from the traditional gin. Simple decor, nothing particularly warm or charming that screams cozy Tuscan country house.

Now for the lasagna, THE signature lasagna! Honestly, underwhelming. Not particularly flavorful and the noodles were quite overcooked. We also got the rabbit wrapped in porchetta with spinach, which was more porchetta than rabbit and a tad salty. The portions were quite generous, I must say.

Nothing was bad exactly, but I didn't walk away particularly impressed either. This will be one of those "tried once but wouldn't return" spots for me.

Ugh. Wish I understood the hype after going for lunch. It's like any other overly hyped Italian place in the area. We ordered a bunch of things to share, and nothing was particularly notable. 

Lasagna was nothing special other than the cool look of all the layers, ravioli was too sweet, crispy artichokes were good for about 4 bites then were way too oily, the bread that comes with the table tasted store bought-- like corner store bought. You also get a whopping *four* olives with the bread (??). 

Tiramisu was good, but honestly when isn't it?

Only pro was the waiter messed up our order and comped one of our pastas. Total was still over $180 and we only had one drink and a latte.

Second stop on my wife's birthday extravaganza. We posted up at 4:15 and were seated at the bar once they opened at 4:30. Lining up may not have been necessary but the bar was filled by 5. 

Big wine selection. Good selection of whiskeys too but quite pricey. My wife had a cocktail while I had a whiskey. The bartender was super patient and very attentive.

We started with the non-complimentary bread and olives. Four pieces of bread and four large olives in these inflationary times. Bread was quite dense and heavy. 

Next we had one of the specials. It was fried polenta with cheese and oil on top. I believe it was stracciatella. Polenta was super crispy and just perfect level of greasy. It was super savory and ultra comfy. I'd highly recommend it if it's available.

For the main course, we shared the lasagna and the pappardelle de limone. I preferred the pappardelle. Great texture on pasta. Sauce was cheesy, citrusy, and a bit funky. 

For dessert, we shared the tiramisu. Ultra rich and creamy. Not as sweet as I expected and was surprisingly bitter forward. I liked the interesting take as the presentation was traditional and I did not anticipate such a unique flavor. 

I believe there were two gender neutral restrooms. The one I used was handicap accessible.

The food is a 10, but getting a reservation is a silly and futile game. Your choices are setting your alarm daily to hop on Resy two weeks ahead at 9 a.m. (which never, ever yields a table; bots?) or standing in line at 4:30 p.m. with your prize being a 4:30 dinner if it's a slow night or a 2+ hour wait if not.  Major, MAJOR attitude at the door and from every single server we encountered.  I had a friend from out of town with me who observed "they are simply UNcharm-able."  That sums it up perfectly.  The casting call for staff here must be:  MOODY, RUDE, SMILE-AVERSE, POMPOUS.  Baffling because the owners' other spots (Via Carota, Bar Pisellino, Buvette, etc) are at least 70% friendlier (none are the most charming crew you've ever encountered).  The one time I stopped in at i Sodi to ask in person what the secret is to getting a table without all the song and dance mentioned above the charmer at the door told me "It's just not that hard."  UH, not true! Plus who says that!?  We live a block away and I even said:  "You must not want neighbors to join you for dinner?" to which he smirked and wordlessly moved on to the next table beggar behind me.  Can't imagine going back here unless something changes.  NYC has so many other excellent options.

Got a 4:30 reservation and are so happy we did. The waiter was super nice and knowledgeable about the dishes and the kitchen was accommodating to our nut allergy. We would highly recommend the fried artichoke hearts, ox tail wheat pasta, and the lasagne. Small, intimate setting that was perfect for a girls night.

The food is not bad, I've had better 
The service was not good at all. The waiter rushed us out because they had other people coming. We got a bottle of wine, which we did not finish because they needed the table. We tried seating at the bar to finish our glass of wine and the host stated we had 10 minutes at the bar because he needed the space for others. This is definitely not a place to go if you want to enjoy quality time with friends and enjoy a bottle of wine.

Food is standard. Service is horrible. Gave a formal complaint regarding timing of food to the bald "manager", response was that he thought the timing was reasonable despite the 1.5 hour wait for entrees. Go to the other 10 better Italian restaurants around the corner. Surprised about the hype. Avoid.

Waiter: The steak tartare is the best in the city.  sure. if you like overdressed with Worcester sauce. 

Waiter: The special is Ox Tail and mushroom Ragu over hand pulled wide noodles.  in reality, tasted like an over sauced and over salty stew with overly cooked pasta. 

Waiter: delicious ravioli with chestnut filling.  again, over cooked pasta and beyond salty. 

worse $231 I ever spent. (not including a nice tip/ not his fault the food is awful)  
this place would never last in Italy. a joke.

Loved the tartare. Simple, clean damn near perfect. The pasta was over-cheesed for my taste but then this is typical of Italian American food so I cannot complain about that. The wine selection was excellent. Enjoyed every aspect of the experience, although the interior design was a touch too austere for such a lovely place. 
Definitely worth the trip and cost. Good service.

We were delighted to be seated as walk-ins after a 45 minute wait at 5:30 on a Thurs. evening.  Unfortunately the meal didn't live up to our expectations.  We had the fried baby artichokes for first.  They were tasty, like artichoke flavored potato chips, but half of them were over salted.  On the other hand, the bread was severely undersalted, and the accompanying 4 olives tasted like they came out of a can.  My husband had the short rib with polenta, which he enjoyed.  I had the rabbit, which was well prepared and a generous portion.  It was accompanied by (boiled?) chopped spinach, which tasted like it had no seasoning whatsoever--no garlic, oil, pepper, even salt.  We opted to go elsewhere for dessert.
After anticipating an excellent meal at this expensive restaurant, needless to say we were very disappointed.  It seems like they are overwhelmed by their success, and no one is minding the shop.  Hopefully the owners will realize the problems and correct them, but we won't return to find out.

Overall, I was disappointed given the hype. The pastas were good, but sauces were a bit heavy. The ambience is nothing special. The service was indifferent and not welcoming. Had a much better experience at Rezdora the following week- very warm service, great pastas and other dishes and nice touches such as an amuse Bouche and chocolates with dessert. Perhaps I Sodi is living off an old reputation

I'm giving a restaurant five stars if there's something that has 1) fundamentally changed my view of a dish or 2) has something I would go back to ten times over. I Sodi has checked off both those boxes for me.

THE HITS: the pappardelle al limone and lasagna a sugo are spectacular. If you're going to choose two pastas, choose these. They're classics, highly recommended, and for good reason: the creamy pappardelle that has the refreshing lemony undertones and the decadent, béchamel layered lasagna...say no more.

We also ordered the fried artichoke antipasti (scrumptious for the first two bites, then it got to be too oily) - would recommend ordering this for a group of 4+.

I've gone to I Sodi once before, and the cacio e Pepe was much too salty for my taste, but the lasagna was fantastic.

All but the very best tend to go through the motions on the classics. I Sodi is stuck in that rut, with the cacio e pepe and the famed lasagna both fine but not notable (or worth the effort to get in the door). Go for the specials instead, which together with the intimate rustic vibe, do make it worthwhile to wait in line at 4:15 pm.

Conversely, while the tiramisu is not my favorite tiramisu in the city (not enough coffee in the ladyfingers or cocoa on top), it is simplicity done subtly--and well.

Pastas are solid though I think overall the experience is average at best. Reservations are hard to get.

Pappardelle al limone: 5/5 (the BEST, def get this)
Ravioli burro e salvia: 4/5 
Lasagne a sugo: 3/5
Steak tartare: 2/5
Flourless cake w/ gelato: (2/5)

FOOD
Overall, I expected a lot more of I Sodi. I've heard it compared to other greats incl. L'Artusi and unfortunately this wasn't it. The steak tartare was extremely average and no one flavor popped out. The lasagne was also very average. However, our server recommended 2 pastas which ended up being pretty great. The ravioli was delicious and came with a great butter sauce. However, the star (by FAR) was the pappardelle al limone. I worried it would have a strong lemony flavor, but that was not the case. The pasta was also cooked beautifully - al dente has never been done so right. Truly a memorable pasta and the only dish that made the meal worth it. 

AMBIANCE
The restaurant is small, cozy, and intimate. A great place for a date.

SERVICE
Our server was great! Had a lot of energy throughout the meal and gave us great recommendations (except for the dessert which was a total fail)

Overall, not a bad place. I'm glad I tried to see what the hype was about, but probably won't be back

I was shocked by my first visit to I Sodi. Given the hype, I was really excited when I got a reservation for Saturday night but my meal was disappointing. 

My partner and I shared two pastas and a side of broccolini. We got the lasagna and it was not good. I do not understand the fanfare for it. Both pastas were heavy and dark. The broccolini side was similarly bad - it felt a bit soggy and didn't have a lot of flavor. The service was great but I would honestly not return again. Bummer.

Excellent food, not so great service, pretty tight seating. The three stars are purely for the food, it was quite delicious. The salad we started with was a great combination of flavors and the lasagna is one of my favorite dishes I've ever had in the city, melt in your mouth amazing. Now for the service, we requested bread, seeing all the other tables had some, and we were brought out cold, stale bread that was in a completely different basket and clearly was different bread from the other tables. We were also charged for it, this was very odd and frustrating. Our server also just had a very bad attitude and made us feel like we didn't belong there. To get in and out of the table, the whole table had to be moved and we were uncomfortably close to others. I would love to go to I Sodi again for the excellent lasagna, but the service makes me want to steer clear.
Solid 4.5. The experience, service and food is top notch - the price is a little bit expensive. I would recommend a visit at least once.

Walked in at 8pm on a Monday with 2, and were seated at the bar in the time it took to drink 3/4 a glass of Chianti 

Best seats in the house perhaps, as the bartender (Michael) was welcoming and quick to share the specials. We ordered the steak tartare on his recommendation and it was 10/10.

We ordered two pastas... both delicious and large sizes. The biggest surprise was the pasta with sautéed onions. So simple. Beyond delicious. I couldn't figure out how they created such flavor with amazingly simple ingredients.

We ended the meal with a simply prepared branzino with fried capers. 

It was everything and more. This could be my favorite Italian in the neighborhood. Can't wait to be back.

I've heard a lot about this restaurant, and since we couldn't get a seat at saint Theo's we decided to give I sodi a try.

We came on a Friday night with no reservations and honestly just got lucky. Some people were on the wait list for 2+ hours we got a table right away, but it was outside seating. There were heat lamps so it was fine, but in the spring this would be a really nice place to sit. They have a little patio set up which is part of the restaurant (we didn't sit in one of those outdoor street things)

We both ordered red wine which was good. It paired well with the food. We started with the burrata app which was tasty. The burrata could have been a little creamier/softer but it was good. We paired that with the bread.

The lasagna was good. It's not your typical lasagna! If you have ever been to lady M's cakes with the multiple layers that's the exact representation of this lasagna. There's so many thin layers of pasta paired with meat sauce. I don't think there's any ricotta in it. It is dry, but it's tasty and soft because of the layers of pasta. I enjoyed it. We also ordered the oxtail with wheat pasta which was the special of the night. This dish was really really good. We shared both so it was a good mix of flavors.

For desert we ordered 2, but the brought out chocolate cake by mistake and just let us keep it on the house :) the tiramisu was amazing. That was my fav desert out of the 3, and one of the best I've had in a while. We also ordered another that came with vanilla ice cream and 3 round chocolate nut circles which was good. The chocolate cake wasn't good, really really dry-don't recommend that one.

Overall everything was good and I'll be returning soon!
Best classic Italian in all of NYC. The pastas, the service and the ambiance are all so classically quaint and perfect. You must try the artichokes and the limone pasta.
i love the food here but i dont like the staff so much. they are often rude. lasagna and cacico peppe are the best

Once you figure out a reservation here, you won't be disappointed. We had a spacious, comfortable table for 4 in the back room. The service was excellent, informative but relaxed. We enjoyed all of the food, but the fish (branzino) and pastas (cacio e Pepe, pappardelle limone, and the famous lasagna) were exceptional. Next time, I would skip the appetizers (we tried the crispy artichokes and fava beans). If you like tiramisu, theirs is exceptional.

Was a long time customer at the old I Sodi. It was a favorite. Once again like Via Carota, I could not believe the rudeness of the staff. They take pleasure in having no class even when they are no tables available. To be in hospitality they is a level of decorum and bedside manner. They had none here. I don't understand Rita and Jodi not overseeing this. You will lose customers if they do not know how to treat your customers. The staff looks miserable and it shows in their attitudes. Not what it used to be. The owners don't care anymore and that also shows that this is all for show. The pastas were gloopy. The waiter seemed irritable. Overall it left us feeling very disappointed.

I have never experienced such disdain and rudeness. We walked in 90min before close, with 6 folks ahead of us. I asked if we might make it in, the host said NO. I mentioned I'm in from Phoenix, it's my last night in NY, and if I could get something to go, the host said NO. A few spots opened up at the bar, I asked if we could get a drink while we tried to wait it out. The Bartender said I had to ask the host, the host said we could not order a drink, what!?? Lastly, a walk-in after us asked it he could have a seat at the bar, the host said he would see what he could do. I asked if we could sit at the other open spots at the bar, the host said NO. When I asked why a guest behind us could get a seat, why couldn't we, the host said "You're not getting a seat here and I ask you to leave". In all my years in Hospitality I have NEVER experienced such rudeness to a customer!!! Do not waste your time or money, nothing is worth that type of mistreatment to their guests.

Food was excellent, however, if you are forcing everyone who walks in to sit at the bar, the host should give the heads up that the only available seats are at the bar. For individuals with mobility issues, bar seating is painful/dangerous and it would have been helpful to know that prior to waiting 1.5 hrs for a seat. Further, if you are forcing everyone to sit at the bar, more than just a hook should be provided for coats/bags, especially in the winter. Food was excellent, but luckily there are many restaurants with excellent food in NYC and minus the inconsiderate attitude at the front of house.

If you're lookin' for a taste of Italy right here in the heart of New York City, look no further than I Sodi. This place ain't just a restaurant, it's an experience. 

From the moment you walk in, you're greeted with warmth and hospitality that'll make you feel like family.

Now let's talk about the food. The lamb? Oh my goodness, it's like a symphony of flavors dancing on your taste buds. Juicy, tender, and seasoned to perfection. And don't even get me started on the lasagna! It's a towering masterpiece, with layer upon layer of rich, savory goodness. You take one bite, and you'll be transported straight to the streets of Florence.

And let's not forget about dessert. The tiramisu? It's like heaven on a plate. Creamy, dreamy, and just the right amount of sweetness to end your meal on the perfect note.

The service here is top-notch. The staff goes above and beyond to make sure you have everything you need, with a smile on their face the whole time.

It's cozy, it's inviting, it's like stepping into Nonna's kitchen on a Sunday afternoon. You can't help but feel right at home.So if you're lookin' for a taste of Italy with a New York twist, do yourself a favor and head on over to I Sodi. You won't be disappointed.

I came with my friend on a Sunday evening around 6:15 pm without a reservation but we were able to get seated at the bar within less than 10 minutes. The bar seating wasn't the most comfortable - I think these seats were designed for super tall people (I'm 5'9" but still couldn't reach the bottom). 

My friend and I both ordered the bread to start and then the lasagna. The bread was nice and soft and warm paired with olive oil. The lasagna was a fat stack and came out steaming hot. It was super yummy and a large enough portion to bring back leftovers. Overall, yummy food!

Although we didn't have a reservation, we were fortunate to secure a table for dinner around 10:30 pm. The culinary experience was matched only by the simple yet impeccably crafted interior decor. However, it's worth noting that if you're sensitive to salt, you may find some dishes a tad on the heavy side.

I really enjoyed my dinner at I Sodi! I walked in around 5pm and got a seat at the bar around 8pm, which was perfect!

The bartender was nice, and the bear is beautiful, so I enjoyed sitting there.

Lemon pasta: 8.5/10

The noodles in the pasta were delicious. I absolutely loved the the texture. I will say it was almost too sour. I don't think I could eat a whole bowl of this but enjoyed sharing it as an appetizer with my friend. I think it's good, but wouldn't recommend solely ordering this. It gets old and the lemon flavor is a bit too sharp.

Meat lasagna: 9/10

The layered lasagna is very good and very filling. You can taste the quality in the meat and the sauce. Overall, it's good. I think the issue with the layers for me is it just becomes mush once it's in your mouth. The layers are so thin and there are so many layers of pasta it's kind of a weird mushy mouthfeel if that makes sense. It's still good, but it's lasagna nonetheless.

Pappardelle with oxtail ragu and mushrooms: 9/10

Great texture of the noodles. The pasta sauce was delicious!

Tiramisu: 5/10

The tiramisu was a huge let down. The sponge inside was dry. It hadn't been soaked with the espresso. It was weird taking a bite and having the nice cream but then having the weird dry cake... I do not recommend. This was a fail.

Overall, I enjoyed trying I Sodi. I wouldn't come back, but I did enjoy the food and experience. There are just other Italian restaurants and nothing blew my socks off in terms of flavor.

Awful ! Rude Matre de and server
Food great but very uncomfortable treatment. management awful

I think this place is great, but a bit overhyped. It's super pricey too. Server wasn't clear on the wine recommendations, specifically the price. Ended up paying $30 x2 per glass unbeknownst to me but that's ok.  The lasagna is worth the hype  though. Loved that. Super heavy and filling, just the way pasta should be. I'd go back just for that. Also had the pappardelle or something that was similar. Delish, yet nothing to rave about here. It's the lasagna. Yall already know. Cozy and romantic vibes inside. Perfect for date night. Prepare to shell out though.

I finally made it to I Sodi. I enjoyed my meal but I don't know if I want to go through the 'whole line up outside and wait' process again. I did, in fact, get to the restaurant at about 3:50PM yesterday, a Friday, and there were already three people in line to get in. 

Once the restaurant opened, everyone was sat quickly and the bartender started taking drink orders and going through the specials for the night. He was really friendly and made you feel like a regular even if it was the 10th or 1st time at the restaurant. I was struck by how quiet the restaurant is. There's no music playing and you can hear your neighbors from across the bar. 

The thing they don't tell you is that the bread service is $5. They offer you bread but don't tell you how much it costs or that it costs anything. It's NYC so of course I shouldn't expect anything is complimentary anymore but it still left me with a bad feeling. The bread was fine, to be honest. It was a bit gluey. It was definitely house made and still warm when you opened it up.

I had the Insalta di Asparagi [$18]. It was a beautiful salad and very light. The goat cheese made it creamy and I really liked the pine nuts. It was a very big portion. I would definitely recommend sharing. 

The Lasagna a Sugo [$29], the "lasagna", I get the hype. It's enormous. One would call it a mountain. There are 22 layers, as thin as a sheet of paper. It is extremely light for something so hefty, wizardry. The lasagna is creamy and meat-forward, there was a lot of cheese [the perfect ratio if you ask me]. It was definitely worth ordering and bringing the unfinished portion home. 

Lastly, I had the vanilla panna cotta for dessert. I was looking for something light since I was pretty full from the rest of the meal. This fit the bill, but overall, I wasn't blown away by it. It was good. I enjoyed the fruity jam that was paired with it. 

I had a glass of white wine [$18] on the recommendation of the bartender. I'm not a wine expert but it was a good glass. There's about 10 options for Negronis [not a fan], and a few standard cocktails with a twist. 

I paid $108 after tax and tip. Whether I come back is TBD.

Came right before the dinner rush and sat at the bar. Really impressed with their amaro selection and well versed bartenders. Ordered the artichoke hearts (very salty but WOW), the lamb special and the papardelle special. Go with the lamb!!!!
Put our name in at 4:30 and got a table at 7! Pasta was delicious, atmosphere was cozy, and you should definitely get dessert!

I love the dining ambience and the service was pleasant and attentive. The asparagus and mushroom was wonderful. The pasta was less al dente than what I prefer, but the taste of the lasagna was good otherwise.

Really great Italian restaurant that, in my opinion, still stands out among the sea of Italian restaurants in the West Village. I Sodi focuses on Tuscan-style dishes and there is an emphasis on simplicity. 

The restaurant was fairly quiet, not quite the loud environment as the nearby Via Carota. Service was solid and our server gave great suggestions throughout the night. 

The food, as a whole, was simple but executed really well. I don't think this is the type of place that you get necessarily wowed by the presentation, but I cannot deny that I thoroughly enjoyed my dinner here. The pasta is cooked to perfection here and of course the lasagna is good (but you should try the other pastas too, as I think they're even better). Do pay attention to the specials, both of the ones we grabbed were awesome.
Best lasagna I have ever had. Service was great as well. Definitely worth the hype. Also worth the hassle to get a res at least once in your life.

Ambiance, food, drinks, service, all great. 

Hard to snag a reservation but saw a few people come as walk ins for lunch and not have to wait too long so may try that next, because I can't wait to come back.

A new favorite!

I Sodi is such an iconic west village restaurant! It definitely lives up to the hype and is a great counterpart to its sister restaurant Via Carota down the street. Be prepared to wait ~30min or more; our group of 4 came on a Friday night with no reservations but we were able to pass the time at Talea Beer Co while waiting for our table. I would also recommend passing the wait time at Bar Pisellino which is also nearby. Our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and also recommended a great Chianti to go with our pastas. The Cacio e Pepe and Lemon Papparadelle were our favorites, and the bread basket was also amazing! We sat indoors this time, but I would love to come back and enjoy al fresco dining in the garden since the ambience looked very chill and peaceful!

Absolutely incredible meal. The best lasagna and fried artichokes we've ever had hands down. The ny strip steak was shockingly one of the best steaks we've ever had. And the chocolate cake was incredible. The fries and lemon pasta also excellent.

My friend and I stopped by I Sodi without a reservation at around 5pm, and to our surprise, they seated us at the bar immediately. The bartender was extremely attentive and patiently answered our questions and told us about the specials. The restaurant is small and cozy with a bar that's fully stocked, and there's a garden in the back. I could tell this place gets really cute as the sun sets!

I ordered the lemon pasta, and I'm so glad I did. It was fresh, creamy, peppery, and the lemon really shone through. Honestly the best lemon pasta I've ever had. The noodles were also handmade, and they were soft and perfectly cooked. 

I would definitely recommend booking a reservation, but you could also try to test your luck walking in like we did. I'm happy we tried this place and would love to go back!

Impossible to get a reservation so went at 430 when they opened , seated at a table in the back room no problem , plenty of unused seating also the whole time we were there. Bar is lovely and friendly for dining. They def didn't rush us, prob because there were open tables .  Great wine list, very knowledgeable server versed in all the offerings food and drink. Fried artichokes were very salty but fantastic. The salad with radishes, faves and mint was dynamite. The pasta, the whole reason we wanted to go, was just OK. I wanted it to be amazing. We ordered the seasonal pasta specials, but it was just so so. Pasta was a little sticky and gummy, kind of a bummer. Excellent panna cotta and espresso for dessert. Prices were not unreasonable, two of us ate for $220 with the tip (alcohol was two glasses of wine and a Negroni). Glad we went, but one and done for us.

With some luck checking Resy, I was able to snag an early dinner in the I Sodi garden. The garden space is lovely and calm. Our waiter was very attentive and helpful with recommendations. 

To start, we had the fried artichoke and insalata mista. The artichoke was delicious, and the salad was light and I really enjoyed the dressing. 

For mains, we split the lasagna and nettle pappardelle with butter sauce (one of the specials). The pappardelle was great, and the lasagna was to die for.

For dessert, we had the flourless chocolate cake. Normally this isn't one of my favorite desserts, but I really enjoyed this cake. It was somehow rich yet light at the same time. 

I will definitely be returning to I Sodi, and will be dreaming of the lasagna until my return.

Really expected more from I Sodi...was looking forward to the meal when my friend and I were able to get bar seating around 5:45 on a Thursday night and had high hopes based on reviews. The lasagna is definitely amazing and worth going for but everything else is just fine. The pappardelle was very underwhelming and lacked flavor, that we even had to order the pesto because we could not eat the lemon one. The zucchini salad was good but nothing amazing.

Ok the food was 10/10 but we had a pretty negative experience with the service. 

My friend and I were so excited to meet for dinner and had made a reservation months ago. For starters, the host who was checking us in for our reservation was simply not in a good mood and was incredibly unfriendly. It felt like he wanted to ruin our night or was annoyed at our general demeanor. 

We sat down and happened to be sitting near a celebrity of sorts, when our waiter came up to us he goes "please don't embarrass yourselves" as if we had never seen a celebrity before in New York City... like relax. He then promptly calls a bus boy over to our table telling him to "f**k off" he was very strange and was also not very friendly. 

I'm not sure I'll be going back to this restaurant. The food was good but when I'm in the mood for Italian, we'll look elsewhere.

A few notes:
