First of all, they have a limited amount of lasagna per night. We ordered a little after 8:30 on a Wednesday and the bartender told us they just ran out of the lasagna 5 minutes prior. The Paccheri Strascicati uses the same meat sauce so it was a decent alternative, but still a bit disappointing. 

The rabbit was one of the most disappointing dishes I've had in the city, WAY too salty. Drinks were good, highly recommend the Negroni al Caffe. Server was nice. Really cute spot. Would order differently next time.

Been wanting to try this place for a long time but getting a res has always been a struggle! I decided to go here solo on a Monday evening. It was definitely the move! I waited about 5 minutes for a seat to open at the bar. The bartender was informative and attentive. I got a martini and got the lasagna as my entree. It was very large and absolutely amazing! I had half and brought the rest home. Everything on the menu looked amazing. Glad I got to try!

2.5 - Ok did not regret

Food overall was fine, nothing special. Fried artichokes are overrated. They're quite salty, essentially chips. I would skip the panna cotta. Service was a bit slow it seemed like they were short on staff.

My dining experience at I Sodi was not bad at all
The portions were generous
Artichoke special was excellent
Service was quite good 
I think I'd skip the lasagna next time and try their other pasta dishes
I would definitely come back for a next time which is saying a lot 
One thing to note tho the bread wasn't complimentary.

I loved the outdoor seating here - reminded me of Europe and it was super easy walking in and we got a table for 4 in an hour on a week night. We ordered the lasagna, lemon pasta and ravioli. I loved the texture of the pasta, it was perfectly Al dente and the lemon one was definitely the best. The lasagna had too much meat and was super mushy which we didn't enjoy. The burrata was fresh and we liked the cucumber salad as well. I also really liked their gin martini, it was refreshing and strong!

Incredible pastas. Incredibly rude service.

Our server was snarky and curt, which really put a damper on what was otherwise an amazing meal. I've always wondered why I Sodi receives such negative reviews regarding their service, and now I understand why. Such a shame. Even the best pastas cannot justify such an uncomfortable experience.

Leaving a review to remind myself not to ever eat there again. Super mid, way overrated. The paccheri strascicati was super dry and needed more flavor. Even the bread was dull. Too many options in New York for this.
call me garfield the way im gobbling this lasagna and loathing the beginning of the workweek

I regularly see this place hyped as one of the best Italian spots in NYC, so when I was in town for work I put it on my list of places to go. I showed up maybe an hour after they opened on a weekday and told it would be about 45 mins. I didn't get a text until nearly an hour and 30 mins later. In general the host was not friendly and gave off pretentious vibes. 

I ordered the bread.. which I did not realize they charged for, it was not on the menu so when they asked if I wanted any, I assumed it was complimentary. Just like I didn't assume my sparkling water would be $10. I got the lasagne, of course.. and while the layers were definitely impressive to look at, taste wise I found this dish to just be ok. I could barely finish half of it.. very filling and dense. I'm glad I got to try it, but not something I'm still thinking about or would go out of my way to go again.

If I could eat at this place each night, I would!  Each time I venture to NYC, I make a point to visit this quaint spot in the Village.  Staff are professional yet inviting.  Food bar-none some of the best Italian I've ever had outside of Italy!

Was good not the greatest I've ever had. The bread and the olives were great. 
The lemon pasta could have been better.
Short ribs were great!

Finally made my way here after hearing good things all these years and the pasta did not disappoint :). The cacio e pepe was very good - it came out hot (clearly made on the spot), cheesy, and al dente. Note that the portion size is ok but on the smaller side. The environment felt cozy and intimate with a rustic yet refined decor. Think wooden tables, wooden beams, and soft lights. The atmosphere is inviting but casual - a nice blend between a charming neighborhood spot and a chic, sophisticated trattoria. Bring your dates here, it's a vibe. Came at 5pm on a Monday (lol) and no line at all. While good, it sat on the slightly pricier side. On par with the NYC restaurant scene but most of the pastas were $25+ (...and without meat lmao, sorry I am a carnivore). Hence, I likely wouldn't come all the time but I'd come with friends and dates.

I Sodi is hands down my favorite restaurant in New York. I love coming here and have never had a negative experience. The service is fantastic: attentive, kind, and knowledgeable. The intimate setting makes it a fabulous place for a date or bringing parents. And now... the food. The lasagna is 1000% worth the hype. The fried artichokes are a must (this recent time they did not have, but the burrata was great). The pomarola pasta and spinach ravioli were also musts. 

I brought my parents here this time (my husband is away and he was SO jealous when I told him) and they loved it. Thank you I Sodi! Can't wait to be back soon!

We sat out the back outdoor area and it was a really nice place to sit, calm and nice greenery. Lasagne was delicious and very filling. Tiramisu was massive, split between 2 people we still couldn't finish it. The service was a little slow but it was prime time on the weekend and the restaurant was fully packed.

Sodi...more like SodiUM. Agree with the reviews from most people here who commented that the dishes are far too salty. This was the consensus among our 7-people party who each ordered different dishes. I'm sad to give this place a mediocre review because our waiter was kind and helpful. 

Presentation of the dishes was great, and the restaurant has more seating in the back along with a patio for outdoor dining. Sadly the salt content is something they really need to fix.

Overall: This is one of the most difficult reviews I've written in a while.  

I spent a year trying to get a reservation at a reasonable time with zero luck.  Eventually, I gave up and I've spent the past couple of weeks putting my name in early to try to get a spot.  The wait time is regularly quoted at 3+ hours on Friday/Saturday.  They start taking walk ins at 4:30pm, and there is usually already a line.  This time we ended up committing and waiting a full 3.5 hours for a table.  Brutal.

Once we got seated, everything was fantastic.  Food was incredible, service was helpful and improved the experience, and prices were relatively reasonable (all things considered).  

I decided to rate this place based on my experience at dinner and not based on the wait.  If you live in the West Village or if you're willing to make a full evening of popping between bars or app spots then this spot is amazing.  But it takes a good bit of planning and effort to get a spot on a weekend.

Food: 5
Drinks: 4
Service: 5
Value: 4
Atmosphere: 5 


Food: All of the food was amazing.  We ordered the Antipasto Toscano(charcuterie platter) and Insalata di Pomodori (heirloom tomatoes) as appetizers and the Paccheri Strascicati (pasta with meat sauce) and rough cut noodles (daily special - hand cut noodles with braised lamb) as our pasta dishes.  The pasta in particular was extra special.  It was cooked perfectly and the proteins mixed in had layers of flavor that complemented each other well.  

Drinks: We ordered a bottle of wine to go with our dinner.  The wine list was predominantly Italian wines.  The Chianti we ordered was tasty, but they did have a slightly limited selection that didn't offer many choices outside of Italian wines and didn't have a ton of options at the lower end of the price scale.

Service:  Our waiter was serving as both a server and the host.  He was extremely friendly, gave lots of good advice on the menu, and even gave some tips on times to come back that might be easier to get a table.  He definitely added to our experience and was more than just someone to take our order.

Value:  Most everything was reasonable here, but slightly on the more expensive side.  It was all very high quality so it was hard to complain, but some of it was kind of expensive.  In particular, the beverages tended to skew towards the pricey side.

Atmosphere: I Sodi has nailed the restaurant vibes in the West Village.  They don't do outdoor dining on the street like other places do, which I think helps the ambiance.  The windows are blurred out which helps keep the chaos out.  Tables are close together but it doesn't feel too cramped.  Its an ideal date spot thats been perfectly executed.

came on a tuesday night with a party of 6 after shockingly getting off the resy waitlist. this is a known hard to get reservation so i am very happy we were able to snag it. my friends and i were celebrating a friends engagement over dinner! 

service was great our server was really chill and on top of it. 

we ordered to start the artichoke and tomatoes with goat cheese. the artichokes i was a little unimpressed especially since yelp really rates it high. most reviews said it was a little too salty and i agree. the tomatoes and goat cheese were quite excellent however - great dish to balance out some saltiness. 

for mains split a bunch with friends: the clam pasta and lamb pasta were my absolute favorites. shocking dont see the hype with the lemon pasta but most of the table enjoyed the dish so maybe its just me. but lemme tell you: the clam and lamb pasta was to DIE for these were literally so good and the portions were big, i have leftovers! 

for dessert im not a tiramusi girl but everyone said this was made extra well done and more on the expensive side - def a table favorite. lemme tell you the panna cotta was absolutely excellent we were all literally licking the plate clean (as you can see from the picture). would come back for the clam pasta and panna cotta 100%

def recommend and would return!!!

The meanest host I have ever experienced. Didn't honor my reservation because I was 10 minutes late (despite having a 15 min grace period), belittled me and was ruthless and unapologetic. 
The food might be good but being arrogant and mean is not acceptable.

I don't get the hype around this place. The pasta is pretty mediocre.

We started with the Rucola e Castelmagno salad, which is essentially arugula with blocks of cheese. The arugula was fresh with a nice balsamic vinaigrette, but I wish they had shaved the cheese instead of just tossing big chunks on top.

Naturally, we tried some of the "popular" dishes, like the fried artichoke. It felt like eating fried leaves--crunchy and overly salty. We also ordered the lasagna a sugo, and it was incredibly dry, probably one of the worst lasagnas I've ever had. It became stale very quickly. Lastly, the Cacio e Pepe was just basic and overly salty. Nothing stood out.

There are definitely better Italian restaurants in the area. I'd recommend skipping this one.

I Sodi is hands down the best Italian restaurant I've ever had even compared to Via Carota. Everything was delicious and the service was excellent. We got to sit outside and as tourists the ambiance felt incredible.

I am unsure about the hype surrounding this restaurant, as my experience with the dishes was disappointing. The artichokes resembled fried leaves (esp like fried maple leaves) and lacked flavor, while the lasagna was dry, and the cacio e pepe was excessively salty. Overall, the flavor profiles of the dishes did not meet my expectations.

Luckily we got a bar seats within 1 hour, the front dinning room is a little bit noise. 

The food was really great, the pasta definitely is above average. We love the Parpadelle Limone and Faro salad, the salad is the prefect start for heavy pasta. 

Meat lasagna is a little too salty for us, ravioli is cream but not flavorful at all. However, the pasta itself is great! Also, servers are really friendly and passionate to explain the menu in the busy environment:)

Cozy vibes and great warm service. Came here before the renovation and the restaurant used to be really small. Now it's much larger. 

Reservations - super hard to get, I walked in and waited

Food - can't go wrong with anything. the lasagna is a must get as everyone says. Negroni is also great
An absolutely lovely dinner. The cocktails are to die for and the fried artichoke is life changing!

I have been trying to secure a reservation here for so long, and was so excited to finally get a chance to go. We ordered the fried artichokes, pappardelle al limone, tagliatelle con cipolla, lasagna a sugo, galleto al mattone, and coniglio in porchetta. Overall the food was okay but not as good as I expected, considering the type around it and the difficulty in getting a reservation. My favorite dishes were the pappardelle al limone and the galletto al mattone. The fried artichokes and coniglio in porchetta were honestly not great. The ambience was very nice though, with a larger indoor space and outdoor garden than I expected! Overall, I'm glad I got to try it but would probably not try too hard to go back soon.

Another amazing visit to one of our all time favorites. Again the lasagna and cake are two of the best dishes anywhere, and the antipasto is incredible as well. This time we got the limone and maltagliata as well, which were great but we'd probably sub both next time. (Also, three pastas plus the antipasto is way too much food for two people.)
waited on line for a reservation. gave me a time slot so we went to an excellent nearby bar called xou. the service was exceptional. all the food was phenomenal

Really really good Italian food and great service. The menu is pretty extensive and they have a lot of options even if you're vegetarian. Reservations are hard to get and there usually is a wait if you want to walk in. 
For apps we for the fried zucchini and mushroom and it was really good. 
For mains I got the cacio e Pepe and that was absolutely delicious. The portion may seem slightly small but it's extremely heavy and you can share it with someone too.

I've been here twice now and was pretty shocked at how many complaints I now see in the comments. I absolutely loved it both times. I've just now read lots of complaints about the lasagna and the the pappardelle, but I would highly recommend both. The only reason I can think of why these dishes are getting beat up in the reviews is that people are coming in expecting your typical American pasta drowning in sauce and garlic. If that's what you're looking for, definitely do not come here.

Are you kidding me 3.
7. This is a 4 or better. Sat at the bar the bartender male was terrific well informed of both the menu and the specialty drinks. The food was excellent. Wife did indeed like the lasagna and i had the Paccheri Strascicati. The ratings and complaints are head scratchers. This place is very good. Very small and better get reservations. But for me this is better than 3.7

Managed to walk in on a Sunday around 12:15pm and got lucky to get a spot at the bar. The bartender was very friendly and helpful with the menu. 

We split the fried artichoke and ravioli with spinach, ricotta, butter, and sage. The ravioli was delicious. The lemon pasta was light and melt in your mouth. The meat lasagna was also a winner as it was so easy to cut into -- truly didn't even need a knife. 

Def recommend a weekday lunch if you're struggling to get in. Super quaint vibes -- almost feel like you're in a country house. Hope to go back again!

Very delicious food in classic environments. We sat at the bar as we did not have a reservation, and our bartender and server was very sweet. I enjoyed that there were multiple specials for the day, which we did get one of, along with two other pastas to share. My favorite was the special, which was lamb and mushroom pasta, and then I enjoyed the lemon pasta as well. I really enjoyed the ravioli, but wish they were in a true butter sage sauce, instead of the creamy cheesy sauce it seemed to have. 

I think the prices are a bit steep for the food, but I'm also not local to NYC, and understand prices there are just more expensive in general! 

We wanted some good pasta, and that's what we got. Thanks!
Incredible food! What else is there to say? Very well worth walking in or trying to score a reservation!

The place is cute and the food is good but the service - actually the check in person is pretentious for no goood reasons. We get it that this is a hot ticket but does the guy checking people in have to be such a stick up his butt tool? Lame and makes us not want to dine there... it's pasta for gods sake . Child . It's pasta :/ take the stick out of your arse and be nice to people who desire to dine here.. there has to be another way :/
The Lasagna was fantastic!! 22 layers of Italian goodness. I got lucky and got a seat at the bar with a friend. The service was very good and the food was excellent.

I see why this is such a sought-after Italian restaurant in the city. Not to brag, we even managed to walk-in and land on a table.

After scouring the city for Cacio e Pepe, this is the best one I've found yet. The spaghetti pasta choice is actually such a great choice, it was cooked perfect al-dente and has an amazing chew. The cheese sauce is so rich and delicious. The standout however was the black pepper. It had such a nice kick and lasting effect, providing a perfect complement to the cheese sauce.

The braised short ribs were so tender with a bit of fattiness and melted in my mouth, and the sauce was so rich and a bit sweet too. I was not a fan of the peas that came along with it, it seemed too normal.

The lasagna was so interesting. It wasn't like any other lasagna I've ever had. What mille crepe / thousand layer cake is to normal layer cake is what this lasagna feels to normal lasagna. There are so many layers of rich meat and pasta goodness. I've never had texture of meat like this before, the creamy meat sauce is so savory full of flavor. I do wish maybe there was a bit more cheese however, both in the layers and baked on top, for even more flavor and texture.

The lamb and mushroom pasta special was also amazing, so rich and with amazing flavor. The burrata and bread service are skippable, we were hoping for a lot more burrata and bread for the price.

The tiramisu was amazing and a great way to end the meal. The marscspone layer was light, not too sweet, but so creamy. All the layers were done perfectly.

This ended up being one of my favorite Italian spots in the city, and my go-to if I want good cacio e pepe.

One star is too many for this establishment. THE most rudest people ever to work in a restaurant. Waited over 2 hours (patiently) for a table when we were told 1 hour and 15 minutes. When we were finally seated the host said "right on schedule" and I said not really. He told us to leave the restaurant. We proceeded to sit at our seats at the bar and the bartender said "I'm not serving you". I have NEVER been treated this way EVER and even worse for NO REASON. Everyone in the restaurant couldn't believe what was happening. I don't care how good the food is I would never go back and tell everyone to do the same. My hard earned money can be used at restaurants that welcome me as a customer. Disgusting behavior.

I am not a pasta person. I do not often get pasta, I almost never order it at a restaurant, and I never cook it at home. I sodi was the best pasta I've ever had. It made me love pasta. Each dish was so well crafted and so flavorful. The lasagna has gone viral, but I'd say that the other pasta dishes are honestly even better. It is so good. It is so hard to get into and for good reason. The place is tiny, but the food is so good. If you can get in here, it is worth every dollar.

quite possibly the best lasagna i've ever had. i think it has something like 14 layers?! 

a group of 3 of us went here for dinner in mid november. the ambiance was lovely and they have such a sweet little back patio (although it was too cold out that night to sit outside). we split the following: burrata and prosciutto, an artichoke salad, lasagna, & pappardelle. everything was delicious. their cocktail menu is full of negronis but i opted for the sage martini which was so refreshing. we were too full for dessert but will definitely be back to try it. overall a great experience.

My roommate and I have been dying to go here for a very long time and decided that today was the day. We walked over at 4:30 when it opened and it was already busy inside. We put our names down and were texted that our seats were available an hour and a half later so we ate at 6. 

Luckily, a table became available instead of bar seats and we ended up sitting by the window with a beautiful view of the outside patio. The restaurant was beautiful and the service was good too. 

We started with the complimentary bread and olives. The bread was amazing and warm (unfortunately not pictured as we ate it quickly haha). We could tell that it was freshly baked. We started with the prosciutto and burrata and the fried artichokes. The prosciutto and burrata were very fresh and tasty. The artichokes had great flavor but I think an aioli on the side would have benefitted them. 

For our main course we split the lasagna and lemon pasta. Both were amazing but I preferred the lemon pasta. The pasta was somehow perfectly rich yet light and not heavy. The sauce consistency was just right and spiced perfectly. The lasagna had a rich and thick ragu style sauce that had a very deep flavor. I will say the lasagna feels a bit heavy but I would reccomend for first time goers. 

All around a 10/10 experience and would visit again in a heartbeat.

We lucked out and got a seat at the bar on a rainy Sunday. The staff was very nice and helpful with our questions. We started with a cappuccino and an americano and both were delicious!

The only miss for us was the artichoke salad. It was oil-heavy and a bit bland, tho the  artichokes and parm were so fresh. Both the spinach ravioli and carmelzied onion pasta were great. Heavier dishes, but the flavors were on point.

Portions look smaller, but you'll fill up. I look forward to coming back and trying more dishes!

For Doordash order--
Idk if I got them on a bad night or something, but my lasagna tasted more like a glutinous meat cake than sheets of pasta with meat. The sugo part was good, but the noodles were way overcooked. So odd.

A lovely meal ruined completely by a nasty and deliberately rude server. 
Rita's food will never not impress. She's that good. But our server was so unapologetically rude for no reason we  could figure out, we would never go back. I'm so completely disappointed. Why would Rita have him run the front of the house?  From what I hear, l'm not the only person who feels this way.
